entries: Strike damage increases by {@damage 1d12} at levels 5, 11, and 17. The hand's weight capacity becomes 100 pounds at level 5, 300 pounds at level 11, and 1,000 pounds at level 17.

spell.name: Voidstride
entries: You step into the smallest possible absence between one position and the next.
There is no flash or tunnel, only a brief impression that your outline skipped a piece of distance.
Space closes before anything can follow the route you used.
With experience, the missing step grows longer while remaining just as effortless.

entries.name: Short Teleport
entries: Teleport up to 10 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The teleport distance becomes 15 feet at level 5, 20 feet at level 11, and 30 feet at level 17.

spell.name: Death Recall
entries: Death ends a creature's future, but for a moment its body still remembers what it was capable of doing.
You call that final physical record forward without restoring life or creating undeath.
The corpse rises only long enough to spend one impossible turn using fragments of the abilities it possessed before death.
Then the borrowed continuity collapses and the body returns to exactly what it is: a corpse.

entries.name: Stolen Turn
entries: Choose one corpse you can see within range. Immediately after your turn ends, the corpse takes one Stolen Turn under your control, using the statistics and capabilities it possessed immediately before it died, subject to the limits below. The corpse isn't revived and doesn't become Undead.

entries.name: Level 1: Last Motion
entries: The corpse can move up to half its Speed, take the Attack action to make one ordinary attack it possessed in life, and perform one simple object interaction. It can use inherent riders that are inseparable from that ordinary attack. It can't use a Bonus Action, Reaction, spell, Multiattack, Recharge action, Legendary Action, or other special action.

entries.name: Level 5: Lesser Reconstruction
entries: The corpse can use its full Speed and movement modes, Multiattack or another ordinary combat Action it possessed, Bonus Actions, and one Reaction during the Stolen Turn. The spell temporarily repairs major bodily damage and can restore one missing limb or equivalent structure for the duration of the Stolen Turn.

entries.name: Level 11: Greater Reconstruction
entries: The corpse can use special actions, Recharge abilities, breath weapons, supernatural movement, teleportation, and transformations it possessed in life. It can cast its cantrips and spells up to a spell level equal to half the highest spell level it could cast in life, rounded up, using its original spellcasting ability, spell attack modifier, and spell save DC. A spell slot required for a spell cast during the Stolen Turn is treated as available for that casting. The spell reconstructs anatomy necessary for those abilities.

entries.name: Level 17: Perfect Reconstruction
entries: The corpse can use its full capabilities from immediately before death, including Actions, Bonus Actions, one Reaction, spells, innate spells, limited-use abilities, and Legendary Actions when their normal timing permits. Temporary resources supplied by this spell exist only for the Stolen Turn.

entries.name: Concentration and Return to Death
entries: If the corpse casts or activates something that requires Concentration, the corpse maintains that Concentration using its original Constitution saving throw modifier. That Concentration ends when Death Recall ends.
At the end of the Stolen Turn, every temporary reconstruction and resource created by this spell disappears and the corpse returns to death.

spell.name: Glacier Fang
entries: Frost gathers along a weapon in a narrow ridge shaped like a translucent fang.
The cold bites after the weapon does, stealing a little momentum from anything struck.
Away from combat, the same controlled chill can smother a small flame or lock exposed water into ice.
The enchantment clings briefly even if the weapon leaves your hand.

entries.name: Frozen Weapon
entries: Touch one weapon. For the duration, attacks made with it deal an extra {@damage 1d4} Cold damage.
Once on each turn when the weapon deals this extra damage to a creature, that creature's Speed is reduced by 5 feet until the start of the attacker's next turn.
As a Bonus Action while holding the affected weapon, you can extinguish one ordinary flame no larger than a torch within 5 feet of the weapon or freeze a small amount of exposed water it touches.
If you stop holding the weapon, the spell remains on it until the end of your next turn before ending.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The extra damage becomes {@damage 2d4} at level 5, {@damage 3d4} at level 11, and {@damage 4d4} at level 17. The Speed reduction becomes 10 feet at level 11 and 15 feet at level 17.

spell.name: Fatehook

time.condition: which you take when a creature you can see within 30 feet makes an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw

entries: You catch a tiny loose thread in the probability surrounding a creature's attempt.
A favorable tug can turn an almost into an enough; a hostile tug can make certainty slip.
The spell doesn't show you the future or guarantee an outcome.
It simply hooks one possibility and gives it a little more or less weight.

entries.name: Boon or Bane
entries: Roll {@dice 1d4}. Choose Boon or Bane. With Boon, add the number rolled to the triggering roll. With Bane, subtract it.
If you choose Bane against an unwilling creature, that creature can make a Wisdom saving throw. On a success, Fatehook has no effect on its roll.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The die becomes {@dice 1d6} at level 5, {@dice 1d8} at level 11, and {@dice 1d10} at level 17.

spell.name: Ghostwalk
entries: The target's body becomes slightly less committed to being solid.
Edges blur, carried objects lose their weight against walls, and matter can overlap matter without becoming fully ethereal.
Passing through solid structures remains slow and deliberate because the body must continuously negotiate with the material around it.
The spell always remembers where the nearest safe open space was, preventing a careless passage from becoming a tomb.

entries.name: Partial Spectral Form
entries: Choose one willing creature you can see within range. For the duration, the target and everything it is wearing or carrying can move through creatures and solid objects. Moving through such matter costs 1 extra foot of movement for each foot traveled.
The target can't move through more than 15 continuous feet of solid matter during a single passage.

entries.name: Ethereal Reach
entries: The target can reach a hand or held object through a solid barrier as part of an interaction, provided the depth of solid matter doesn't exceed the spell's current passage limit.

entries.name: Living Passage
entries: Moving through another creature doesn't damage or displace either creature, and the spaces occupied by creatures are treated as Difficult Terrain for the target.

entries.name: Distort Through Openings
entries: The target can squeeze through openings substantially smaller than its body if its carried equipment can pass with it in spectral form.

entries.name: Look Beyond
entries: By placing part of its face through a barrier within the passage limit, the target can see and hear from the opposite side.

entries.name: Safe Return
entries: If the spell would end while the target is inside a solid object or creature, the target is immediately moved by the shortest route to the nearest unoccupied space it can occupy.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The maximum continuous depth of solid matter becomes 30 feet at level 5, 60 feet at level 11, and 120 feet at level 17.

spell.name: Rewind

components.m: a small hourglass filled with silver sand

entries: With a single command, you force one creature backward through the moments it has just lived.
Wounds close in reverse, spent strength returns, expended magic gathers back into the body, and the creature is dragged back to where it stood only moments before.
Even death can be undone if it occurred within the brief span your magic can reach.
Yet the world around the creature remains unchanged. Every attack it made, every spell it cast, and every consequence it caused remains behind—the creature alone is rewound.

entries.name: Rewind
entries: Choose one creature you can see within range, or the corpse of a creature that died within the period this spell can rewind.
Choose either the start of the target's previous turn or the start of the turn before its previous turn. The target is returned to exactly the state it possessed at the chosen point.

This includes the target's location, Hit Points, Temporary Hit Points, conditions, spell slots, expended Hit Dice, expended class features, species features, and other limited-use abilities, Actions, Bonus Actions, Reactions, movement, magic item charges it expended, ammunition and other expendable resources it used, Material components it consumed, Concentration, physical form, missing or destroyed body parts, and equipment and carried objects it possessed at that moment.
If the target's former space is occupied or otherwise impossible for it to occupy, it appears in the nearest unoccupied space it can safely occupy.

entries.name: The World Remains Changed
entries: Only the target is rewound. Nothing the target did after the chosen point is undone.

Damage it dealt remains. Creatures it killed remain dead. Healing it provided remains. Conditions it inflicted or removed remain changed. Objects it damaged, destroyed, created, or moved remain as they are. Spells it cast remain in effect for their normal remaining durations. Creatures it summoned remain. Information it revealed remains known. Creatures it moved or teleported remain in their new locations.

Resources restored to the target return even though the effects created by spending those resources remain. For example, an expended spell slot, magic item charge, consumed Material component, or limited-use feature can return without undoing the spell or effect it produced.

entries.name: Death Rewound
entries: If the target died after the chosen point and was alive at that point, it returns to life as part of the rewind. The target doesn't need to be willing.
If the target was dead at the chosen point, the spell restores it to that dead state instead.

spell.name: Sovereign Edict
entries: Your presence becomes the center of an unquestionable decree.
With a word, you impose a single law upon the space surrounding you, and the world itself refuses to permit its violation.
The decree moves wherever you move, surrounding allies and enemies alike—yet you decide whose actions are bound by your authority.
Within your dominion, resistance is possible. Defiance is not always.

entries.name: Sovereign Aura
entries: A 30-foot Emanation surrounds you for the duration and moves with you.
When you cast the spell, choose one Edict from the options below.

Whenever a creature other than you enters the Emanation for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, you can choose whether that creature is subject to the Edict. You make this choice separately for each creature.
You are never restricted by your own Edict. A creature ceases to be subject to the Edict when it leaves the Emanation.

entries.name: Defy the Edict
entries: Whenever a subject creature would violate the chosen Edict, it makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a successful save, it can perform that action or receive that effect normally. On a failed save, the prohibited action or effect fails, and any Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, spell slot, charge, or other resource it would have spent isn't expended.
A creature makes this saving throw each time it would violate the Edict.

entries.name: No Passage
entries: A subject creature can't willingly leave the Emanation. Teleportation, planar travel, or any other effect it willingly uses to move itself outside the Emanation is also prohibited.
If you move far enough that a subject creature would fall outside the Emanation, the creature isn't dragged with you; the Edict doesn't prevent you from moving away from it.

entries.name: No Violence
entries: A subject creature can't willingly deal damage to another creature. This includes weapon attacks, spells, features, and other effects whose direct result would deal damage to another creature.
It can still attack objects, move, defend itself, heal, or use effects that don't deal damage to another creature.

entries.name: No Restoration
entries: A subject creature can't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points.
It can still cast or use an effect that restores Hit Points to another creature, provided the subject creature doesn't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points from that effect.

entries.name: No Transformation
entries: A subject creature can't willingly change its form, size, or physical shape through a spell, feature, or magical effect.
A transformation already active when the creature becomes subject to the Edict isn't ended.

entries.name: No Spellcasting
entries: A subject creature can't cast spells of 6th level or lower. Spells of 7th level or higher can be cast normally.

spell.name: Severance

components.m: a length of silver thread cut cleanly in two

entries: Every bond leaves a thread behind—between spell and victim, master and servant, memory and identity, bearer and artifact.
You perceive those invisible connections and draw an unseen edge across them.
Magic collapses, curses lose their claim, memories rewrite themselves around what has vanished, and bonds once thought permanent simply cease to exist.
Nothing is truly beyond the blade. Some connections merely require a sharper spell.

Choose one creature you can see within range. An unwilling target must make a Charisma saving throw. A willing creature can choose to fail the saving throw. On a failed save, choose up to three connections involving the target from the options below and sever them immediately. If an option has multiple valid instances, each instance counts as a separate connection unless that option states otherwise.

entries.name: Concentration
entries: Choose one spell or effect on which the target is concentrating. The target's Concentration on that effect immediately ends.

entries.name: Summoning
entries: Choose one creature magically summoned, conjured, or called by the target. The magical connection sustaining that creature is severed, and the chosen creature immediately disappears.
It returns to whatever state or place is appropriate for the effect that brought it forth, if applicable. If no such state or place exists, it simply ceases to be present.

This happens even if the summoning effect would normally allow the creature to remain after losing contact with its summoner. The spell or feature that produced the creature doesn't necessarily end for any other summoned creatures it created unless you separately sever those connections.

entries.name: Control
entries: Choose one magical connection through which the target controls another creature or another creature controls the target. This can include a Charm, possession, domination, supernatural command, compelled behavior, magical obedience, or a similar effect that directly controls another creature.

That connection ends immediately. If the effect affects multiple creatures, only the chosen connection involving the target is severed unless ending that connection necessarily ends the entire effect.

entries.name: Telepathic Link
entries: Choose one magical telepathic, sensory, emotional, or communication connection involving the target. That connection immediately ends.
Neither side can continue communicating, perceiving, sharing senses, or exchanging information through that connection.

entries.name: Shared Effect
entries: Choose one ongoing magical effect that directly links the target to another creature. This can include an effect that shares damage, transfers Hit Points, redirects harm, exchanges senses, shares conditions or resources, causes one creature to suffer or benefit when the other does, or otherwise magically connects the states of two creatures.
That connection ends.

entries.name: Planar Bond
entries: Choose one magical connection binding the target to a particular plane, location, creature, or object. The chosen connection is severed.
This doesn't transport the target, destroy either end of the connection, or reverse anything that already happened because of that bond.

entries.name: Remote Effect
entries: Choose one ongoing spell or magical effect that the target can command, direct, manipulate, or control from a distance. The target permanently loses its connection to that effect.
If the effect can continue independently, it remains but can no longer be controlled by the target. If the effect can't exist without that connection, it ends.

entries.name: Spell or Curse
entries: Choose one ongoing spell, curse, or magical effect affecting the target. You sever that effect from the target.
If the effect also affects other creatures, objects, or areas, it ends only for the target unless the effect can't continue without the target's connection to it.

This option can sever curses, magical diseases or afflictions, magical transformations, magical restraints, seals, wards attached to the target, magical buffs or debuffs, ongoing spell effects, effects with a duration of Until Dispelled, and permanent magical effects.
The casting of Severance must be sufficiently powerful to cut the chosen effect, as described under Severance Power.

entries.name: Attunement
entries: Choose one magic item to which the target is attuned. The target's Attunement to that item immediately ends.

The item itself isn't damaged, destroyed, or otherwise altered. This connection can be severed even if the item's curse or properties normally prevent its bearer from willingly ending Attunement, provided the casting of Severance is sufficiently powerful.

Ending Attunement doesn't automatically end unrelated effects that the item already created unless you separately sever those effects. Attunement to an Artifact requires a sufficiently powerful casting of this spell.

entries.name: Memory
entries: Choose one memory or one connected group of memories possessed by the target concerning a clearly defined creature, place, event, period of time, relationship, agreement, experience, or subject. The chosen memories are permanently severed from the target.

The target doesn't merely experience an empty gap. Instead, Severance creates plausible false memories to replace whatever was removed. The surrounding memories are altered only as much as necessary to make the target's remembered past feel natural, continuous, and internally consistent.

The target might remember being alone when another creature was actually present, meeting someone else instead, reaching a destination by another route, learning information from another plausible source, making a choice for a different reason, surviving an event without remembering who actually helped, or an uneventful period of time in place of something significant.
Severance favors the smallest plausible reconstruction necessary to conceal the removed memories. These false memories don't alter reality.

Physical evidence, written records, magical records, possessions, injuries, portraits, and the memories of unaffected creatures remain unchanged. If the target later encounters evidence contradicting its reconstructed memories, it can realize that something is inconsistent, but doing so doesn't automatically restore the severed memories.
The target can learn the forgotten information again and form new memories normally. Magically protected or otherwise exceptionally resistant memories may require a higher-level casting of Severance.

entries.name: Identity
entries: You sever the target's identity from the memories of every other creature that currently remembers the target as an individual. This counts as one connection, regardless of how many creatures are affected.

Every affected creature permanently forgets the target's identity and all personal memories specifically connecting that identity to its experiences. This can include the target's name, aliases, face, voice, mannerisms, personality, relationships, conversations, shared experiences, friendships, rivalries, promises, conflicts, affection, hatred, and role in remembered events.
The target retains its own memories.

entries.name: Reconstructed Identity
entries: The memories removed through Identity don't leave obvious gaps. Instead, Severance creates individualized false memories for every affected creature, reconstructing their past in whatever plausible way requires the fewest changes.

Different creatures don't necessarily receive the same replacement history. One creature might remember escaping danger alone, another might remember being rescued by an unidentified stranger, someone taught by the target might remember learning from books or another teacher, and a former companion might remember traveling with the same group but never remember the target being among them.
Someone who loved the target might remember that period of life differently, with the relationship removed or plausibly attributed elsewhere.
The spell doesn't create knowledge a creature couldn't plausibly have possessed. It reconstructs recollection using information and possibilities consistent with that creature's experiences.

entries.name: Evidence Remains
entries: Identity doesn't alter reality or physical evidence. Written records, portraits, signatures, letters, possessions, monuments, magical records, historical documents, and other evidence of the target's actions remain unchanged.

An affected creature can rediscover the target's existence through surviving evidence. If it encounters the target again, it doesn't recognize the target through the severed memories but can meet them anew, learn about them, and form entirely new memories normally.

entries.name: Seamless Reconstruction
entries: False memories created by Memory or Identity aren't ongoing illusions and don't require Severance to remain active. Once created, they become part of the affected creature's memories.

They don't disappear in an Antimagic Field, don't end if Severance is later dispelled, and aren't automatically revealed by Detect Magic. They can conflict with surviving physical evidence and can later be altered, removed, or replaced by sufficiently powerful memory-affecting magic.

entries.name: Violent Severance
entries: After successfully severing the chosen connections, you can make the Severance clean or violent. A clean Severance deals no damage.

If you choose a violent Severance, the target takes {@damage 4d10} Force or Psychic damage, your choice, for each connection successfully severed. The damage is dealt after all chosen connections are severed.
Only the primary target of Severance takes this damage. Creatures whose memories are altered by Identity aren't damaged.

entries.name: Cut Either Side
entries: Severance doesn't care who created the chosen connection. You can use it to free an ally from an enemy's curse, break possession, end unwanted Attunement, remove an enemy's control over a summon, cut another creature's Concentration, sever a bond maintained by a third party, remove beneficial magic from an enemy, or remove harmful magic from an ally.
The spell affects the connection itself, not its ownership.

entries.name: Severance Power
entries: Not every connection can be severed by every casting of this spell. The level of the spell slot used to cast Severance determines how powerful a connection it can cut.
For an effect created by a spell, the slot used to cast Severance must be at least as high as the level of that spell.
For magical effects that have no spell level, the DM determines the minimum level of Severance necessary based on the effect's power and source.

Ordinary curses, magic item effects, supernatural bonds, memories, Attunement, and similar connections can normally be severed by the spell's base 7th-level casting unless something specifically makes them more powerful.

items: {@b 8th Level.} You can sever up to four connections. You can sever spells and effects of 8th level or lower, as well as connections that normally resist ordinary methods of removal. This includes exceptionally powerful curses, effects that specifically prevent themselves from being removed, magically protected memories, Attunement that can't normally be willingly ended, connections created or sustained by an Artifact, curses or magical effects created by an Artifact, and Attunement to an Artifact. Severance doesn't destroy, damage, suppress, or remove the inherent properties of an Artifact; it cuts only the specific connection or effect you choose. If you use Violent Severance after severing four connections, the maximum damage is {@damage 16d10}.

{@b 9th Level.} You can sever up to five connections. You can sever spells and effects of 9th level or lower and eligible connections regardless of protections that would normally prevent their removal. This includes permanent magical effects, Artifact connections, Artifact Attunement, divine curses, divine blessings, divine possession or control, magical bonds directly created by a deity, effects directly sustained by a deity, memories protected by magic of comparable power, and other connections originating from similarly transcendent supernatural sources. Severing a divine connection doesn't harm, weaken, banish, control, or otherwise affect the deity itself; only the chosen connection involving the target is severed. If you use Violent Severance after severing five connections, the maximum damage is {@damage 20d10}.

spell.name: Final Sanctuary
entries: You draw a boundary around a creature and declare that nothing beyond it may claim them.
Blades stop short. Curses lose their path. Hostile magic frays against an unseen edge, unable to complete the final step toward its target.
The protected creature is not hidden, unreachable, or removed from the world.
It is simply denied to hostile intent.

Choose one willing creature you can see within range. For the duration, hostile creatures can't directly affect the target unless they first succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. A creature makes this save each time it attempts to directly affect the protected target. On a failed save, the attempted effect fails against that target.

entries.name: Protected Against
entries: Final Sanctuary can prevent weapon attacks, spell attacks, damaging spells, harmful conditions, curses, forced movement, grapples and restraints, possession, Charm or domination, teleportation imposed by another creature, and any other hostile effect that directly targets or specifically includes the protected creature.
If an effect targets multiple creatures, it can still affect all other targets normally.

entries.name: Area Effects
entries: If a creature attempts to create an area of effect that would include the protected target, that creature must first make a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC.

On a failed save, the creature can't place, aim, shape, or direct the effect in a way that would include the protected target. If possible, it must choose a different point, direction, area, or arrangement that excludes the protected target.

If the effect can't be used without including the protected target, the attempted use fails, and any Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, spell slot, charge, or other resource that would have been spent isn't expended.
On a successful save, the effect can include the protected target normally.

entries.name: Indirect Harm
entries: Final Sanctuary doesn't erase consequences already present in the environment. It doesn't prevent a collapsing building from falling, ordinary fire already burning, falling due to destroyed terrain, or being struck by an object that is no longer being magically or deliberately directed at the protected target.
However, if another creature deliberately creates or directs such a hazard specifically to harm the protected target, that creature must make the saving throw before doing so.

entries.name: The Target Can Still Act
entries: The protected creature can attack, cast spells, move, and otherwise act normally. Doing so doesn't end Final Sanctuary.

entries.name: Absolute Refuge
entries: If a creature succeeds on its saving throw against Final Sanctuary, it can affect the protected creature with that one effect only. It must save again for any later hostile action or effect.

spell.name: Grand Design

m.text: a sculpted figure depicting the intended transformation, worth at least 1,000 GP, which the spell consumes

entries: You don't borrow another shape for a moment.
You convince flesh, bone, blood, and living structure that another form is equally natural.
When the working is complete, there is no spell left clinging to the body and no transformation waiting to expire.
What you create becomes flesh. What you change becomes real.

Choose one willing creature you touch. You can choose yourself. Over the course of the casting, you permanently reshape the target's body. The target remains the same creature. Its creature type, personality, memories, class features, ability scores, and other game statistics remain unchanged except where an adaptation granted by this spell specifically changes them.
At 7th level, you can make any number of cosmetic alterations and choose two Major Adaptations.

entries.name: Cosmetic Alterations
entries: You can permanently alter any ordinary physical characteristic that doesn't itself provide a mechanical benefit, including height and weight, facial structure, body proportions, skin, fur, scales, feathers, hair, eye appearance, voice, sex characteristics, horns, fins, decorative tails, apparent age, and other comparable aspects of physical appearance.
Changing apparent age doesn't alter the target's actual age, lifespan, development, or the effects of aging.

entries.name: Repeated Transformation
entries: A creature can be affected by Grand Design any number of times, including the caster. Each casting is permanent and cumulative with previous castings.
Adaptations gained from a new casting don't replace adaptations gained from an earlier casting unless the caster specifically chooses to remove, replace, reshape, or upgrade one of them.
A creature can therefore accumulate additional adaptations through repeated castings of this spell over time.
The same adaptation doesn't normally stack with itself unless that adaptation specifically says it can be chosen more than once.
A later casting using an 8th- or 9th-level spell slot can add Greater or Perfect Adaptations to a creature that was previously altered by a lower-level casting.

entries.name: Major Adaptations
entries: The following adaptations are available when Grand Design is cast using a 7th-level spell slot or higher.

entries.name: Wings
entries: The target permanently grows functional wings and gains a Fly Speed equal to its Speed.

entries.name: Aquatic Adaptation
entries: The target gains a Swim Speed equal to its Speed and can breathe air and water. It also suffers no harmful effects from ordinary underwater pressure.

entries.name: Burrowing Adaptation
entries: The target gains a Burrow Speed equal to half its Speed through earth, sand, clay, and similar natural material. It can't burrow through solid stone or worked structures.

entries.name: Climbing Adaptation
entries: The target gains a Climb Speed equal to its Speed and can move across walls and ceilings without needing to use its hands.

entries.name: Natural Armor
entries: The target develops scales, plates, dense hide, crystalline tissue, barklike growth, or similar protection. While the target isn't wearing armor, its base AC is 13 + its Dexterity modifier.

entries.name: Natural Weapon
entries: The target develops one natural weapon, such as claws, fangs, horns, spines, a tail, or a reinforced limb. It is a Simple Melee weapon with which the target is proficient.
It deals {@damage 1d8} Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, chosen when the adaptation is created. The target can use Strength or Dexterity for its attack and damage rolls with the weapon.

entries.name: Enhanced Senses
entries: The target gains Darkvision 120 feet. If it already has Darkvision, its existing range instead increases by 60 feet.

entries.name: Elemental Resilience
entries: Choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison. The target permanently gains Resistance to the chosen damage type.
This adaptation can be chosen more than once, choosing a different damage type each time.

entries.name: Powerful Build
entries: The target counts as one Size larger when determining its carrying capacity and the weight it can push, drag, or lift.

entries.name: Compression
entries: The target can squeeze through spaces as though it were one Size smaller.

entries.name: Additional Limbs
entries: The target grows one additional pair of arms, tentacles, or similarly functional appendages. They can hold, carry, manipulate, draw, stow, and interact with objects normally.
They don't grant additional Actions, Bonus Actions, Reactions, or attacks.

entries.name: Prehensile Tail
entries: The target develops a strong prehensile tail or comparable appendage. It can hold and manipulate objects, open doors, retrieve items, and perform other simple object interactions.
The appendage can't wield weapons, use a Shield, or perform Somatic components unless another feature allows it.

entries.name: Leaping Musculature
entries: The target's Long Jump and High Jump distances are tripled. It doesn't need to move 10 feet before making a running jump.
The first 20 feet of any fall are ignored when calculating its falling damage.

entries.name: Amphibious Skin
entries: The target can breathe air and water and can comfortably survive ordinary freshwater, saltwater, and deep-water environments. Unlike Aquatic Adaptation, this adaptation doesn't grant a Swim Speed.

entries.name: Environmental Adaptation
entries: Choose extreme heat or extreme cold. The target automatically succeeds on saving throws and ignores ordinary environmental penalties caused solely by the chosen environment.
This doesn't grant Resistance to Fire or Cold damage.

entries.name: Keen Senses
entries: Choose sight, hearing, or smell. The target has Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks relying on the chosen sense.
This adaptation can be chosen repeatedly for different senses.

entries.name: Venom Gland
entries: The target develops organs capable of producing dangerous venom. Once per turn when the target deals Piercing or Slashing damage with a natural weapon created by this spell, it can deal an additional {@damage 1d6} Poison damage.

entries.name: Adhesive Limbs
entries: The target can adhere to solid surfaces. It can remain attached to walls and ceilings without using its hands.

entries.name: Dense Frame
entries: The target can permanently increase its weight to as much as four times its normal weight without changing Size. It has Advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to resist being pushed, pulled, knocked Prone, or otherwise forcibly moved.

entries.name: Hollow Frame
entries: The target can permanently reduce its weight to as little as one-quarter normal. Falling damage it takes is reduced by an amount equal to five times its Proficiency Bonus.

entries.name: Extended Reach
entries: Choose one pair of limbs or one natural weapon created by Grand Design. Its reach increases by 5 feet.

entries.name: Echolocation
entries: The target gains Blindsight 10 feet while it can hear. This sense doesn't function while the target is Deafened.

entries.name: Photosynthetic Tissue
entries: If the target spends at least 1 hour in bright sunlight during a day, it requires only half as much food that day. This doesn't remove its need for water, air, or rest.

entries.name: 8th-Level Casting
entries: When you cast Grand Design using an 8th-level spell slot, choose three adaptations rather than two. Each choice can be a Major Adaptation or one of the following Greater Adaptations.

entries.name: Blindsight
entries: The target permanently gains Blindsight 60 feet.

entries.name: Greater Wings
entries: The target gains a Fly Speed equal to twice its Speed and can Hover. If it already possesses Wings from this spell, Greater Wings replaces that adaptation.

entries.name: Greater Burrowing
entries: The target gains a Burrow Speed equal to its Speed. It can burrow through natural earth normally and through solid natural stone at half speed. It still can't freely burrow through worked structures.

entries.name: Regenerative Flesh
entries: At the start of each of the target's turns, if it has at least 1 Hit Point and no more than half its Hit Points, it regains Hit Points equal to its Proficiency Bonus.

entries.name: Flexible Anatomy
entries: The target can compress its body enough to pass through an opening as narrow as 6 inches without squeezing. Objects too large to fit through the opening don't compress unless they are physically part of the transformed body.

entries.name: Greater Natural Weapon
entries: Choose one natural weapon created by Grand Design. Its damage die becomes {@damage 2d8} instead of {@damage 1d8}.

entries.name: Greater Resilience
entries: Choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Poison, Radiant, or Thunder. The target permanently gains Resistance to the chosen damage type.
This adaptation can be chosen repeatedly for different damage types.

entries.name: Mighty Frame
entries: The target can permanently become Large. Its equipment can be reshaped to accommodate its new body as part of the casting. Its statistics don't otherwise change merely because its Size changes.
If the target is already Large or larger, it can instead count as one additional Size larger when determining carrying, pushing, dragging, and lifting capacity.

entries.name: Tremorsense
entries: The target gains Tremorsense 60 feet while it and whatever it is detecting are in contact with the same ground or continuous solid surface.

entries.name: Elastic Anatomy
entries: The target can stretch its limbs and body far beyond their normal proportions. Its reach with unarmed strikes, natural weapons, and object interactions increases by 10 feet. It can extend or retract these structures freely.

entries.name: Chameleon Flesh
entries: The target can alter the color, pattern, and texture of its exterior to match its environment. It has Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.
It can also take the Hide action while only Lightly Obscured by natural terrain or environmental features.

entries.name: Reactive Armor
entries: When the target takes Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison damage, it can use its Reaction to gain Resistance to that instance of damage.

entries.name: Venomous Arsenal
entries: Choose one natural weapon created by Grand Design. Once per turn when the target hits with that weapon, it deals an additional {@damage 2d8} Poison damage. When this adaptation is gained, you can choose Acid instead of Poison.

entries.name: Secondary Heart
entries: The target develops redundant circulatory organs. It has Advantage on Constitution saving throws against effects that would cause it to be Paralyzed, Stunned, or Unconscious.

entries.name: Redundant Organs
entries: The target's vital organs are duplicated or distributed through its body. It has Advantage on saving throws against Poison and Disease.
Destroying or removing a single ordinary vital organ doesn't by itself kill the target.

entries.name: Amphibious Metabolism
entries: The target can hold its breath for 1 hour. If it can already breathe underwater, it no longer needs to breathe while underwater.

entries.name: Thermal Vision
entries: The target gains Darkvision 180 feet. Within 60 feet, it can also perceive creatures through ordinary smoke, mist, steam, and similar atmospheric concealment by detecting heat differences.

entries.name: Shock-Absorbing Body
entries: The target gains Resistance to falling damage and damage caused specifically by collisions or crushing impacts.

entries.name: Reserve Metabolism
entries: The target can survive for 30 days without food and 7 days without water before suffering the normal effects of deprivation. This doesn't prevent Exhaustion from other sources.

entries.name: 9th-Level Casting
entries: When you cast Grand Design using a 9th-level spell slot, choose four adaptations. Each choice can be a Major Adaptation, Greater Adaptation, or one of the following Perfect Adaptations.

entries.name: Truesight
entries: The target permanently gains Truesight 60 feet.

entries.name: Perfect Flight
entries: The target gains a Fly Speed equal to twice its Speed and can Hover. It doesn't fall solely because it becomes Incapacitated while airborne.
If it possesses Wings or Greater Wings from Grand Design, this adaptation replaces them.

entries.name: Greater Regeneration
entries: At the start of each of the target's turns, if it has at least 1 Hit Point, it regains {@dice 2d10} Hit Points.
This replaces Regenerative Flesh rather than stacking with it.

entries.name: Deathless Organs
entries: The target's vital anatomy becomes extraordinarily redundant. It has Advantage on Death Saving Throws.
When it rolls a 19 or 20 on a Death Saving Throw, it gains the benefit normally gained from rolling a 20.
The destruction of an ordinary individual organ doesn't automatically kill it while enough of its body remains functional.

entries.name: Perfect Resilience
entries: Choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Poison, Radiant, or Thunder. The target permanently gains Immunity to the chosen damage type.
Any Resistance it possesses to that type from Grand Design is replaced by this Immunity. This adaptation can be chosen repeatedly for different damage types.

entries.name: Colossal Anatomy
entries: The target can permanently become Huge. Its equipment can be reshaped to accommodate its body as part of the casting. Its statistics don't otherwise change merely because of its Size.

entries.name: Mutable Flesh
entries: The target gains voluntary control over its alterations from Grand Design. As a Bonus Action, it can alter its cosmetic appearance and retract or manifest physical adaptations granted by this spell, such as wings, natural weapons, additional limbs, tails, horns, and similar external anatomy.
Retracting an adaptation doesn't remove it. The target can manifest it again with another Bonus Action.

entries.name: Perfect Adaptation
entries: Choose two Major Adaptations. Those two adaptations together consume only one adaptation choice from this casting.

entries.name: Universal Respiration
entries: The target no longer needs to breathe. It is therefore unaffected by ordinary suffocation, drowning, smoke inhalation, vacuum, or similar hazards that function solely by preventing respiration.

entries.name: Perfect Metabolism
entries: The target no longer needs ordinary food or water to survive. It can still eat and drink normally. This doesn't remove its need for rest.

entries.name: Perfect Senses
entries: The target gains Darkvision 300 feet, Blindsight 30 feet, and Tremorsense 60 feet.
If it already has one of these senses with a greater range, it retains the greater range.

entries.name: Distributed Mind
entries: The target's nervous system and cognitive functions become distributed throughout its body. It has Advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws against effects that would Charm it, Frighten it, Stun it, or control its actions.
Destroying or removing its head doesn't automatically kill it while enough of the rest of its body remains functional.

entries.name: Perfect Regrowth
entries: If the target loses a limb or other body part, that part naturally regrows after {@dice 1d6} hours, provided the target remains alive.
A severed body part held against its original location can instead reattach over the course of 1 minute.

entries.name: Internal Armory
entries: The target can retract any natural weapon created by Grand Design completely inside its body and manifest it again as a Bonus Action.
Whenever it manifests that weapon, it can change its damage type to Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing.

entries.name: Perfect Camouflage
entries: As a Bonus Action, the target can alter its exterior with such precision that it becomes Invisible until the start of its next turn, until it makes an attack roll, or until it casts a spell.
It can do this a number of times equal to its Proficiency Bonus and regains all expended uses when it finishes a Long Rest.

entries.name: Living Fortress
entries: The target's body becomes extraordinarily resistant to physical harm. While it isn't wearing armor, its base AC is 18. A Shield can modify this AC normally.

entries.name: Perfect Amphibian
entries: The target can survive comfortably in air, water, extreme ocean depths, and vacuum. It suffers no harm from ordinary environmental pressure or lack of atmospheric pressure.
This doesn't provide Resistance or Immunity to magical or supernatural pressure damage.

entries.name: Adaptive Immunity
entries: Whenever the target finishes a Long Rest, choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, or Thunder. The target gains Immunity to the chosen damage type until it finishes its next Long Rest.
The chosen type can be changed after each Long Rest.

entries.name: Monstrous Reach
entries: Choose one pair of limbs or one natural weapon created by Grand Design. Its reach increases by 15 feet.

entries.name: Independent Limbs
entries: Additional limbs created by Grand Design become capable of extraordinarily precise independent coordination.
Once on each of the target's turns, it can perform one additional object interaction and can draw or stow up to two objects without using an Action.
This doesn't grant an additional Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, or attack.

entries.name: Perfect Compression
entries: The target can compress its body enough to pass through an opening as narrow as 1 inch, regardless of its Size.
Equipment physically incorporated into the target's transformed anatomy compresses with it. Separately carried objects don't.

entries.name: Ageless Body
entries: The target's body no longer physically deteriorates because of aging. Its chronological age continues to increase, but it no longer becomes physically weaker, frailer, or less healthy solely from age.
This adaptation doesn't prevent death from damage, disease, starvation, suffocation, or other causes.

entries.name: Naturalized Form
entries: The alterations created by Grand Design aren't an ongoing spell effect. Once the casting is complete, they become part of the target's actual body.

Dispel Magic can't remove them. An Antimagic Field doesn't suppress them. They don't require Concentration, don't disappear when the caster dies, and physical body parts created by the spell can be injured, severed, healed, or restored like natural body parts.
Magic that restores a lost natural body part can restore one created by this spell. The target is not considered transformed by an ongoing spell merely because its body was altered by Grand Design.
The spell doesn't automatically cause alterations to become hereditary. Whether descendants can inherit them depends on the creature's biology and the setting.

entries.name: Reversal and Further Modification
entries: Another casting of Grand Design can permanently remove, replace, reshape, or upgrade alterations previously created by the spell.
A Wish spell or similarly powerful effect can also restore a creature to an earlier physical form.
There is otherwise no automatic expiration to the transformation.

spell.name: Spellheart

m.text: a flawless gemstone worth at least 2,500 GP, which the spell consumes

entries: Some spells are learned. Others are memorized.
You take a formula and drive it deeper than either, engraving its pattern into the very structure of a living soul.
When the ritual ends, the magic no longer needs a page, a prepared thought, or even the caster who bestowed it.
The spell has become part of the creature itself.

Choose one willing creature you touch throughout the casting and one spell of 3rd level or lower that you know, have prepared, or have recorded in a spellbook you can use. The chosen spell becomes permanently embedded within the target.

entries.name: Innate Spell
entries: The target permanently gains the ability to cast the embedded spell without needing to prepare it or otherwise know it.
When the spell is embedded, choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. The target uses that ability as its spellcasting ability for the embedded spell.

If the target doesn't already have a spell save DC or spell attack modifier using that ability, its spell save DC equals 8 + its Proficiency Bonus + the chosen ability modifier, and its spell attack modifier equals its Proficiency Bonus + the chosen ability modifier.

entries.name: Casting the Embedded Spell
entries: The target can cast the embedded spell once without expending a spell slot and regains this free casting when it finishes a Long Rest. The free casting is cast at the spell's lowest level.
If the target has spell slots, it can also cast the embedded spell using those slots normally. The embedded spell can be upcast normally.

For example, if Spellheart embeds a 3rd-level spell and the target later expends a 6th-level spell slot to cast it, the spell is cast at 6th level and gains any benefits it normally receives from being cast using a higher-level slot.
The target doesn't need to possess the spell on any of its class spell lists to cast it this way.

entries.name: Components
entries: The target must provide the embedded spell's normal Verbal, Somatic, and Material components.
If a Material component has a cost, the target must provide it normally. If the component is consumed, it is consumed normally.

entries.name: Permanent Integration
entries: Spellheart isn't an ongoing magical effect after the ritual is completed. The embedded spell becomes a permanent innate magical capability of the target.
Dispel Magic can't remove it. An Antimagic Field can suppress the casting or effects of the embedded spell normally, but doesn't remove the target's ability to cast it.
The ability remains if the caster of Spellheart dies. Destroying or losing the original spellbook or other source of the embedded spell has no effect.
The target doesn't need to remain near the original caster and retains the embedded spell even if it later changes class or loses access to the spell list from which the spell originally came.

entries.name: Repeated Spellheart
entries: A creature can be affected by Spellheart any number of times. Each casting can embed another spell, and the effects of separate castings are cumulative.
A creature can't gain the same spell more than once from Spellheart. Repeatedly embedding the same spell doesn't grant additional free uses.
There is otherwise no inherent limit to the number of different spells a creature can permanently possess through Spellheart.
The caster can target themself with Spellheart.

entries.name: Replacing or Removing a Spell
entries: When you cast Spellheart on a creature that already possesses one or more spells from Spellheart, you can choose to permanently remove one embedded spell instead of adding a new one.
You can also replace one embedded spell with another spell valid for that casting.
A Wish spell or similarly powerful effect can also remove a spell embedded by Spellheart.

items: {@b 8th Level.} You can embed a spell of 5th level or lower. The target can use the embedded spell's free casting twice per Long Rest instead of once. Both free castings are made at the embedded spell's lowest level. When using a spell slot of its own, the target can still upcast the embedded spell normally.

{@b 9th Level.} You can embed a spell of 7th level or lower. The target can use the embedded spell's free casting three times per Long Rest. All three free castings are made at the embedded spell's lowest level. When using a spell slot of its own, the target can still upcast the embedded spell normally.

spell.name: Soul Anchor

m.text: a specially prepared vessel worth at least 5,000 GP, which the spell consumes when the anchor activates

entries: Death can claim a body only when there is nowhere else for the soul to return.
You prepare such a place in advance, fastening a living creature to a vessel that remembers exactly what it is meant to restore.
When death finally arrives, the bond tears the creature away from its ending and rebuilds what was lost.
The anchor waits for years if necessary. Death only determines when it is used.

Choose one willing living creature you touch and one object within your reach that will serve as its Soul Anchor. When the casting is completed, the target becomes permanently bound to that anchor until the bond is triggered or removed. The target can be you.

entries.name: The Anchor
entries: The chosen object becomes the target's Soul Anchor. It can be almost any nonliving object that can reasonably remain intact, such as a gemstone, statue, sealed urn, weapon, piece of jewelry, book, or specially constructed reliquary.
The anchor doesn't need to remain near the target. The target always knows whether its Soul Anchor still exists and what plane of existence it is on.

entries.name: When the Target Dies
entries: When the target dies, the Soul Anchor activates automatically.

The target's body disappears after 1 minute, along with everything it was wearing or carrying when it died. At the end of that minute, the target reappears alive in the nearest unoccupied space within 5 feet of the Soul Anchor.
The restored creature returns with all its Hit Points, has its missing body parts restored, retains all memories it possessed when it died, and returns with the equipment it possessed when it died.

The creature's spell slots, expended features, charges, and other resources remain exactly as they were when it died. Conditions or effects that ended only because the creature died don't automatically return unless their own rules say otherwise.
The Soul Anchor is then consumed, ending the spell.

entries.name: Forced Return
entries: The restoration doesn't require the creature to be willing at the moment of death.
Effects that normally require a soul to be free or willing to return don't prevent Soul Anchor from functioning.

If the creature's soul or consciousness has been trapped, imprisoned, consumed, or otherwise prevented from existing independently, the Anchor attempts to reclaim it as part of the restoration. A sufficiently powerful effect can still prevent this, as determined by the DM.

entries.name: Destruction of the Anchor
entries: If the Soul Anchor is destroyed before the target dies, the spell ends without triggering. Destroying the anchor doesn't harm the target.

entries.name: No Distance Limit
entries: The target and its Soul Anchor can be any distance apart, including on different planes of existence. Distance doesn't weaken the bond.

entries.name: Recasting Soul Anchor
entries: A creature can have only one Soul Anchor created by this spell at a time.
Casting Soul Anchor on a creature that already has one replaces the previous bond. The old anchor immediately ceases to function as a Soul Anchor but isn't otherwise harmed.

items: {@b 8th Level.} The Soul Anchor activates immediately when the target dies instead of after 1 minute. The target can also choose whether its equipment returns with it or remains where it died.

{@b 9th Level.} The Soul Anchor isn't consumed when it activates. After restoring the target, it becomes dormant until the target finishes 7 Long Rests, after which it can activate again. A 9th-level Soul Anchor can therefore restore the same creature repeatedly as long as the anchor itself survives.

spell.name: Unbound
entries: Magic ceases to recognize the limitations imposed upon you.
Your body and will exist as though restraints were merely suggestions.
For the duration, you move and act according to your own rules.
While the spell lasts, you gain the following benefits:

items: Your Speed can't be reduced, and you ignore Difficult Terrain.

You can move through the spaces of creatures and through nonmagical objects as though they were Difficult Terrain. If you end your turn inside an object, you are shunted to the nearest unoccupied space and take 2d10 Force damage.
You can't be Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Restrained, or magically put to sleep.
You can take Actions, Bonus Actions, and Reactions even if another effect would normally prevent you from taking them.
Magical effects can't force you to move, teleport you, banish you, or change your form unless you allow them to.
You can speak and provide Verbal components even while within an area of magical Silence.
You can perform Somatic components even if your hands are occupied or restrained.
You don't require Material components that lack a listed cost.

entries: Whenever a spell or magical effect would impose a limitation that directly prevents you from moving, acting, casting a spell, or using one of your features, you can ignore that limitation for the duration of Unbound.

Unbound doesn't end an effect affecting you. It merely prevents that effect from restricting you while this spell lasts. When the spell ends, any effects that haven't otherwise expired resume affecting you normally.

items: {@b 8th Level.} The duration becomes 1 hour.

{@b 9th Level.} The duration becomes 8 hours, and the spell can't be ended early by Dispel Magic or a similar effect unless that effect was created with a 9th-level spell slot or is otherwise capable of ending a 9th-level spell.

spell.name: Invincible Form
entries: Your body is forced into a state that refuses to acknowledge damage as meaningful.
For the duration, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have Resistance to all damage.
Whenever you take damage, reduce that damage by 10 after applying Resistance.
Your Hit Point Maximum can't be reduced.
You can't be knocked Prone or moved against your will.
You have Advantage on Strength and Constitution saving throws.
If damage would reduce you to 0 Hit Points but not kill you outright, you drop to 1 Hit Point instead.

entries: Each time the final benefit prevents you from dropping to 0 Hit Points, its damage reduction increases by 5 for the rest of the spell.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The damage reduction becomes 15 instead of 10, and you are immune to the Grappled and Restrained conditions for the duration.
{@b 9th Level.} The damage reduction becomes 20, and while you have at least 1 Hit Point, damage can't reduce you below 1 Hit Point unless the damage would kill you outright.

spell.name: Worldbreaker Lance
entries: You condense overwhelming magical force into a single line and drive it through everything in its path.
A 300-foot-long, 10-foot-wide line erupts from you in a direction you choose.

Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 12d12} Force damage and is pushed up to 30 feet directly away from you. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and isn't pushed.
Objects and structures in the line take the spell's full damage automatically.

The line ignores half cover and three-quarters cover. Nonmagical objects and structures reduced to 0 Hit Points by this spell are destroyed outright, and the line continues through them without ending.

Magical barriers and created objects in the line take damage from the spell as though they were creatures. If such an effect has no Hit Points, treat it as having Hit Points equal to 20 × the level of the spell that created it for the purpose of this spell only.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The damage increases to {@damage 24d12}, and the line becomes 15 feet wide.
{@b 9th Level.} The damage increases to {@damage 48d12}, the line becomes 20 feet wide, and creatures that fail the saving throw are also knocked Prone.

spell.name: Arcane Cataclysm
entries: You force raw magic into a violent collapse and detonate it at a point you can see within range.

Each creature in a 30-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 10d12} Force damage and suffers one of the following effects of your choice:

items: It is knocked Prone.
It is pushed up to 30 feet directly away from the center of the sphere.
It can't take Reactions until the end of its next turn.
Its Speed is halved until the end of its next turn.

entries: On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and suffers none of the additional effects.
Objects and structures in the area take the spell's full damage automatically.

entries.name: Arcane Collapse
entries: Any spell or magical effect whose area overlaps the sphere and whose level is lower than the spell slot used to cast Arcane Cataclysm immediately ends, provided it is an effect that could normally be ended by {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB}.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The damage increases to {@damage 20d12}, and you can choose two additional effects instead of one.
{@b 9th Level.} The damage increases to {@damage 40d12}, and you can choose all four additional effects for creatures that fail the saving throw.

spell.name: Spell Devourer

time.condition: which you take when you are targeted by a spell or included in a spell's area

entries: You seize the magic attempting to affect you, tear it from its caster's control, and consume it as your own power.

The triggering spell is the first spell devoured by this casting. If it was cast using a spell slot of 7th level or lower, it has no effect on you. If it affects other creatures or areas, it continues to affect them normally.

For the duration, whenever you are targeted by a spell or included in a spell's area, you can devour that spell as it affects you. If the spell was cast using a spell slot of 7th level or lower, it has no effect on you. A devoured spell otherwise continues to affect other creatures, objects, and areas normally.
Each time you successfully devour a spell, choose one of the following benefits:

items.name: Arcane Nourishment.
items.entry: Regain one expended spell slot of a level equal to or lower than the devoured spell's level, up to a maximum of 5th level.

items.name: Borrowed Power.
items.entry: Until Spell Devourer ends, you know the devoured spell and can cast it without expending a spell slot or providing Material components. You use your own spellcasting ability, spell attack modifier, and spell save DC for it. Each casting uses the same spell level as the spell you devoured. If you choose this benefit for multiple spells, each of those spells remains available to you until Spell Devourer ends.

items.name: Overcharge.
items.entry: Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to 10 × the devoured spell's level. Until the end of your next turn, you have Advantage on spell attack rolls, and creatures have Disadvantage on saving throws against the next spell you cast.

entries: Spell Devourer has no limit on the number of spells it can devour during its duration.
If a spell was cast without using a spell slot, the GM determines its effective spell level for the purpose of this spell.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} You can devour spells of 8th level or lower, and Arcane Nourishment can restore a spell slot of up to 6th level.
{@b 9th Level.} You can devour spells of 9th level or lower, and Arcane Nourishment can restore a spell slot of up to 7th level.

spell.name: Sovereign Pressure
entries: You release an overwhelming magical presence that crushes resistance and forces weaker wills beneath your authority.
When you cast this spell, each creature of your choice within 60 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw.
On a failed save, a creature is Overwhelmed for the duration. While Overwhelmed, it suffers the following effects:

items: Its Speed is halved.
It has Disadvantage on attack rolls against you.
It has Disadvantage on saving throws against your spells and magical effects.
It can't willingly move closer to you unless you allow it.
It can't take Reactions.
The first time on each of its turns that it deals damage to you, reduce that damage by 20.

entries: At the end of each of its turns, an Overwhelmed creature can repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.
Whenever a creature succeeds on this saving throw, you can use your Reaction to force it to reroll the save and use the new result.

entries.name: Crushing Presence
entries: Whenever a creature Overwhelmed by this spell starts its turn within 30 feet of you, it takes {@damage 4d10} Psychic damage.
A creature reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage is knocked unconscious rather than killed, unless you choose otherwise.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The radius becomes 90 feet, the damage reduction becomes 30, and Crushing Presence deals {@damage 8d10} Psychic damage.

{@b 9th Level.} The radius becomes 120 feet, the damage reduction becomes 40, and Crushing Presence deals {@damage 16d10} Psychic damage. Creatures affected by the spell also have Disadvantage on the saving throw they make at the end of their turns to end the effect.

spell.name: Death Sentence
entries: You designate one creature you can see within range as condemned. The target must make a Constitution saving throw.
On a failed save, it becomes Condemned for the duration. On a successful save, it takes {@damage 6d10} Necrotic damage, and the spell ends.
While Condemned, the target suffers the following effects:

items: The target can't regain Hit Points.
It has Disadvantage on Death Saving Throws.
Whenever you deal damage to it, it takes an additional {@damage 3d10} Necrotic damage. This additional damage can occur only once per turn.
The first time each round the target is reduced to half its Hit Points or fewer, it must immediately make another Constitution saving throw.

entries: On a failed save against this secondary saving throw, the target takes {@damage 10d10} Necrotic damage.
If this damage reduces the target to 50 Hit Points or fewer, you can choose to execute it. If you do, the target immediately drops to 0 Hit Points.
A creature that is immune to Necrotic damage can't be executed by this spell, but it can still become Condemned.
At the end of each of its turns, the target can repeat the original saving throw, ending the spell on itself on a success.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The bonus damage becomes {@damage 6d10}, the secondary damage becomes {@damage 20d10}, and the execution threshold becomes 75 Hit Points.

{@b 9th Level.} The bonus damage becomes {@damage 12d10}, the secondary damage becomes {@damage 40d10}, and the execution threshold becomes 100 Hit Points. In addition, the target has Disadvantage on all saving throws it makes against this spell.

spell.name: Arcane Overlord
entries: You tear away the restraints on your spellcasting and force your magic to operate beyond its normal limits.
For the duration, you gain the following benefits:

items: Whenever a spell you cast deals damage, that damage is increased by {@damage 2d10} Force damage. This increase applies each time the spell deals damage.
When you cast a spell that forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw, choose one creature affected by the spell. That creature has Disadvantage on its first saving throw against that spell.
When you cast a spell with a casting time of 1 Action, you can cast it as a Bonus Action instead. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until the start of your next turn.
Casting a spell as a Bonus Action through this spell doesn't prevent you from casting another leveled spell during the same turn.
Your spell attacks ignore half cover and three-quarters cover.
Your spells ignore Resistance to Force, Necrotic, Psychic, Radiant, Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, and Thunder damage.
If a spell you cast would normally end because you lose Concentration, you can choose for it to remain active until the end of your next turn instead.

entries.name: Unrestricted Casting
entries: Once on each of your turns, when you cast a spell using a spell slot of 5th level or lower, you can cast that spell without expending the spell slot.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The additional damage becomes {@damage 4d10}, and Unrestricted Casting can affect spells of 6th level or lower.

{@b 9th Level.} The additional damage becomes {@damage 8d10}, Unrestricted Casting can affect spells of 7th level or lower, and you can use the Bonus Action casting benefit twice on each of your turns instead of once.

spell.name: Grand Survey

m.text: a map, chart, or blank sheet of parchment worth at least 100 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: You extend your awareness across the surrounding land and impress what you perceive onto the material used to cast the spell.
When the casting is complete, choose a point on the same plane within 10 miles of you. For the duration, you gain supernatural knowledge of the area within 5 miles of that point.
You learn the location and general nature of:

items: settlements, roads, ruins, caves, tunnels, and major structures;
bodies of water, cliffs, forests, mountains, and other major terrain features;
active portals, teleportation circles, planar breaches, and extradimensional entrances;
areas affected by spells or persistent magical effects of 7th level or lower;
creatures of your choice that are Huge or larger;
any concentration of 100 or more creatures within a contiguous area;
major sources of magical power, provided they aren't concealed by an effect of a higher level than this spell.

entries: The spell doesn't automatically reveal the identities of individual creatures, the contents of sealed containers, thoughts, passwords, or information that couldn't reasonably be represented as a location or feature.

entries.name: Living Map
entries: The material component becomes a magical map for the duration.
The map updates itself as terrain, creatures, magical effects, entrances, and other revealed features change.
While touching the map, you can focus on any revealed location and learn:

items: its approximate dimensions;
its distance and direction from you;
whether it is above ground, underground, underwater, or extradimensional;
and the shortest reasonably traversable route to it known to the spell.

entries: The map can reveal secret doors, hidden passages, buried chambers, and magically concealed locations if the effect hiding them was created by a spell of 7th level or lower.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The chosen point can be within 100 miles, the surveyed radius becomes 20 miles, and the duration becomes 24 hours.

{@b 9th Level.} You can choose any point on the same plane that you can name or clearly identify, the surveyed radius becomes 100 miles, and the duration becomes 7 days. Effects of 8th level or lower can't conceal locations or magical phenomena from the survey.

spell.name: Echoes of the Departed

components.m: an object that belonged to the deceased creature or a fragment of its remains

entries: You draw out the lingering imprint left behind by a dead creature and give that memory enough form to answer you.
Touch the material component and name the deceased creature you intend to contact. The creature must have been dead for no more than 100 years.

A spectral reconstruction of the creature appears in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of you. This manifestation isn't the creature's soul and doesn't return it to life. It is an echo formed from residual memory, emotion, and magical traces.
For the duration, the echo can:

items: speak and understand the languages the creature knew in life;
answer questions using memories the creature possessed before death;
describe creatures, locations, events, objects, and conversations it personally witnessed;
reproduce its own voice, mannerisms, and appearance as they were at any point in its life;
identify individuals, symbols, places, or objects it personally knew;
recount memories without the evasiveness normally associated with {@spell Speak with Dead|XPHB}.

entries: The echo can't deliberately lie, but its memories can still be incomplete, mistaken, altered, or missing.

entries.name: Memory Reconstruction
entries: You can ask the echo to recreate one memory it personally experienced.

The surrounding area within 30 feet becomes an illusory reconstruction of that memory. Creatures you choose within the area can see and hear the memory as though they were present, though they can't interact with or alter it.
The reconstruction lasts for up to 10 minutes and can be paused, repeated, or viewed from any position within the recreated area.
You can reconstruct any number of memories during the spell's duration.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The creature can have been dead for up to 1,000 years, the duration becomes 8 hours, and Memory Reconstruction can recreate an area up to 100 feet across.

{@b 9th Level.} There is no limit based on how long the creature has been dead, the duration becomes 7 days, and the echo can reconstruct memories even if its physical remains no longer exist, provided you possess an object that was personally significant to it.

spell.name: Witness of the Place

m.text: a silver lens worth at least 500 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: You awaken the memory carried by a place itself, drawing impressions from stone, soil, air, and lingering magic.
Choose the area within 60 feet of you. For the duration, you can perceive significant events that occurred within that area during the previous 30 days.
As an Action, choose a point in the area and a moment or event you wish to investigate. If such an event occurred there, the area produces a spectral reconstruction of it.

entries.name: Echo of Events
entries: The reconstruction can reproduce:

items: creatures that were physically present;
their appearance, movements, voices, and visible actions;
spoken conversations;
spells and magical effects that were visibly or audibly manifested;
objects that were moved, damaged, created, destroyed, or taken;
entrances, exits, hidden passages, or doors used during the event;
the sequence and approximate timing of events.

entries: The reconstruction isn't an illusion created from a creature's memory. It is drawn from the residual history of the location itself.
You can move freely through the reconstruction, pause it, resume it, repeat it, or accelerate and slow its playback.

entries.name: Truth of the Scene
entries: While viewing a reconstruction, you can focus on one creature, object, or event. You then learn whether what you are witnessing was altered by an Illusion, shapechanging effect, magical disguise, memory manipulation, or similar magic.
If such magic was created by a spell of 7th level or lower, the reconstruction shows both the altered appearance and the underlying reality.
The spell can't reveal thoughts, intentions, information that was never expressed or manifested, or events that occurred entirely outside the affected area.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} You can examine events from the previous 10 years, the radius becomes 300 feet, and the duration becomes 8 hours.

{@b 9th Level.} You can examine any event that has ever occurred within the area, the radius becomes 1 mile, and the duration becomes 7 days. Effects created by spells of 8th level or lower can't conceal, erase, or falsify the history revealed by this spell.

spell.name: Sanctum of Accord

m.text: a silver seal worth at least 1,000 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: You inscribe a binding sanctuary into a structure, chamber, or enclosed area you touch. The protected area can fill a space up to 100 feet on a side.
When you cast the spell, choose creatures individually, by a clearly defined group, or by a password or symbol known to you. Those creatures are Authorized for the duration.
You decide which Authorized creatures receive each beneficial effect of the sanctum. You can grant or withhold individual benefits separately for each creature or clearly defined group.

For the entire duration of the spell, you retain control over its adjustable functions regardless of distance or planar boundaries. Whenever the spell allows you to choose permissions, designations, instructions, zones, settings, targets for its benefits, or similar ongoing options, you can change those choices at any time, requiring no action. This doesn't move or enlarge the spell's original area unless the spell says otherwise.

entries.name: Absolute Threshold
entries: An Unauthorized creature can't enter the protected area by teleportation, planar travel, extradimensional movement, possession, or magical transformation that would place it inside.
If such a creature attempts to enter by one of those means, the attempt fails and any resource used is expended.
Physical entry remains possible unless prevented by another effect.

entries.name: Sanctified Interior
entries: While inside the sanctum, Authorized creatures gain the following benefits:

items: They have Advantage on saving throws against spells and magical effects.
They can't be magically Charmed, Frightened, or possessed.
Their location can't be detected by Divination spells cast from outside the sanctum.
Magical effects originating outside the sanctum can't forcibly teleport, banish, summon, or move them out of it.
Creatures outside the sanctum can't magically observe or hear events occurring inside it.

entries.name: Suppression of Intrusion
entries: Whenever an Unauthorized creature inside the sanctum casts a spell of 5th level or lower, you can cause that spell to fail.
You don't need to be present or conscious to do so.
The spell slot and any consumed components are still expended.
You can suppress a number of spells equal to your Proficiency Bonus during the spell's duration.

entries.name: Living Seal
entries: While touching any part of the sanctum, you know:

items: how many Unauthorized creatures are currently inside;
whether an Authorized creature has entered or left since you last checked;
whether the sanctum has been targeted by a spell or magical effect;
and the location of any damaged opening, broken seal, or magical breach within the protected area.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The protected area can be up to 500 feet on a side, the duration becomes 7 days, and Suppression of Intrusion can stop spells of 6th level or lower.

{@b 9th Level.} The protected area can encompass an entire structure or contiguous complex no larger than 1 mile across, the duration becomes 30 days, and Suppression of Intrusion can stop spells of 8th level or lower. In addition, teleportation, planar travel, and magical observation created by spells of 8th level or lower can't bypass the sanctum.

spell.name: Name the Unseen

m.text: a polished obsidian mirror worth at least 1,000 gp, which isn't consumed
