entries: You call upon the hidden structure of magic to reveal the true identity of what stands concealed behind false names, disguises, altered forms, and magical deception.
For the duration, whenever you can see a creature, object, or magical effect, you can use an Action to scrutinize it.
If the target is within 120 feet, you learn all of the following that apply:

items: whether it is disguised, transformed, shapechanged, possessed, duplicated, or magically concealed;
whether its current appearance differs from its natural or original form;
whether the name by which it is currently known is its true name, an alias, a title, or a fabricated identity;
whether it is under an Illusion, Transmutation, Enchantment, possession, or similar effect;
the school of magic and spell level of each spell currently affecting it, if any;
whether the creature or object is native to the plane you are currently on;
whether its body is its original body.

entries.name: True Name
entries: If the target is a creature, you can focus on it for 1 minute without breaking line of sight.
At the end of that minute, the target makes a Charisma saving throw.
On a failed save, you learn the creature's true name, if it has one.
For the purpose of this spell, a true name is the identity by which the creature fundamentally recognizes itself, not merely its legal name, title, nickname, or current alias.
A creature that succeeds on the saving throw is immune to this part of the spell for 24 hours.

entries.name: Unmasking
entries: If an effect concealing or altering the target was created by a spell of 7th level or lower, you can see through that effect automatically for the duration.
This doesn't end the effect for other creatures.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The duration becomes 8 hours, the range becomes 1 mile, and True Name no longer requires you to maintain line of sight for the full minute after you begin focusing.

{@b 9th Level.} The duration becomes 7 days. You can scrutinize any creature, object, or magical effect on the same plane that you can clearly identify, even if you can't currently see it. Effects created by spells of 8th level or lower can't conceal a target's identity, form, origin, or true name from this spell.

spell.name: Grand Conclave

m.text: a circular mirror or polished table worth at least 1,000 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: You create a private extradimensional demiplane where distant allies can gather, communicate, and work together beyond the limitations of ordinary distance.

When you cast this spell, name or clearly identify up to twenty-four willing creatures on the same plane of existence as you. Each chosen creature immediately becomes aware of the invitation and can accept or refuse it.

An invited creature can enter the conclave at any time during the spell's duration. Its physical body remains in its original location while a tangible magical projection of the creature appears within the conclave. The creature perceives through this projection and can see, hear, speak, move, and interact with the conclave normally.
You decide which invited creatures can use each benefit or capability provided by the conclave. You can grant or withhold individual benefits separately for each participant or group of participants.

For the entire duration of the spell, you retain control over its adjustable functions regardless of distance or planar boundaries. Whenever the spell allows you to choose permissions, designations, instructions, zones, settings, targets for its benefits, or similar ongoing options, you can change those choices at any time, requiring no action. This doesn't move or enlarge the spell's original area unless the spell says otherwise.

entries.name: The Conclave
entries: The conclave is a comfortable extradimensional chamber whose appearance and layout you determine when you cast the spell. It automatically provides enough space and ordinary furnishings for all participants.

The conclave is a sealed private demiplane. Only creatures you have invited can enter it. A creature that hasn't been invited can't enter the conclave by any means, including teleportation, planar travel, portals, summoning, possession, or similar magic. Creatures outside the conclave can't see, hear, perceive, physically interact with, or magically observe anything occurring within it.

Once created, the conclave exists independently for the spell's full duration. You don't need to remain inside it, remain near the place where you cast the spell, or maintain Concentration. You can leave and return freely, and doing so doesn't end the spell. Every invited creature can likewise enter, leave, and later return any number of times while the spell lasts.
While within the conclave, participants gain the following benefits:

items: They can see, hear, speak with, and physically interact with one another's projections normally.
Every participant understands the literal meaning of any language spoken by another participant.
A participant can manifest accurate representations of books, maps, diagrams, written records, tools, and other objects currently in its possession.
Participants can examine, read, copy, discuss, and work with those representations as though the original objects were physically present.
Participants can cooperate on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma ability checks and can take the Help action for one another regardless of the distance between their physical bodies.

Anything written, drawn, designed, calculated, translated, or otherwise recorded within the conclave can be reproduced perfectly onto suitable physical materials possessed by any participant when that participant leaves.

A participant can voluntarily share one of its memories. The memory manifests throughout the chamber as a sensory reconstruction that the participants can pause, replay, accelerate, slow, or examine from different viewpoints.
A participant retains complete memory of everything it personally experienced within the conclave.

entries: A participant can maintain Concentration on a spell that was already active before entering the conclave. Entering or leaving the conclave doesn't by itself interrupt Concentration.

A spell, attack, condition, or other harmful effect created within the conclave can't affect a participant's physical body, and participants can't use the conclave to directly cast spells upon or otherwise affect creatures, objects, or locations outside it.

If a participant becomes unconscious or dies, its projection disappears immediately. If it leaves the plane on which its body was located, its connection to the conclave ends until it again meets the requirements for entry.
You can revoke a creature's invitation at any time while you are within the conclave. Its projection immediately disappears, and it can't return unless you invite it again.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The duration becomes 24 hours, and you can invite up to 100 willing creatures. Invited creatures can enter the conclave from anywhere on the same plane regardless of whether you know their current location.
{@b 9th Level.} The duration becomes 30 days, there is no limit to the number of willing creatures you can invite, and invited creatures can enter from any plane of existence.

In addition, the conclave can transport physical matter. A participant can bring objects it is carrying into the conclave and give them to another participant, with a total weight of up to 1,000 pounds per transfer. When the recipient leaves, those objects appear with it.

A willing participant can also choose another participant when leaving the conclave. Instead of returning to its original location, its physical body appears in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of that creature's physical body, provided both creatures are on a plane that permits planar travel.

spell.name: Living Archive

m.text: a blank master volume bound in fine materials worth at least 1,000 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: You awaken every written record around you into a single living body of knowledge.
When the casting is complete, the master volume becomes magically linked to every book, scroll, tablet, inscription, map, diagram, encoded document, and other readable record within 300 feet of you.
For the duration, you can use the master volume to access the linked collection without physically handling its individual contents.

You can ask the archive a question by speaking or writing it into the master volume. If the answer exists somewhere within the linked records, the volume immediately identifies the relevant sources and presents the information to you in a concise form.
The archive can:

items: search the entire linked collection simultaneously;
translate any written language contained within it;
reproduce text, illustrations, maps, tables, diagrams, and formulae exactly;
compare multiple records and identify where their contents agree, conflict, or differ;
reconstruct the intended reading order of damaged, scattered, or disorganized documents;
identify duplicate, altered, forged, missing, or magically modified portions of linked records;
create an index or catalogue of any subject you specify;
and copy any amount of linked information into blank books, parchment, or similar suitable materials you provide.

entries: The spell doesn't create knowledge that isn't present somewhere within the linked records. It also doesn't determine which conflicting source is objectively correct unless the collection itself contains enough information to establish that fact.

Magically encrypted or concealed information created by a spell of 7th level or lower can be read normally through the archive. Nonmagical codes, ciphers, and constructed languages are deciphered if sufficient examples exist within the linked collection to determine their meaning.

If a linked record is removed from the spell's area, information already indexed from it remains accessible for the rest of the duration, but the archive no longer receives changes made to that record.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The duration becomes 7 days, the radius becomes 1 mile, and the archive can link to written records contained inside extradimensional spaces whose entrances lie within the area.

{@b 9th Level.} The duration becomes 30 days. You can designate an entire contiguous settlement, fortress, university, library complex, or similar site no larger than 10 miles across as the linked archive, provided you cast the spell somewhere within it. Effects created by spells of 8th level or lower can't hide, encrypt, falsify, or prevent access to written information within the linked collection.

spell.name: Grand Reclamation

m.text: a flawless crystal prism worth at least 2,500 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: You call upon the lingering patterns of matter and magic, forcing everything you choose within range to remember what it once was.
When the casting is complete, choose any number of noncreature objects, structures, constructions, or portions of terrain within range that have been damaged, altered, ruined, or destroyed.
Each chosen target is restored simultaneously to the complete state it possessed at a point of your choice within the previous 100 years. You can choose a different point in history for each target.
The spell can restore, among other things:

items: weapons, armor, tools, and equipment;
books, documents, paintings, statues, and other works;
doors, walls, bridges, roads, ships, vehicles, and machinery;
buildings, towers, fortifications, and other structures;
damaged or excavated terrain;
and magic items whose physical forms have been damaged or destroyed.

entries: Missing pieces reform from surrounding inert matter, which is transformed as necessary. If insufficient ordinary matter is available, the spell creates the required nonvaluable material.
Each restored target regains its internal mechanisms, inscriptions, hidden compartments, structural details, and other physical features it possessed at the chosen point in its history.

If a chosen target is a magic item, its magical properties are restored as well unless its destruction specifically caused those properties to be permanently lost or required a unique method of destruction that this spell can't reverse.
You may freely exclude anything within the area. Only targets you choose are restored.
The spell can't restore a living creature, return a dead creature to life, restore a soul, or recreate something whose existence depended upon a living creature remaining alive.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} You can restore each chosen target to a state it possessed at any point within the previous 1,000 years, and the spell's range becomes 1,000 feet. You no longer need any identifiable fragment of a destroyed target if you cast the spell at a location where that target once existed.

{@b 9th Level.} You can restore each chosen target to any previous physical state it has ever possessed, regardless of how long ago it existed, and the spell's range becomes 5 miles. A chosen target that has been completely reduced to dust, scattered, melted, disintegrated, or otherwise physically erased can still be reconstructed if it once existed within range. An Artifact can be restored unless the method that destroyed it explicitly states that its destruction is permanent or prevents magical restoration.

spell.name: Architect's Mandate

m.text: a set of masterwork drafting instruments worth at least 2,500 gp, which aren't consumed

entries: You impose a design upon the physical world, compelling raw matter and existing construction to rearrange itself according to your intent.

When the casting is complete, choose any amount of nonliving, nonmagical matter within range. You can reshape, move, join, separate, excavate, compress, or reconstruct that material into any arrangement you can clearly envision.
The transformation can create or alter things such as:

items: buildings, walls, towers, bridges, roads, stairs, and fortifications;
tunnels, chambers, trenches, canals, wells, and underground complexes;
doors, windows, furniture, containers, scaffolding, and ordinary mechanisms;
ships, wagons, siege engines, and other nonmagical vehicles;
statues, monuments, signs, inscriptions, and architectural ornamentation;
or large-scale changes to stone, earth, wood, metal, glass, and similar material.

entries: The spell can work with many different materials simultaneously. You decide exactly which matter is affected and what form each portion takes.
The finished creation is real and permanent. It isn't magical after the transformation is complete and can't be dispelled.

You don't need to provide complete engineering plans. If you understand the intended purpose of a construction, the spell can supply ordinary structural details necessary for it to function safely, such as supports, joints, drainage, ventilation, stairs, hinges, and foundations.

The spell can't create matter from nothing, but it can freely redistribute available material within range. It can't create creatures, magic items, active magical effects, or substances whose total value would significantly exceed the materials consumed to create them.
Objects worn or carried by an unwilling creature aren't affected.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The range becomes 1 mile. You can also transform nonmagical material between different mundane substances of comparable value, such as turning stone into steel, wood into glass, or earth into worked stone.

{@b 9th Level.} The range becomes 5 miles, and you can reshape all nonliving matter you choose within range simultaneously, including complete landscapes and existing settlements. You can raise mountains, excavate vast underground complexes, redirect rivers, construct cities, or completely redesign existing terrain, provided sufficient matter exists within the affected area.
At 9th level, transformations between mundane materials no longer need to be of comparable value, though this spell still can't create magical substances, Artifacts, or unique supernatural materials.

spell.name: Living Bastion

m.text: a miniature architectural model or engraved boundary marker worth at least 2,500 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: You awaken a structure or territory, binding everything within its boundaries into a single obedient magical intelligence.

When you cast this spell, choose either one contiguous structure you touch or a contiguous area centered on the point you touch. The chosen structure or area can be no more than 300 feet across. For the duration, it becomes your Living Bastion.

If you choose an area rather than a structure, you determine its boundaries when you cast the spell. The area can include buildings, roads, courtyards, caves, gardens, tunnels, open ground, and similar spaces.

The bastion understands every language you know and follows your spoken or mentally issued instructions. It can communicate with creatures within itself through voices, writing appearing on surfaces, moving images, lights, sounds, or other manifestations appropriate to the area.

It perceives everything occurring within its boundaries and within 30 feet beyond them. Within that space, it can distinguish creatures you designate as allies, guests, residents, intruders, or any other category you define.

You decide which creatures or categories of creatures the bastion assists, ignores, restricts, or affects with each of its functions. You can grant or withhold access to individual services, mechanisms, routes, defenses, servant-like tasks, and other capabilities separately.

The bastion can manipulate its environment throughout its entire area. It can open, close, lock, and unlock doors; operate gates, lifts, machinery, tools, traps, siege equipment, plumbing, furnaces, lights, and other mechanisms; move furniture and unattended objects; arrange rooms; extinguish ordinary fires; clean, organize, prepare, carry, retrieve, serve, pour, repair, maintain, and perform other simple tasks.

In addition, any point within the bastion can act as though an {@spell Unseen Servant|XPHB} were present there. The bastion can perform any simple task an Unseen Servant could perform, including carrying objects, cleaning, mending, folding clothes, lighting fires, serving food, pouring drinks, opening containers, operating simple tools, or performing similar household and labor tasks.

The bastion can perform any number of such simple tasks simultaneously in different parts of itself. These manifestations are invisible magical forces rather than creatures and can't leave the bastion's boundaries.

It can manipulate unattended objects weighing up to 1,000 pounds with its greater environmental control. For delicate or ordinary servant-like tasks, its invisible forces have whatever fine control is reasonably necessary to perform the task.
The bastion can also automatically regulate lighting, temperature, ventilation, ordinary utilities, doors, access routes, and similar systems where the environment provides the necessary means.

If weapons, traps, defenses, or machinery already exist within the area, the bastion can operate them normally, but the spell doesn't create weapons, ammunition, magic items, or defensive systems that weren't already present.
The bastion remembers everything it perceives during the spell. You can mentally ask it about anything that occurred within its boundaries, and it can accurately recount what it witnessed.

At the start of each hour, the bastion repairs up to 100 Hit Points of damage to nonmagical objects, structures, roads, terrain works, mechanisms, and other constructions within itself. It uses available material within its boundaries or within 30 feet of them. It can't create valuable or magical materials through this repair.
Once created, the bastion continues to exist and obey your standing instructions even if you leave its area. You don't need to remain nearby or maintain Concentration.

For the entire duration of the spell, you retain control over its adjustable functions regardless of distance or planar boundaries. Whenever the spell allows you to choose permissions, designations, instructions, zones, settings, targets for its benefits, or similar ongoing options, you can change those choices at any time, requiring no action. This doesn't move or enlarge the spell's original area unless the spell says otherwise.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The duration becomes 30 days, the affected structure or area can be up to 1 mile across, its perception extends 300 feet beyond its boundaries, it can manipulate unattended objects weighing up to 10,000 pounds, and it repairs up to 500 Hit Points of damage each hour.
{@b 9th Level.} The spell becomes permanent until dispelled, and the affected structure or area can be up to 5 miles across.

At 9th level, the bastion can manipulate unattended objects of any weight that can physically move within its environment, repairs up to 1,000 Hit Points of damage each hour, and can reconstruct destroyed portions of ordinary nonmagical structures and terrain within itself even when suitable replacement material is unavailable.
It retains its memories indefinitely and can receive your mental commands across planar boundaries.

spell.name: Grand Waygate

m.text: two matching gate keys fashioned from precious metal worth at least 2,500 gp each, which aren't consumed

entries: You establish a stable passage through space, joining two distant locations as though they stood beside one another.

Choose an unoccupied space within range large enough to contain a 20-foot-wide, 20-foot-high portal. Then choose a destination on the same plane of existence that you have personally visited or can identify with exceptional precision.
A second portal appears at an unoccupied space you choose at that destination. The two portals are connected for the spell's duration.

A creature or object that passes completely through either portal immediately emerges from the other. Travel can occur in either direction, and there is no limit to the number of creatures or objects that can pass through.

The portals remain open continuously unless you choose to close them. While closed, they remain present but intangible and can be reopened by you at any time while the spell lasts. Opening or closing the portals requires no action.

You can designate any creatures, groups, symbols, passwords, or other conditions as Authorized when you cast the spell or at any time afterward. Only Authorized creatures can pass through the portals. An Unauthorized creature treats each portal as an immovable, impenetrable surface and can't bypass this restriction through teleportation, possession, transformation, or similar magic.

You can give different Authorized creatures or groups different permissions. You decide which direction they can travel, which objects they can bring through, and, if the gate has multiple destinations, which destinations they can use.

For the entire duration of the spell, you retain control over its adjustable functions regardless of distance or planar boundaries. Whenever the spell allows you to choose permissions, designations, instructions, zones, settings, targets for its benefits, or similar ongoing options, you can change those choices at any time, requiring no action. This doesn't move or enlarge the spell's original area unless the spell says otherwise.

Objects can pass through without a creature accompanying them. This allows the gate to transport carts, cargo, machinery, vehicles, livestock, and other material that physically fits through its opening.

The passage itself imposes no harmful environmental transition. Pressure, wind, water, smoke, fire, hazardous atmosphere, and similar environmental effects don't automatically flow through an unattended portal unless you allow them to do so.
If either portal's location becomes obstructed or unsafe, that end of the gate becomes inactive until a suitable space is available again.
Once created, Grand Waygate persists for its full duration even if you leave either location, and it requires no Concentration.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The duration becomes 7 days, each portal can be up to 50 feet wide and 50 feet high, and the two ends can be located on different planes of existence, provided you have personally visited both locations.

{@b 9th Level.} The duration becomes permanent until dispelled, each portal can be up to 100 feet wide and 100 feet high, and you can connect any two locations you can clearly identify, even if you have never personally visited them.

At 9th level, you can also create up to six linked portals as part of the same casting. Each portal can connect to any other portal in the network. When a creature enters one, it chooses its destination from among the other linked portals it is Authorized to use.

spell.name: Land of Plenty

m.text: a vessel containing fertile soil, pure water, and seeds worth at least 1,000 gp, which aren't consumed

entries: You awaken the productive potential of the land, causing a chosen territory to sustain life with supernatural abundance.
Choose a contiguous area centered on the point you touch and no more than 1 mile across. You can freely exclude portions of the area when you cast the spell.

You decide which creatures, plants, resources, and portions of the chosen land receive each beneficial effect of this spell. You can grant or withhold individual effects separately for each target, category, or portion of the area.

For the entire duration of the spell, you retain control over its adjustable functions regardless of distance or planar boundaries. Whenever the spell allows you to choose permissions, designations, instructions, zones, settings, targets for its benefits, or similar ongoing options, you can change those choices at any time, requiring no action. This doesn't move or enlarge the spell's original area unless the spell says otherwise.
For the duration, the chosen land gains the following effects:

items: Soil becomes fertile enough to support any nonmagical plant that could reasonably survive the local environment.
Existing nonmagical plants recover from disease, drought, ordinary damage, and nutrient deficiency.
Crops and other useful plants grow at ten times their normal rate.
Harvested plants regrow when their biology would normally allow them to do so.
Natural freshwater within the area is purified of ordinary poison, disease, salt, sewage, and nonmagical contamination.
Wells, springs, and other renewable water sources replenish at the fastest rate their surroundings can naturally sustain.
Ordinary plant diseases, crop pests, and destructive infestations can't establish themselves within the area unless you allow them.
Weather within the area becomes less destructive to agriculture. Ordinary drought, frost, excessive heat, hail, and flooding are moderated enough to prevent widespread crop failure.
Damaged nonmagical ecosystems gradually recover, with native plants spreading into suitable empty ground.

Creatures gathering food, lumber, fibers, herbs, or other renewable biological resources from the area can do so without permanently exhausting those resources, provided they don't deliberately destroy the source faster than the spell can restore it.

entries: The spell doesn't create finished goods, precious materials, creatures, or food from nothing. Instead, it greatly accelerates and stabilizes the natural processes that produce them.
You decide which plants, crops, and natural resources the spell encourages. Unwanted vegetation doesn't have to grow merely because the land is fertile.

If the area contains magically corrupted soil, water, or vegetation, effects created by spells of 6th level or lower are suppressed for the duration if they would prevent the land from functioning normally.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The affected area can be up to 10 miles across, the duration becomes 1 year, and crops and renewable plants grow at fifty times their normal rate. Magical corruption created by spells of 7th level or lower is suppressed.
{@b 9th Level.} The affected area can be up to 50 miles across, and the spell becomes permanent until dispelled.

At 9th level, the land can gradually restore severely damaged nonmagical ecosystems, depleted soil, dried natural waterways, deforested regions, and other environmental devastation so long as the necessary matter and fundamental environmental conditions still exist. Renewable biological resources within the area replenish at the fastest rate the ecosystem can support without collapsing.
Magical corruption created by spells of 8th level or lower can't prevent this restoration.

spell.name: Eternal Preservation

m.text: a crystal hourglass filled with powdered diamond worth at least 2,500 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: You impose perfect preservation upon a chosen place, preventing time, decay, and ordinary deterioration from claiming anything you choose within it.

Choose a contiguous area centered on the point you touch and no more than 300 feet across. When you cast the spell, you can designate any creatures, objects, substances, structures, corpses, plants, food, documents, or other matter within the area as Preserved. You can also designate categories, such as "all food," "all books," or "everything except living creatures."

You decide which eligible targets receive each benefit of this spell. You can grant or withhold preservation and other beneficial effects separately for each creature, object, substance, structure, category, or portion of the area. Perfect Stasis still follows its own saving throw rules for unwilling creatures.

For the entire duration of the spell, you retain control over its adjustable functions regardless of distance or planar boundaries. Whenever the spell allows you to choose permissions, designations, instructions, zones, settings, targets for its benefits, or similar ongoing options, you can change those choices at any time, requiring no action. This doesn't move or enlarge the spell's original area unless the spell says otherwise.
For the duration, Preserved targets remain physically unchanged by the passage of time.

They don't rot, spoil, corrode, rust, weather, decay, dry out, become stale, lose freshness, degrade from age, or suffer ordinary wear. Dead creatures don't decompose, harvested plants remain fresh, food remains as edible as when the spell was cast, and written or painted materials don't fade.

Living creatures you choose can also be preserved without being placed in suspended animation. Such creatures continue to move, act, eat, sleep, heal, and live normally, but don't physically age while within the area.

entries.name: Perfect Stasis
entries: You can place a willing creature or unattended object within the affected area into Perfect Stasis automatically.

An unwilling creature within the affected area can also be placed into Perfect Stasis. When you attempt to do so, the creature must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, it enters Perfect Stasis. On a successful save, it resists this attempt for 1 hour.

A creature placed into Perfect Stasis unwillingly repeats the Constitution saving throw at the end of each hour. On a success, the stasis ends for that creature, and it can't be placed into Perfect Stasis by this spell again for 1 hour.

While in Perfect Stasis, a creature is Incapacitated, can't move or take actions, doesn't age, breathe, hunger, thirst, heal, or expend biological resources, is immune to damage and conditions, and doesn't perceive the passage of time.
A willing creature can choose to end its own Perfect Stasis at the end of any hour.
You can end Perfect Stasis on any target at any time while you are on the same plane, requiring no action.

Preserved structures and objects can't be damaged by ordinary weather, erosion, pests, neglect, or similar environmental processes, though they can still be deliberately damaged by creatures, spells, hazards, and other immediate forces.
If a Preserved target leaves the affected area, preservation ends for that target until it returns. Any aging or deterioration prevented by the spell doesn't occur retroactively.
The spell remains for its full duration without Concentration.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The affected area can be up to 1 mile across, and the duration becomes 10 years. Preserved objects and structures also become immune to nonmagical corrosion, erosion, weathering, and environmental damage while within the area.
{@b 9th Level.} The affected area can be up to 10 miles across, and the spell becomes permanent until dispelled.

At 9th level, anything placed into Perfect Stasis can remain suspended indefinitely, even if you die or leave the plane. You can also designate portions of the affected area where all nonliving matter is automatically preserved, including anything brought into those areas later.
Effects created by spells of 8th level or lower can't magically age, decay, spoil, corrode, or otherwise accelerate the deterioration of a Preserved target.

spell.name: Grand Manufactorum

m.text: a masterwork tool set and a miniature forge worth at least 2,500 gp total, which aren't consumed

entries: You transform a chosen workshop, factory, warehouse, forge, or contiguous area into an autonomous center of production.

Choose a contiguous area centered on the point you touch and no more than 300 feet across. For the duration, invisible magical forces within the area can process raw materials and manufacture nonmagical objects according to your instructions.

You can describe an object verbally, provide a physical example, or supply plans, diagrams, or other instructions. The spell can then repeatedly manufacture that object for as long as suitable materials remain available.

The manufactorum can cut, shape, melt, forge, cast, weave, sew, grind, mix, assemble, polish, sharpen, bind, print, engrave, package, and perform any other ordinary manufacturing process necessary to complete its work.
It can create, among other things:

items: weapons, armor, ammunition, tools, and adventuring equipment;
furniture, clothing, containers, books, paper, and household goods;
mechanical components, locks, gears, pipes, fittings, and machinery;
carts, wagons, boats, siege equipment, and other nonmagical vehicles;
construction materials such as bricks, beams, panels, glass, nails, and worked stone;
food products and preserved goods from suitable ingredients;
and any other nonmagical object whose required materials are available.

entries: The spell can perform any number of manufacturing processes simultaneously throughout the affected area.

During each hour, it can finish products whose combined weight is up to 10,000 pounds. Particularly delicate or complex work doesn't reduce this limit; if the spell has sufficient instructions to understand the intended result, it can perform the required precision automatically.
The spell doesn't create raw material from nothing and can't manufacture creatures, souls, Artifacts, or active magical effects.

It can manufacture components for magic items and perform mundane portions of magic-item construction, but it can't provide unique supernatural ingredients or magical power that the finished item specifically requires.

For the entire duration of the spell, you retain control over its adjustable functions regardless of distance or planar boundaries. Whenever the spell allows you to choose permissions, designations, instructions, zones, settings, targets for its benefits, or similar ongoing options, you can change those choices at any time, requiring no action. This doesn't move or enlarge the spell's original area unless the spell says otherwise. Once given, production instructions continue until you change them or the spell ends.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The affected area can be up to 1 mile across, the duration becomes 30 days, and the manufactorum can complete up to 100,000 pounds of finished products each hour. It can also reproduce any nonmagical object you provide as a sample even if you don't understand how that object was originally made.

{@b 9th Level.} The affected area can be up to 5 miles across, and the spell becomes permanent until dispelled. There is no fixed hourly weight limit; the manufactorum works as quickly as available space, raw materials, and the physical movement of those materials reasonably allow.

At 9th level, if you provide a complete magic-item formula and every special material required by that formula, the manufactorum can also perform the full construction process for that magic item. It doesn't waive the required materials or create unique components, but no additional workforce is required.

spell.name: Arcane Reservoir

m.text: a flawless crystal vessel worth at least 5,000 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: You transform the material component into a stable reservoir capable of storing magical power for later use.

The reservoir remains fixed at the location where the spell is cast. For the duration, a willing creature touching it can deposit an unexpended spell slot into the reservoir. The slot is expended, and the reservoir gains a number of Arcane Charges determined by the slot's level, as shown in the Arcane Charge Cost table.
The reservoir can hold a maximum of 50 Arcane Charges at one time. If depositing a spell slot would exceed this maximum, the deposit fails and the spell slot isn't expended.
A creature touching the reservoir can spend Arcane Charges in either of the following ways:

items.name: Restore a Spell Slot.
items.entry: The creature restores one expended spell slot by spending the number of Arcane Charges shown for that slot's level in the Arcane Charge Cost table. The restored slot can be no higher than 5th level.

items.name: Fuel a Spell.
items.entry: When the creature casts a spell while touching the reservoir, it can spend the number of Arcane Charges shown for the spell slot's level instead of expending one of its own spell slots. At 7th level, this can fuel a spell using a slot of no higher than 5th level.

entries: A creature can draw from the reservoir only willingly, and you can designate creatures, groups, passwords, symbols, or other qualifications that determine who is Authorized to use it.

You can assign different permissions to different Authorized creatures or groups. You decide independently who can deposit spell slots, restore spell slots, fuel spells, and what maximum spell-slot level each creature or group is allowed to draw from the reservoir.

For the entire duration of the spell, you retain control over its adjustable functions regardless of distance or planar boundaries. Whenever the spell allows you to choose permissions, designations, instructions, zones, settings, targets for its benefits, or similar ongoing options, you can change those choices at any time, requiring no action. This doesn't move or enlarge the spell's original area unless the spell says otherwise.
The reservoir can receive and provide magical energy any number of times during its duration, provided it doesn't exceed its storage limit.
You always know how many Arcane Charges remain stored in the reservoir, regardless of distance or planar boundaries.
If the spell ends while Arcane Charges remain stored, those charges harmlessly dissipate.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The duration becomes 1 year, the reservoir can store up to 200 Arcane Charges, and it can restore or fuel spell slots of up to 7th level.
{@b 9th Level.} The spell becomes permanent until dispelled, the reservoir can store up to 1,000 Arcane Charges, and it can restore or fuel spell slots of up to 9th level.

At 9th level, you can create a network of up to ten Arcane Reservoirs cast by you. Reservoirs in the same network share their stored Arcane Charges regardless of distance, even across planar boundaries. A creature using one reservoir can draw Arcane Charges deposited into any other reservoir in the network.

spell.name: Grand Infirmary

m.text: a crystal medical sigil set with diamond and silver worth at least 2,500 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: You transform a structure or contiguous area into a supernatural place of healing, recovery, and tranquility, filling it with restorative magic and invisible attendants.

Choose a contiguous structure or area centered on the point you touch and no more than 300 feet across. When you cast the spell, you can designate creatures individually, by group, symbol, password, or any other clear qualification as Patients.
You decide which creatures receive each benefit of this spell. You can grant or withhold individual benefits separately for each creature or category of creatures.

For the entire duration of the spell, you retain control over its adjustable functions regardless of distance or planar boundaries. Whenever the spell allows you to choose permissions, designations, instructions, zones, settings, targets for its benefits, or similar ongoing options, you can change those choices at any time, requiring no action. This doesn't move or enlarge the spell's original area unless the spell says otherwise.

When a creature enters the infirmary, you can choose for it to be affected by {@spell Calm Emotions|XPHB} for as long as it remains within the area. No saving throw is required. While affected in this way, any Charmed or Frightened condition affecting the creature is suppressed, and the creature becomes indifferent toward creatures within the infirmary that it was hostile toward. This indifference ends toward a creature if that creature attacks it, damages it, forces it to make a saving throw, or visibly harms one of its allies. If a suppressed condition still has duration remaining when the creature leaves the infirmary, that condition resumes.
A Patient can receive any of the following benefits that you choose for it:

items: It is automatically Stabilized whenever it is Dying.
It has Advantage on Death Saving Throws.
If it has at least 1 Hit Point, it regains 10 Hit Points at the start of each hour.
Whenever it finishes a Short Rest, each Hit Point Die it spends restores the maximum possible number of Hit Points instead of being rolled.
Whenever it finishes a Short Rest, it also regains one expended Hit Point Die.
Ordinary diseases, infections, parasites, and nonmagical poisons can't worsen while it remains within the infirmary.
Nonmagical wounds don't become infected, reopen, or otherwise deteriorate.
Ordinary pain can be suppressed at the Patient's choice without preventing it from perceiving injuries or other bodily sensations necessary for its safety.

entries: Invisible restorative forces can act throughout the entire infirmary as trained medical attendants. They can clean and dress wounds, sterilize equipment, administer prepared medicine, move willing or unconscious Patients, prepare beds, provide food and water already available within the area, monitor breathing and other visible signs of health, and perform similar routine medical care. The infirmary can perform any number of these simple tasks simultaneously.
Once during each hour, each Patient can receive one of the following treatments of your choice:

items: regain {@dice 4d8} + your spellcasting ability modifier Hit Points;
end the Poisoned condition;
end one nonmagical disease, infection, or parasite;
restore one reduced Ability Score to its normal value, provided the reduction wasn't caused by an Artifact, Curse, or similarly exceptional effect;
or end one ordinary injury or impairment that could reasonably be corrected through nonmagical medical treatment.

entries: A Patient can receive only one such treatment during a given hour, but you can choose a different treatment for that Patient during a later hour.
The spell doesn't normally restore missing limbs or organs, remove Curses, or return the dead to life.
Once created, Grand Infirmary remains active for its full duration even if you leave the area. It requires no Concentration and continues providing treatment according to your existing instructions.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The affected structure or area can be up to 1 mile across, and the duration becomes 30 days. The hourly healing treatment becomes {@dice 8d8} + your spellcasting ability modifier Hit Points. In addition, an hourly treatment can end one of the following conditions: Blinded, Deafened, Paralyzed, or Petrified.
{@b 9th Level.} The affected structure or area can be up to 5 miles across, and the spell becomes permanent until dispelled.
At 9th level, the infirmary can also perform the following restorative procedures:

items: A missing limb or organ is completely regenerated after the creature spends 24 continuous hours as a Patient within the infirmary.
After 1 hour of treatment, the infirmary can end one Curse, magical disease, or other removable magical affliction created by a spell or effect of 8th level or lower.
An hourly treatment can restore a creature's Hit Point Maximum to its normal value.

A creature whose body is within the infirmary and that died there within the previous 1 minute is automatically returned to life with 1 Hit Point, provided its soul is able to return. The creature doesn't need to be willing.

entries: A creature restored to life by this spell can't benefit from that revival effect again until it finishes a Long Rest.

spell.name: Climate Dominion

m.text: a crystal globe containing samples of earth, water, and air worth at least 2,500 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: You bind the atmosphere of a territory to your design, establishing a stable climate that persists without your presence.
Choose a contiguous area centered on the point you touch and no more than 5 miles across. For the duration, you control the ordinary weather and climate throughout the area.
You can divide the affected area into any number of zones and determine the conditions of each zone independently.

For the entire duration of the spell, you retain control over its adjustable functions regardless of distance or planar boundaries. Whenever the spell allows you to choose permissions, designations, instructions, zones, settings, targets for its benefits, or similar ongoing options, you can change those choices at any time, requiring no action. This doesn't move or enlarge the spell's original area unless the spell says otherwise.

Within each zone, you can determine the temperature, cloud cover and sunlight, humidity, precipitation, fog and ordinary visibility, wind direction and strength up to a strong gale, the frequency and intensity of ordinary storms, and whether the area follows its natural season or another ordinary seasonal climate you choose.
Changes occur gradually over 10 minutes unless you choose for them to happen more slowly.

You can designate creatures, structures, roads, farmland, bodies of water, or other clearly defined portions of the area to be protected from particular effects. For example, you can cause heavy rain across a region while keeping roads dry, allow snow throughout a city while preventing accumulation on rooftops, or maintain cool conditions inside agricultural districts while the surrounding territory remains hot.

The spell can suppress ordinary droughts, heat waves, cold snaps, floods caused by rainfall, blizzards, dust storms, and other natural weather occurring within the affected area. It can also prevent new ordinary weather from entering the area if it conflicts with the climate you established.

The spell doesn't create magical lightning, supernatural storms, damaging energy, or other inherently magical weather. It also doesn't directly alter terrain, create water from nothing, or eliminate water that already exists, though precipitation and evaporation caused by the controlled climate function normally.
Climate Dominion continues for its full duration without Concentration, even if you leave the area or the plane.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The affected area can be up to 25 miles across, and the duration becomes 1 year. You can create severe natural weather, including hurricanes, tornadoes, extreme blizzards, torrential rain, prolonged drought, and similarly intense but nonmagical atmospheric conditions. You can still exclude any creatures, structures, routes, or zones you choose from individual effects.

{@b 9th Level.} The affected area can be up to 100 miles across, and the spell becomes permanent until dispelled. You can establish a completely stable artificial climate independent of the surrounding region's latitude, altitude, season, or natural weather patterns. Different parts of the area can permanently maintain entirely different climates, such as snow-covered mountains, temperate farmland, tropical gardens, and dry desert districts existing beside one another. Weather and climate effects created by spells of 8th level or lower can't alter a portion of the dominion unless you allow them to.

spell.name: Civic Nexus

m.text: a crystal relay core engraved with interconnected sigils worth at least 2,500 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: You weave an invisible network of thought, message, location, and warning through a territory, allowing its inhabitants to communicate and coordinate across great distances without conventional infrastructure.
Choose a contiguous area centered on the point you touch and no more than 5 miles across. The area becomes a Nexus for the duration.
You decide which creatures, groups, symbols, passwords, or other clear qualifications are Connected to the Nexus. You can determine separately which functions each creature or group can use.

For the entire duration of the spell, you retain control over its permissions, designations, channels, settings, and other adjustable functions regardless of distance or planar boundaries. You can change any of these choices at any time, requiring no action. This doesn't move or enlarge the spell's original area unless the spell says otherwise.
A Connected creature within the Nexus can use any of the following functions you allow:

items.name: Direct Communication.
items.entry: The creature can mentally communicate with another Connected creature within the Nexus as though speaking normally. The recipients can answer in the same way.

items.name: Group Channels.
items.entry: You can create any number of communication channels. A Connected creature can transmit a message to every creature currently authorized for a channel.

items.name: Location Sharing.
items.entry: A creature can choose to reveal its precise location within the Nexus to creatures or channels you permit. This function never reveals a creature's location against its will unless you specifically designate that creature as being subject to mandatory tracking when it first becomes Connected.

items.name: Emergency Signal.
items.entry: The creature can instantly transmit an alarm, its location, and a brief description of the danger to designated creatures or channels.

items.name: Sensory Message.
items.entry: The creature can transmit a still image, sound, short memory-like impression, map, written message, or similar simple information it can clearly perceive or recall.

items.name: Translation.
items.entry: Connected creatures understand the intended meaning of communications transmitted through the Nexus regardless of the languages they know.

items.name: Public Broadcast.
items.entry: Creatures you authorize can transmit announcements to any number of Connected creatures simultaneously.

entries: Communication through the Nexus is instantaneous within its area and requires no components, spell slots, or shared language.

You can establish automatic alerts based on clearly defined conditions within the Nexus, such as fire, structural collapse, entry into a restricted district, the activation of a designated alarm, or a Connected creature becoming Unconscious. When such a condition occurs, the Nexus immediately notifies the creatures or channels you chose.

The Nexus doesn't read thoughts that a creature doesn't intentionally transmit, and it doesn't reveal memories, identity, location, or other information except through functions you have specifically enabled.
Spells and magical effects of 6th level or lower can't intercept, alter, impersonate, or falsify communications transmitted through the Nexus unless you allow them to.
The spell requires no Concentration and continues functioning for its full duration even if you leave the area or the plane.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The affected area can be up to 25 miles across, and the duration becomes 1 year. Connected creatures can transmit continuous visual and auditory information through the Nexus, allowing another authorized creature to perceive what they currently see and hear. In addition, automatic alerts can respond to magical phenomena, including teleportation, planar travel, active spells, and designated magical signatures.

{@b 9th Level.} The affected area can be up to 100 miles across, and the spell becomes permanent until dispelled. You can link up to ten Civic Nexuses cast by you into a single network. Connected creatures can communicate between linked Nexuses regardless of distance and across planar boundaries. At 9th level, communication within the network can't be intercepted, altered, blocked, impersonated, or falsified by spells or magical effects of 8th level or lower unless you allow it.

spell.name: Sovereign Will
entries: You touch a creature and impose absolute authority over its own mind, body, and supernatural state. For the duration, hostile powers can affect the target only so far as it permits them to.
The spell requires no Concentration.
While the spell lasts, the target gains the following benefits:

items: It is immune to the Charmed and Frightened conditions.
It can't be possessed or have its thoughts, memories, emotions, alignment, personality, or form altered against its will.
It can't be magically compelled to speak, remain silent, move, take an action, or refrain from taking an action.
Its Speed can't be reduced against its will, and it can't be teleported, banished, or moved to another plane against its will.
It can't be magically put to sleep or rendered Unconscious while it has at least 1 Hit Point.
A creature can't control its body, actions, senses, or movement through magic.

entries: Whenever the target would fail a saving throw against a spell or magical effect, it can choose to succeed instead. It can use this benefit once during each of its turns, and using it requires no action.

entries.name: Reject the Effect
entries: Whenever a spell or magical effect would impose a condition on the target or create an ongoing effect affecting it, the target can immediately reject that effect after learning what it does.
The rejected effect ends on the target immediately, even if it would normally have a longer duration.
The target can do this even if the effect would normally prevent it from taking actions or reactions.
This ability doesn't end damage that has already been dealt, though it can end an ongoing effect that would deal additional damage later.

entries.name: Unbroken Concentration
entries: Whenever damage would cause the target to make a Constitution saving throw to maintain Concentration, it can choose to automatically succeed.
Other effects can still end its Concentration if they explicitly end the spell itself.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} Whenever the target rejects a spell or magical effect, it can also reflect that effect back upon its source if the source is a creature within 120 feet of the target. The originating creature becomes the target of the rejected effect instead, using the original caster's spell save DC and spellcasting ability where applicable.

{@b 9th Level.} For the duration, the target can choose to succeed on any saving throw it makes, not only saving throws against spells or magical effects. In addition, a spell or magical effect of 8th level or lower can't alter the target's mind, body, location, form, actions, or ongoing magical state unless the target chooses to allow it.

spell.name: Ruin Cascade
entries: You compress destructive arcane force into a point you can see within range, then allow the collapse to propagate through everything caught within it.

Each creature in a 30-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 12d12} Force damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.
Objects and structures damaged by the initial eruption or by a Secondary Rupture automatically take the maximum possible damage from that instance.

entries.name: Secondary Rupture
entries: Whenever a creature or object is reduced to 0 Hit Points or destroyed by this spell, it becomes the center of a Secondary Rupture.

Each creature within 15 feet of the rupture must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 6d12} Force damage, or half as much on a successful save. This damage is always equal to half the number of damage dice rolled by the spell's initial eruption.

A Secondary Rupture can reduce another creature or object to 0 Hit Points or destroy it and create another Secondary Rupture. There is no limit to the number of Secondary Ruptures that can occur from a single casting.
A creature can be damaged by multiple Secondary Ruptures from the same casting, but only once by each individual rupture.

entries.name: Overwhelming Collapse
entries: If a creature fails its saving throw against the initial eruption by 5 or more, it is also knocked Prone and pushed up to 30 feet directly away from the center of the spell.
If it fails that saving throw by 10 or more, it instead takes an additional {@damage 6d12} Force damage.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The initial damage becomes {@damage 18d12}. Each Secondary Rupture deals {@damage 9d12} Force damage, and its radius becomes 20 feet.

{@b 9th Level.} The initial damage becomes {@damage 30d12}. Each Secondary Rupture deals {@damage 15d12} Force damage in a 30-foot radius. Whenever a creature succeeds on a saving throw against this spell, it takes three-quarters of the damage instead of half.

spell.name: Final Rupture
entries: You focus destructive magic into a single point within a creature's body or form, then tear that point apart from the inside.

Choose one creature you can see within range. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 20d12} Force damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.
This damage ignores Resistance to Force damage. If the target is immune to Force damage, it instead has Resistance to this damage.

entries.name: Internal Collapse
entries: If the target fails the saving throw, the spell also ruptures its ability to recover until the end of your next turn:

items: it can't regain Hit Points;
Regeneration and similar traits don't restore Hit Points;
Temporary Hit Points can't be gained;
and any effect that would prevent it from dropping to 0 Hit Points or cause it to remain at 1 Hit Point instead is suppressed for this damage.

entries: If this spell reduces the target to 0 Hit Points, any Regeneration or feature that would automatically restore it to life or consciousness before the end of your next turn doesn't function.

entries.name: Catastrophic Failure
entries: If the target fails its saving throw by 5 or more, it takes an additional {@damage 6d12} Force damage.
If it fails by 10 or more, the additional damage becomes {@damage 12d12} instead.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The initial damage becomes {@damage 30d12} Force damage. Catastrophic Failure deals {@damage 10d12} on a failure by 5 or more, or {@damage 20d12} on a failure by 10 or more.

{@b 9th Level.} The initial damage becomes {@damage 50d12} Force damage. On a failed saving throw, the target's Immunity to Force damage is ignored entirely. Catastrophic Failure deals {@damage 15d12} on a failure by 5 or more, or {@damage 30d12} on a failure by 10 or more. In addition, if the 9th-level version reduces the target to 0 Hit Points, effects of 8th level or lower can't restore that creature to life until 24 hours have passed.

spell.name: Gravitic Implosion
entries: You collapse gravity around a point you can see within range, dragging everything nearby inward before crushing the gathered mass under impossible pressure.

Each creature in a 40-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 14d12} Force damage, is pulled up to 40 feet directly toward the center, and is knocked Prone. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and isn't pulled or knocked Prone.
Objects and structures in the area automatically fail this saving throw.

entries.name: Crushing Convergence
entries: After all creatures and objects have been pulled, every creature within 10 feet of the center suffers a second gravitational collapse.
Each such creature must make a Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 8d12} Force damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one.
For every other creature of Medium size or larger within 10 feet of the center, this secondary damage increases by {@damage 1d12}, to a maximum increase of {@damage 10d12}.

entries.name: Compression
entries: A creature that fails both saving throws is Restrained until the end of its next turn as gravitational pressure pins it in place.
A Huge or smaller unattended object caught within 10 feet of the center is crushed, folded, or compacted as appropriate. Structures take maximum damage from both instances of this spell.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The initial damage becomes {@damage 20d12}, the secondary collapse becomes {@damage 12d12}, and the sphere's radius becomes 60 feet. The maximum bonus damage from Crushing Convergence becomes {@damage 15d12}.

{@b 9th Level.} The initial damage becomes {@damage 32d12}, the secondary collapse becomes {@damage 20d12}, and the sphere's radius becomes 100 feet. There is no maximum to the bonus damage from Crushing Convergence; each additional Medium or larger creature pulled into the central 10 feet adds another {@damage 1d12} Force damage to the secondary collapse. A creature that fails both saving throws is Stunned until the end of its next turn instead of Restrained.

spell.name: Endless Thunderbolt
entries: You unleash a bolt of lightning so violently overcharged that its energy continues multiplying as it tears through its victims.

Choose one creature you can see within range. The target must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 14d12} Lightning damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.

entries.name: Explosive Current
entries: Whenever you roll a 9, 10, 11, or 12 on any d12 rolled for this spell's damage, roll one additional d12 and add it to the damage.

Each additional die can trigger Explosive Current again. There is no limit to the number of additional dice that can be generated this way. All additional dice generated this way are part of the same damage roll.

entries.name: Overkill Arc
entries: If a creature is reduced to 0 Hit Points by this spell, choose another creature you can see within 60 feet of that creature.

The spell immediately arcs to the new target. The new target is affected by Endless Thunderbolt as though you had cast the spell again using the same spell slot level as the original casting, except no spell slot, action, or components are required.

The new target makes a new Dexterity saving throw and takes the spell's full initial damage appropriate to that spell slot level. All other effects of this spell apply normally to the new target, including Explosive Current, Conductive Ruin, and Overkill Arc.
There is no limit to the number of times the spell can arc in this way. A creature can be targeted only once by the same original casting of this spell.

entries.name: Conductive Ruin
entries: If a target is wearing metal armor, composed primarily of metal, or standing in a substantial body of water, it has Disadvantage on its saving throw against this spell.
Objects and structures made primarily of metal automatically fail their saving throw and take maximum damage.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The initial damage becomes {@damage 20d12} Lightning damage, and Explosive Current triggers whenever a damage die rolls 8, 9, 10, 11, or 12.

{@b 9th Level.} The initial damage becomes {@damage 30d12} Lightning damage, and Explosive Current triggers whenever a damage die rolls 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, or 12. The spell ignores Resistance to Lightning damage. A creature immune to Lightning damage instead has Resistance to this spell.

spell.name: Hellstar
entries: You create a miniature star of violent magical fire at a point you can see within range. The star occupies a 5-foot-radius sphere and radiates annihilating heat through a 40-foot-radius sphere around itself.
The spell requires no Concentration. Once created, the Hellstar persists for the full duration unless you cause it to collapse early.
When the star appears, each creature in the affected area must make a Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 10d12} Fire damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one.
A creature that enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must make the saving throw again.

entries.name: Escalating Heat
entries: The star grows hotter every round. Each time the star deals damage after the round in which it was created, its damage increases by {@damage 2d12} for the remainder of the spell.

Thus, its damage progresses from {@damage 10d12} on the initial eruption to {@damage 12d12}, then {@damage 14d12}, then {@damage 16d12}, and so on. There is no maximum to this increase while the spell remains active.

entries.name: Stellar Collapse
entries: At any time while the spell lasts, you can cause the star to collapse. This requires no action.

Every creature within 60 feet of the star must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes Force damage equal to the star's current Fire damage dice. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.
For example, if Hellstar has reached {@damage 18d12} Fire damage, Stellar Collapse deals {@damage 18d12} Force damage.
After the collapse, the spell ends. If the spell reaches the end of its duration without being collapsed early, it undergoes Stellar Collapse automatically before ending.

entries.name: Event Horizon
entries: A creature within 20 feet of the star treats the area as Difficult Terrain.
Whenever a creature within that distance attempts to move farther away from the star, it must first succeed on a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, that movement costs twice as much movement.
The star itself can't be moved after it is created.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The initial damage becomes {@damage 14d12}, the affected area becomes a 60-foot-radius sphere, and Escalating Heat increases the damage by {@damage 3d12} each round.

{@b 9th Level.} The initial damage becomes {@damage 20d12}, the affected area becomes a 100-foot-radius sphere, and Escalating Heat increases the damage by {@damage 5d12} each round. The spell ignores Resistance to Fire damage, and creatures immune to Fire damage instead have Resistance to it. When the 9th-level star undergoes Stellar Collapse, the collapse deals twice the star's current number of damage dice as Force damage.

spell.name: Heavenfall
entries: You designate a point you can see within range and tear open the sky above it. A colossal mass of condensed radiance and arcane force begins descending toward that point.
The spell requires no Concentration.
The impact occurs at the start of your next turn. Until then, the point of impact is visibly marked by a column of light extending into the sky, and creatures can perceive the descending catastrophe.

entries.name: Heavenfall Impact
entries: When the spell strikes, every creature in a 60-foot-radius, 100-foot-high cylinder centered on the chosen point must make a Constitution saving throw.
On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 12d12} Radiant damage plus {@damage 12d12} Force damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.
Objects and structures automatically fail the saving throw and take maximum damage.
The impact leaves the affected ground shattered and turns it into Difficult Terrain until cleared or repaired.

entries.name: Epicenter
entries: Creatures within 20 feet of the center suffer the full force of the impact.
A creature in this area that fails its saving throw takes an additional {@damage 8d12} Force damage. If it succeeds, it still takes half of this additional damage.

entries.name: Shockwave
entries: After the impact, every creature within 120 feet of the center but outside the primary area must make a Strength saving throw.
On a failed save, it takes {@damage 6d12} Thunder damage, is pushed 60 feet directly away from the center, and is knocked Prone.
On a successful save, it takes half damage and isn't pushed or knocked Prone.

entries.name: Irrevocable Descent
entries: Once cast, the impact can't be canceled by you.
Moving away from the targeted point doesn't alter the destination.
If you become Incapacitated, Unconscious, leave the plane, or die before impact, Heavenfall still strikes normally.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The primary damage becomes {@damage 18d12} Radiant damage plus {@damage 18d12} Force damage, the Epicenter bonus becomes {@damage 12d12} Force damage, and the primary radius becomes 90 feet.

{@b 9th Level.} The primary damage becomes {@damage 30d12} Radiant damage plus {@damage 30d12} Force damage, the Epicenter bonus becomes {@damage 20d12} Force damage, and the primary radius becomes 150 feet. A creature in the Epicenter that fails its saving throw is also Stunned until the end of its next turn. Damage dealt by this version of the spell ignores Resistance to Radiant, Force, and Thunder damage. Immunity to any of those damage types instead functions as Resistance against this spell.

spell.name: Annihilation Beam
entries: You tear open a channel of raw destructive power and sustain it around yourself, allowing you to repeatedly discharge beams capable of stripping matter apart.
The spell requires no Concentration.

When you cast the spell, and once on each of your turns thereafter for the duration, you can fire a beam at one creature or object you can see within range. Firing a beam after the initial casting requires no action.
The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 10d12} Force damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.
Objects and structures automatically fail this saving throw and take maximum damage.

entries.name: Annihilation Mark
entries: Whenever a creature fails its saving throw against the beam, it gains one Annihilation Mark until the spell ends.
For each Annihilation Mark already on the target, the beam deals an additional {@damage 3d12} Force damage to it.
For example, the first hit deals {@damage 10d12}, the second {@damage 13d12}, the third {@damage 16d12}, the fourth {@damage 19d12}, and the fifth {@damage 22d12}.
There is no maximum number of Annihilation Marks a creature can accumulate. A successful saving throw doesn't remove existing marks.

entries.name: Matter Breakdown
entries: A creature that has at least 3 Annihilation Marks loses Resistance to Force damage against this spell.
At 5 Marks, Immunity to Force damage instead functions as Resistance against this spell.
At 7 Marks, this spell ignores both Resistance and Immunity to Force damage against that creature.

In addition, damage from the beam ignores Temporary Hit Points once the target has at least 5 Marks. The Temporary Hit Points aren't removed; the beam simply deals its damage directly to the creature's Hit Points.

entries.name: Terminal Discharge
entries: At any time while the spell lasts, you can end the spell and unleash all remaining destructive energy into one final beam. This requires no action.
Choose one creature or object within range. It makes the normal Constitution saving throw.
The beam deals {@damage 20d12} Force damage plus {@damage 5d12} for each Annihilation Mark on the target. Afterward, the spell ends.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} Each normal beam deals {@damage 15d12} Force damage, and each Annihilation Mark adds {@damage 5d12} instead of {@damage 3d12}. Terminal Discharge deals {@damage 30d12} Force damage plus {@damage 8d12} for each Annihilation Mark on the target.

{@b 9th Level.} Each normal beam deals {@damage 25d12} Force damage, and each Annihilation Mark adds {@damage 8d12}. Terminal Discharge deals {@damage 50d12} Force damage plus {@damage 12d12} for each Annihilation Mark on the target. You can fire two normal beams on each of your turns, choosing the same or different targets. Each beam resolves separately and can add its own Annihilation Mark.

spell.name: Ruinous Verdict
entries: You pronounce a supernatural sentence upon one creature you can see within range, binding its own actions to its destruction.

The target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 14d12} Psychic damage and becomes Condemned for the duration. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and the spell ends.
The spell requires no Concentration.

entries.name: Price of Action
entries: Each time the target does any of the following, it immediately takes {@damage 4d12} Psychic damage:

items: takes an Action;
takes a Bonus Action;
takes a Reaction;
casts a spell;
or willingly moves 10 feet or more during a turn.

entries: Each trigger is counted separately. For example, if the target moves 20 feet, casts a spell using its Action, and then uses a Bonus Action, it takes the damage three times.
A single activity can't trigger the same category more than once, but different categories can all trigger during the same turn.

entries.name: Defiance
entries: Whenever the target succeeds on a saving throw against one of your spells or magical effects while Condemned, it takes {@damage 6d12} Psychic damage.
Whenever it causes you to take damage, it takes Psychic damage equal to half the damage you actually took from that instance.
This retaliatory damage can't itself trigger another instance of Defiance.

entries.name: Final Sentence
entries: If damage from Ruinous Verdict reduces the target to 50 Hit Points or fewer, you can immediately invoke the Final Sentence, requiring no action.
The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 20d12} Psychic damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.
You can invoke Final Sentence only once per casting.
If Final Sentence reduces the target to 0 Hit Points, the target can't regain Hit Points until the start of your next turn.

spell.name: Absolute Zero
entries: You force a region toward an impossible thermal minimum, freezing matter, motion, and life with supernatural cold.
Choose a point you can see within range. A 60-foot-radius sphere centered on that point becomes a zone of absolute cold for the duration.
The spell requires no Concentration.

When the zone appears, each creature within it must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 18d12} Cold damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.
Objects and structures in the area take maximum damage from the spell.
A creature that enters the zone for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must make the saving throw again.

entries.name: Thermal Collapse
entries: Whenever a creature fails its saving throw against this spell, its Speed becomes 0 until the start of its next turn, it can't take Reactions during that time, and it gains one Frost Mark until the spell ends.
For each Frost Mark already on a creature, Absolute Zero deals an additional {@damage 4d12} Cold damage to it.
There is no maximum number of Frost Marks a creature can accumulate.

entries.name: Frozen Solid
entries: If a creature has 3 or more Frost Marks and fails another saving throw against this spell, it becomes encased in supernatural ice.
While encased, the creature is Restrained and has Total Cover against effects originating outside the ice. The ice has AC 15 and 50 Hit Points.
Damage dealt to the ice doesn't damage the creature inside it. If the ice is destroyed, the creature is freed.
If a creature inside the ice fails another saving throw against Absolute Zero, the Cold damage from that instance ignores Resistance to Cold damage.
At 5 Frost Marks, Immunity to Cold damage instead functions as Resistance against this spell.

entries.name: Shatter
entries: At any time while the spell lasts, you can cause every creature currently encased in ice by this spell to shatter violently. This requires no action.
Each such creature takes {@damage 12d12} Force damage, and its ice is destroyed.
For each Frost Mark on that creature beyond the third, this damage increases by {@damage 3d12}.
A creature makes no saving throw against this damage.
Using Shatter doesn't end Absolute Zero.

entries.name: Using a 9th-Level Spell Slot
entries: The zone's radius becomes 100 feet, and its initial damage becomes {@damage 30d12} Cold damage.
Each Frost Mark increases subsequent damage by {@damage 8d12} instead of {@damage 4d12}.
Shatter deals {@damage 20d12} Force damage plus {@damage 5d12} for each Frost Mark beyond the third.
In addition, Absolute Zero ignores Resistance to Cold damage entirely, and Cold Immunity instead functions as Resistance against the spell.

spell.name: Soulburn
entries: You ignite the vital essence of one creature you can see within range, burning through flesh, spirit, and the creature's capacity to sustain itself.

The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 24d12} Radiant or Necrotic damage (your choice when you cast the spell). On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.

entries.name: Burn the Soul
entries: On a failed save, the target's Hit Point Maximum is reduced by an amount equal to half the damage it actually takes from this spell.
On a successful save, its Hit Point Maximum is reduced by an amount equal to one-quarter of the damage it actually takes instead.
This reduction lasts until the creature finishes a Long Rest.
If this reduction lowers the creature's Hit Point Maximum to 0, it dies.

entries.name: Inextinguishable Wound
entries: Until the start of your next turn, the target can't regain Hit Points, can't gain Temporary Hit Points, and Regeneration and similar effects don't restore Hit Points.
During that time, an effect that would restore the target to Hit Points after it is reduced to 0 doesn't function.

entries.name: Soulfire
entries: This spell ignores Resistance to the chosen damage type.
