Examples include: "Never reveal what happened in this chamber," "Protect this bloodline for as long as you exist," "Whenever this city is attacked, defend its people," "You will never willingly harm me or my companions," "When you find the man bearing this symbol, bring him before me," "Guard this door and permit entry only to those carrying my seal," or "If I die, deliver this letter to my successor."

entries.name: Willing Subjects
entries: Permanent.
A willing creature automatically accepts the decree.
No Saving Throw is required.

entries.name: Unwilling Subjects
entries: Permanent on a failed save.
An unwilling creature makes a Wisdom Saving Throw against your Spell Save DC.
On a failed save, the decree takes hold permanently.
On a successful save, the decree fails to take hold.
A creature that successfully saves against a particular decree can't be targeted by that same decree again until you finish a Long Rest.
Once the decree takes hold, the creature receives no further Saving Throws merely because time passes.

entries.name: Bound in Body and Soul
entries: While the decree exists.
An Imperishable Decree binds the creature's body, mind, will, and soul simultaneously.
The creature can't willingly or unwillingly perform an action that directly violates the decree.

This remains true even if the creature is affected by another effect that would normally control or replace its actions, including being Charmed or Dominated, possession, magical or psionic mind control, direct control of its body, forced movement or forced actions, memory alteration, personality or alignment alteration, control or manipulation of its soul, another creature choosing its actions, transformation into another form, or unconscious or altered states in which another effect attempts to direct its behavior.
If another effect attempts to force the creature to violate your decree, the conflicting portion of that effect fails.

For example, if your decree states "Never harm me" and another creature completely controls the Subject and commands it to attack you, the Subject can't make that attack. The controller may command it to perform other actions that don't violate the decree.
An Imperishable Decree therefore takes precedence over other forms of control whenever their instructions conflict.

entries.name: The Body Obeys
entries: While the decree exists.
If fulfilling the decree requires the creature to act, its body must cooperate with the decree even if its conscious mind resists.
It must use its movement, Actions, Bonus Actions, Reactions, speech, possessions, spells, features, and other available capabilities as reasonably necessary to obey.

A creature can't deliberately paralyze itself, surrender control of its body, render itself unconscious, alter its own memories, transform itself, or place itself under another creature's control for the purpose of escaping or violating the decree.

entries.name: The Soul Remembers
entries: While the decree exists.
The decree is attached to the creature's identity and soul, not merely its current body.
Changing bodies, possessing another body, transforming, being reincarnated, being resurrected, or otherwise continuing existence in another physical form doesn't remove the decree.
If the creature temporarily ceases to possess a usable body, the decree remains dormant rather than ending and resumes functioning when the creature can act again.

entries.name: Bound to the Word
entries: While the decree remains active.
The creature is compelled to act according to the decree's wording.
If the decree prohibits something, the creature simply can't violate that prohibition.

If obedience is temporarily impossible, the creature isn't required to accomplish the impossible. The decree remains active and resumes compelling obedience as soon as compliance becomes possible again.

entries.name: Conditional Decrees
entries: Its activation is defined when the decree is created.
Permanent until triggered and completed, unless written to repeat.
A decree can remain dormant until a condition you specify occurs.
For example: "If anyone opens this vault without my permission, sound the alarm and attack them."
You can also create a recurring decree.
For example: "Whenever the bells ring three times, return to this fortress."
A recurring decree continues to function whenever its condition occurs unless its wording states otherwise.

entries.name: The Crown Interprets
entries: While the decree exists.
A decree follows the meaning and intent you held when you created it, rather than merely its most technically convenient interpretation.
The creature can't escape through deliberate grammatical loopholes, technicalities, indirect actions, intermediaries, or intentional misinterpretation.
If circumstances make the wording ambiguous, the decree follows the interpretation that most closely reflects your original intent.

entries.name: Command From Afar
entries: Instantaneous modification.
If the affected creature is also one of your Subjects from Sovereign's Mark, you can modify an existing decree on that creature while both of you are on the same plane of existence.
You communicate the alteration through Speak Across Distance.
The creature receives no new Saving Throw if the alteration remains within the original purpose of the decree.
A fundamentally unrelated command counts as a new decree.

entries.name: Revoke the Law
entries: Instantaneous.
You can permanently end any Imperishable Decree you created, provided you and the affected creature are on the same plane of existence.

optionalfeature.name: Edict of the Unthinking
entries: The Crown doesn't require thought, language, life, or even a soul before it can demand obedience.
Steel, stone, earth, machines, relics, and monuments all possess forms capable of serving a purpose.
Where no will exists to answer your command, your authority becomes the will that moves the world.
Possession is merely another claim made beneath the Crown.
The weapon can hear you even while another hand grips its hilt.
When owner and Crown give conflicting orders, the object itself is forced to choose.
An object doesn't forget what it can do simply because its proper wielder is absent.
Bloodline, training, ritual, and attunement are permissions created for lesser hands.
The Crown asks only whether the power exists—and if it does, commands it to answer.
Attunement, curses, creators, and ancient bonds may all claim an object.
Such claims remain meaningful only until they contradict the Crown.
When two masters command the same thing, lesser authority is made to yield.
At last, the difference between an arsenal, a fortress, and a city becomes irrelevant.
Every silent thing within your domain is another body awaiting a command.
One declaration from the Crown can set an entire landscape into motion.
Sometimes countless servants are less useful than a single hand large enough to move a kingdom.
Weapons, machines, ruins, earth, stone, and every silent material nearby are summoned toward a single point.
What arrives as countless separate things rises again as one colossal body bearing the Crown.

entries.name: Authority Without a Mind
entries: Permanent.
Your features from Pact of the Crown can affect eligible targets even if they possess no mind, can't hear, can't understand language, aren't creatures, or were never alive.
Your Crown authority is imposed directly upon the target's physical form and supernatural essence, if it possesses one.
A genuinely mindless target automatically fails any mental Saving Throw required by one of your Crown features.
A target that possesses genuine independent will still makes its Saving Throws normally, even if it has extremely low Intelligence or can't communicate.

entries.name: Matter Answers the Crown
entries: Permanent.
Eligible targets aren't limited to manufactured objects.
You can command nonliving natural matter and discrete masses of material as though they were objects.
This includes earth, soil, sand, stone, gravel, clay, mud, minerals, ore, raw metal, crystal, ice, snow, bone, dead wood, rubble, ash, glass, and other nonliving natural or artificial matter.
The material doesn't need to have previously been considered an object.
A sufficiently large mass uses the Crown-Bound Object stat block appropriate to the Size of the mass being commanded.

entries.name: Animate the Unthinking
entries: When you command an eligible object or mass of material that normally can't move or act independently, you can animate it as a Crown-Bound Object.

Use the Crown-Bound Object stat block corresponding to its actual Size: {@creature Tiny Crown-Bound Object|FftForbiddenTome}, {@creature Small Crown-Bound Object|FftForbiddenTome}, {@creature Medium Crown-Bound Object|FftForbiddenTome}, {@creature Large Crown-Bound Object|FftForbiddenTome}, {@creature Huge Crown-Bound Object|FftForbiddenTome}, or {@creature Gargantuan Crown-Bound Object|FftForbiddenTome}.
There is no numerical maximum to the number of Crown-Bound Objects you can animate simultaneously.
There is no Size restriction.

Animating something doesn't transform it. A sword remains a sword, stone remains stone, a wagon remains a wagon, and a mass of earth remains earth. The Crown simply grants it movement, the ability to act, and the capacity to obey.

entries.name: The Object Remains Itself
entries: While animated.
Animation doesn't erase or replace the target's existing properties.

It retains any existing Armor Class, Hit Points, Ability Scores, Saving Throws, Skills, Speeds, Resistances, Immunities, Vulnerabilities, senses, attacks, damage dice, weapon properties, magical properties, traits, actions, special functions, and other existing statistics.
The Crown-Bound Object stat block provides statistics or capabilities that the target doesn't already possess.
If the original value is better or more appropriate, use the original value.

entries.name: Bound to the Crown
entries: While animated.
Crown-Bound Objects obey your commands absolutely.
They understand the meaning and intent of your instructions despite lacking normal intelligence.
This doesn't make them Sapient, give them personalities, or create independent desires.

Once given a command, an object continues carrying it out until the task is completed, you replace the command, compliance becomes permanently impossible, or the effect maintaining the animation ends.
No further Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction from you is required.

entries.name: Floating Servants
entries: While animated.
Every Crown-Bound Object gains the Fly Speed listed in its stat block and can Hover.

Its shape doesn't need to be capable of natural flight. Weapons can fly, armor can float, vehicles can hover, statues can rise into the air, and masses of earth or stone can suspend themselves above the ground.
This doesn't physically reshape the target.

entries.name: Initiative
entries: While animated.
Crown-Bound Objects take their turns immediately after yours.
If multiple Crown-Bound Objects act at that time, you determine their order.
They can use their movement, Action, Bonus Action if available, Reaction, native abilities, and Crown-Bound abilities without requiring you to spend any of your actions.

entries.name: Crown Strike
entries: The Crown-Bound Object uses its Action.
Instantaneous.
If a Crown-Bound Object doesn't use a native attack, it can make a Crown Strike.
Attack Roll: d20 + the object's appropriate Strength or Dexterity modifier + your Proficiency Bonus.
Damage: {@damage 1d4} + the same Strength or Dexterity modifier + your Proficiency Bonus.

The damage type is determined by the object's actual form, normally Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing, or another appropriate damage type provided by the object's actual magical or physical properties.
This formula applies to ordinary Crown-Bound Objects. Crownforged Titans use their own Titan Attack Formula instead.

entries.name: Native Attacks
entries: Use the native attack's action economy.
If an object already possesses an attack, it can use that attack instead of Crown Strike.
The native attack retains its normal damage dice, modifiers, Reach, Range, riders, magical properties, additional damage, special effects, and ammunition rules.
Animation never forces a superior native attack to become a Crown Strike.

entries.name: Purpose of Form
entries: While animated.
A Crown-Bound Form describes what the target's existing physical shape is already suited to do.
Choosing or possessing a Form doesn't transform the target.
Available Forms from the Crown-Bound Object stat blocks are Edged, Piercing, Crushing, Guardian, Grasping, and Projectile.
A target can qualify for multiple Forms simultaneously when its actual construction supports them.

entries.name: Independent Servants
entries: While animated.
Your Crown-Bound Objects can independently interpret and execute complex instructions.

They can attack, defend, guard, patrol, search, retrieve objects, carry creatures or cargo, operate mechanisms, use tools, open and close doors, operate machinery, repair, construct, dismantle, sort objects, reload weapons, perform delicate physical work, and perform repetitive labor.
They understand your intended result, so you don't need to describe every individual motion required to accomplish it.

entries.name: The Crown Has Hands
entries: While animated.
A Crown-Bound Object can manipulate itself and nearby objects with whatever precision is necessary to fulfill a command.
It doesn't require literal hands.
When it makes an Ability Check involving a Skill or Tool with which you are proficient, it can add your Proficiency Bonus.
If you have Expertise with that Skill or Tool, it can instead add twice your Proficiency Bonus.

entries.name: Eyes of the Crown
entries: Until you stop perceiving through the object.
You can perceive through any Crown-Bound Object you control.
You can freely switch between your own senses, one Crown-Bound Object, or another Crown-Bound Object. Switching requires no Action.
You can use the senses listed in its stat block and any additional senses or sensory functions belonging to the original target.
You remain aware of your own surroundings unless you deliberately choose to focus entirely through the object.

entries.name: One Crown, Many Bodies
entries: While animated.
Your Crown-Bound Objects can coordinate perfectly with one another.

They can synchronize attacks, surround targets, create formations, divide complicated work, pass materials between one another, operate machines together, synchronize movement, avoid accidentally obstructing each other, and cooperate without verbal communication.
They understand the intended actions of your other Crown-Bound Objects on the same plane of existence.

entries.name: Combined Strength
entries: While cooperating on the same task.
Any number of Crown-Bound Objects can combine their physical capacities when working toward the same goal.
Their capabilities can be combined when determining what they can collectively carry, lift, push, drag, support, restrain, hold in place, construct, or dismantle.

entries.name: Command the Function
entries: While animated.
A Crown-Bound Object can independently activate and use any function genuinely belonging to itself.

This can include Magic Item properties, built-in spells, charges, command-word effects, activated weapon properties, siege weapon functions, vehicles, mechanisms, traps, magical devices, technological systems, and other native activated functions.
The object can fulfill the role of its own wielder, wearer, rider, driver, or operator.
It can press its own controls, pull its own triggers, speak its own command words where necessary, aim itself, and operate itself.
Actual resources such as ammunition, charges, fuel, or consumable components are still spent normally.

entries.name: No Operator Required
entries: While animated.
A Crown-Bound Object doesn't need another creature to hold, wear, wield, ride, or operate it in order to use a function that belongs to itself.
This doesn't give the object functions it never possessed.

entries.name: Endless Labor
entries: While its command remains active.
Crown-Bound Objects don't suffer Exhaustion from ordinary physical labor.

They can continuously perform construction, excavation, repairs, transportation, manufacturing, harvesting, fortification, demolition, maintenance, loading and unloading, cleaning, sorting, and similar labor.
They still require materials, fuel, tools, or other resources when those things are genuinely necessary.

entries.name: Coordinated Command
entries: You can issue the same command to any number of Crown-Bound Objects simultaneously.
There is no numerical limit to the number of objects that can receive that shared command.

entries.name: Command the Mindless
entries: You can use Assume Command against a mindless creature even if it can't hear or understand language.
A creature with no genuine independent will automatically fails its Saving Throw.
You can command its movement, Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, attacks, spells, supernatural abilities, target selection, object interactions, and other capabilities.
A creature possessing genuine independent will makes its Saving Throw normally.

entries.name: Decree Upon Matter
entries: Prerequisite: Imperishable Decree.
Use Imperishable Decree's action economy.
Permanent.
You can place an Imperishable Decree upon objects, natural matter, structures, mechanisms, Crown-Bound Objects, mindless creatures, and other eligible nonthinking targets.
A genuinely mindless target makes no Wisdom Saving Throw.
The decree binds the target's physical form and supernatural essence.
If fulfilling the decree requires an otherwise motionless target to act, it can automatically animate as a Crown-Bound Object whenever necessary.
When no action is required, the target can become motionless again without ending its permanent decree.

entries.name: Level 5: Awakened Instruments
entries: Permanent.
When you gain this Invocation, all of its base abilities become available.

Your Crown can animate objects and natural matter, grant them independent movement and action, allow them to use their own functions, coordinate them, perceive through them, and command mindless beings.

entries.name: Command the Possessed
entries: Your Crown features can target objects that are worn, wielded, carried, held, mounted, installed, operated, or otherwise actively possessed.
This includes weapons, armor, shields, Magic Items, Spellcasting Focuses, equipment, tools, containers, ammunition, and vehicles.
If your command directly opposes a creature's physical control over the object, that creature makes a Strength or Dexterity Saving Throw of its choice against your Spell Save DC.
On a failed save, the object obeys you.

entries.name: Rebellion of Property
entries: While the command remains active.
A commanded object can actively work against its possessor.
Weapons can pull away from attacks, armor can restrict its wearer, shields can expose their bearer, and vehicles can reject their drivers.
If the object can physically separate from its possessor, it can animate as a Crown-Bound Object and leave.

entries.name: Level 9: The Crown Uses All Things
Sovereign Activation
entries: Use the object's ability's action economy.
While animated or acting under your Crown authority.

A Crown-Bound Object can activate its own abilities even when they would normally require Attunement, a particular class, a particular species, a particular Ability Score, a command word, a wielder, a wearer, or another creature operating it.
The object counts as satisfying those requirements for the purpose of using its own abilities.
This doesn't make you personally attuned to the object.

entries.name: The Crown Supplies the Wielder
entries: While Sovereign Activation applies.
If an object's ability requires a wielder's Attack Bonus or Save DC but doesn't provide one itself, use the following values:
Attack Bonus = the object's appropriate Ability modifier + your Proficiency Bonus.
Save DC = 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + the object's appropriate Ability modifier.
If the object already has a superior fixed Attack Bonus or Save DC, it can use the superior value.

entries.name: Unerring Operation
entries: While under your Crown authority.
A Crown-Bound Object automatically understands how to operate its own functions.
You don't need to personally understand how the object works.
This doesn't automatically give that technical knowledge to you.

entries.name: Level 13: Ownership Is a Lesser Law
Override the Bond
entries: For the duration of the Crown command that established control.
Your authority can contest supernatural effects determining who controls an object, owns it, commands it, can activate it, can recall it, or is permitted to use it.

This includes Attunement bonds, magical ownership restrictions, creator-only controls, bonded weapons, summoned weapons, remote control, magical recall effects, curses governing an object's actions, controlled Constructs, and similar supernatural claims.

If another creature actively controls the object, make a contested check: you make a Charisma Check and add your Proficiency Bonus; the opposing controller uses the Ability modifier used by its controlling feature and adds its Proficiency Bonus, if any.
If no creature can reasonably make the opposing check, use 10 + the effect's spell level, or 10 + its creator's Proficiency Bonus if no spell level exists and that Proficiency Bonus is known.
On a success, your Crown takes precedence.

entries.name: The Object Chooses the Crown
entries: While Override the Bond remains active.

While you successfully override another bond, its former controller can't command it, recall effects can't remove it from your control, another creature can't activate it without your permission, and effects attempting to force it to violate your command fail.
The suppressed original bond isn't necessarily destroyed and can resume when your Crown control ends.

entries.name: Relics Must Kneel Too
entries: Permanent modification to Override the Bond.
Magic Items and Artifacts aren't automatically immune to this feature solely because of their rarity or power.
If an object possesses a genuine independent sentient will, that will can resist your Crown normally.

entries.name: Mass Edict
entries: Activating this feature requires an Action.
Up to 1 hour.
Choose a point you can perceive within 1 mile.
Choose any number of eligible objects, structures, or masses of nonliving matter within 1 mile of that point.
Every chosen target can immediately animate if necessary and receive a command from you.
There is no numerical limit and no Size limit. Tiny objects through Gargantuan structures or masses of material can all be affected.
You can freely exclude anything you don't wish to command.

entries.name: One Voice, Countless Bodies
entries: While Mass Edict lasts.
You can communicate commands to every affected target throughout the area regardless of ordinary hearing distance.
You can command all of them together, divide them into groups, assign different commands to different groups, command individual objects, or replace existing instructions.

entries.name: A Living Domain
entries: While Mass Edict lasts.
Affected objects can coordinate as one enormous workforce or army.
They can perform large-scale combat, construction, evacuation, repair, transportation, excavation, searching, fortification, manufacturing, infrastructure maintenance, and logistics.

entries.name: The Crown Does Not Tire
entries: While Mass Edict lasts.
Mass Edict requires no Concentration.
Becoming Incapacitated doesn't automatically end commands already issued, although you can't issue new commands while unable to act.

entries.name: Titan Convergence
entries: Activating this feature requires an Action.
Up to 1 hour.
Choose one point you can perceive within 1 mile.

Choose any number of eligible targets within 1 mile of that point, including Crown-Bound Objects, ordinary objects, weapons, armor, vehicles, machinery, siege equipment, magical objects, statues, corpses, mindless Constructs, structures, sections of structures, rubble, earth, soil, stone, sand, clay, minerals, ore, raw metal, crystal, ice, snow, bone, dead wood, and other eligible nonliving matter.
Command the selected material to converge on the chosen point.
Things incapable of moving automatically animate as necessary. Loose matter can rise, flow, fly, crawl, or otherwise travel toward the convergence point.
When sufficient material reaches the point, it forms one Crownforged Titan.
A single use of Titan Convergence creates one Titan.
The components don't need to share the same material, origin, purpose, Size, shape, or magical nature.

entries.name: Crownforged Titan
entries: For the remainder of Titan Convergence.

Choose whichever stat block is appropriate to the amount of material gathered: {@creature Huge Crownforged Titan|FftForbiddenTome} or {@creature Gargantuan Crownforged Titan|FftForbiddenTome}. Both are CR 24.
The Titan uses its dedicated Crownforged Titan stat block and obeys your Crown absolutely.

entries.name: The Whole Remembers Its Parts
entries: While the Crownforged Titan exists.
Components incorporated into the Titan retain usable functions when those functions can still reasonably operate.

Weapons remain weapons, siege equipment can still fire, Magic Items can retain appropriate abilities, engines and machinery can still function, chains can restrain, armor can reinforce the Titan, and natural matter contributes physical mass and structure.
Consumable resources such as charges, ammunition, or fuel remain consumable normally.

entries.name: Titan Attack Authority
entries: Instantaneous for each attack.
This formula applies only to Crownforged Titans, not ordinary Crown-Bound Objects.
The Titan's Attack Bonus equals the Titan's relevant Ability modifier + the Titan's Proficiency Bonus + your Proficiency Bonus.
Its damage equals the attack's damage dice + the Titan's relevant Ability modifier + the Titan's Proficiency Bonus + your Proficiency Bonus.
Its abilities use the Save DC specified by the Titan stat block: 20 + your Proficiency Bonus.

entries.name: When Titan Convergence Ends
entries: Instantaneous when triggered.
When the 1-hour duration ends, or when you voluntarily command the Titan to separate, its surviving components detach.
Objects and materials return to being separate things.
Anything still maintained by another Crown feature can immediately resume functioning under that effect.
Damage actually suffered during the Titan's existence can leave individual components damaged, broken, scattered, or destroyed as appropriate.

optionalfeature.name: Relic Assimilation
entries: The Arsenal does not merely preserve enchanted weapons. It learns them.
Every relic placed within it becomes another principle of violence written into the whole armory.
A single legendary edge can teach a thousand lesser weapons how to bite.

entries.name: Arsenal Relics
entries: When you finish a Long Rest, choose a number of eligible Magic Items stored within your Arsenal up to your Proficiency Bonus. The chosen items become your Arsenal Relics until you choose again when you finish a Long Rest.
An eligible item must be a weapon, ammunition, or a Magic Item whose magical properties directly modify a weapon or weapon attack.

entries.name: Total Assimilation
entries: While you wield or make an attack with any weapon from your Arsenal, that weapon can use every applicable magical property of all your Arsenal Relics simultaneously.
For those properties, the Arsenal weapon counts as each Arsenal Relic whenever a property refers to "this weapon," "the weapon," or otherwise requires the effect to originate from that relic.

entries.name: Relic Without Form
entries: A copied property isn't restricted by the Arsenal Relic's original weapon type, ammunition type, damage type, reach, or range unless the property would be impossible to resolve without that requirement.
If a property requires a melee attack, ranged attack, thrown attack, Critical Hit, specific target, or another condition created by the attack itself, you must still satisfy that condition.

entries.name: Convergent Enchantments
entries: Properties from different Arsenal Relics can function on the same attack and their benefits are cumulative, including bonuses to attack rolls, damage rolls, additional damage, Critical Hit effects, and other effects triggered by an attack.
A property with the same name from multiple Arsenal Relics doesn't stack with itself unless it explicitly says otherwise.

entries.name: Shared Activation
entries: If an Arsenal Relic has a property you can activate while holding, wielding, attacking with, or otherwise using that item, you can activate it through any weapon from your Arsenal as though you were using the Arsenal Relic.
If the property creates an effect from the relic, you can have that effect originate from the Arsenal weapon you're currently using.

entries.name: One Relic, One Resource
entries: The Arsenal shares power, not resources. Charges, limited uses, Recharge, once-per-turn limits, once-per-round limits, and other usage limits remain tied to the original Arsenal Relic.
Using that property through any Arsenal weapon expends or counts against the original Arsenal Relic's resource normally.

entries.name: Bound Requirements
entries: You must still satisfy an Arsenal Relic's Attunement requirement and any requirement based on the wielder, such as class, creature type, alignment, ability score, or another quality of the wielder.
Once you satisfy those requirements, every weapon in your Arsenal is treated as satisfying that item's weapon-specific requirements for the copied property.

entries.name: Transcendent Attunement
entries: As your bond with the Arsenal deepens, the Arsenal learns to sustain relics in your place.
At 7th level, one of your Arsenal Relics can function through this Invocation even if you are not Attuned to it.
At 11th level, up to two of your Arsenal Relics can ignore their Attunement requirements this way.
At 15th level, up to three of your Arsenal Relics can ignore their Attunement requirements this way.
At 17th level, all of your Arsenal Relics can function through this Invocation without requiring Attunement.

Ignoring Attunement this way applies only while the item is one of your Arsenal Relics and only to properties used through Relic Assimilation. It doesn't make you Attuned to the item, grant its normal benefits outside the Arsenal, or increase your number of Attunement slots.

entries.name: Relic Remains Whole
entries: An Arsenal Relic isn't consumed, destroyed, stripped of its magic, or permanently altered by this Invocation.
It remains a normal Magic Item and can still be summoned and used directly.

optionalfeature.name: Arsenal Instinct
entries: The Arsenal watches every clash.
It learns what fails, what pierces, and what kind of weapon the next moment demands.
Before long, you no longer choose the right weapon—the Arsenal does.

entries.name: Predatory Selection
entries: Whenever you miss a creature with a weapon from your Arsenal, or the creature reduces the damage of that attack through Resistance or Immunity, you can immediately return that weapon to the Arsenal and summon another stored weapon into the same hand. The replacement requires no action.
Until the end of your turn, your first attack against that creature with the replacement weapon has Advantage.

entries.name: Learned Weakness
entries: Once you damage a creature with a weapon from your Arsenal, the Arsenal remembers that creature until the end of your next Long Rest.
For a remembered creature, the Arsenal learns how that creature responds to damage dealt by your Arsenal, including any Resistance, Immunity, or Vulnerability revealed by those attacks.

entries.name: Adaptive Armament
entries: Whenever you make a weapon attack against a remembered creature using a weapon from your Arsenal, the Arsenal can alter that attack's damage type to the most effective damage type against that creature.
If the creature has one or more Vulnerabilities, the attack becomes a damage type to which it is Vulnerable.
If it has no Vulnerabilities, the Arsenal instead chooses a damage type that the creature neither Resists nor is Immune to, if one is available.
You don't need to know what damage type was chosen beforehand. The Arsenal determines the most effective option automatically when the attack hits.
The available damage types are Acid, Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire, Force, Lightning, Necrotic, Piercing, Poison, Psychic, Radiant, Slashing, and Thunder.

entries.name: Perfect Answer
entries: Starting at 11th level, attacks altered by Adaptive Armament also ignore Resistance to the chosen damage type.
Starting at 17th level, if the creature has no Vulnerability, the chosen damage type treats the creature as though it had Vulnerability to that damage for that attack.

optionalfeature.name: Adaptive Arsenal
entries: No weapon leaves the Arsenal unchanged.
Each one is refined for the exact moment it is called.
What you draw is not merely a stored weapon, but the version of it the battle demands.

entries.name: Mutable Armament
entries: Whenever you summon a weapon from your Arsenal, choose one of the following properties: Finesse, Light, Thrown (20/60), Reach, or Versatile (1d10). The weapon gains the chosen property until it returns to the Arsenal.
If the weapon already has the chosen property, choose another.

entries.name: Greater Adaptation
entries: Starting at 7th level, choose two properties whenever you summon the weapon.
Starting at 13th level, choose three properties whenever you summon the weapon.

entries.name: Perfect Form
entries: Starting at 17th level, when you summon a weapon, you can also change its normal weapon damage die to 1d12 if it would normally be lower.
If the weapon normally rolls multiple weapon damage dice, you can instead change each of those dice to 1d8.

entries.name: Arsenal Mastery
entries: Whenever you summon a weapon from your Arsenal, you can choose which Weapon Mastery property you use with that weapon from among any Weapon Mastery properties you know.
You can choose again each time the weapon is summoned.

optionalfeature.name: Echoed Form
entries: The Mirror studies not what you are, but how you act.
A spell, a strike, a dash, a gesture—each leaves behind a perfect pattern.
For a moment, that pattern can be called upon again.

entries.name: Reflected Action
entries: Once on each of your turns after you take an Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction, the Mirror records the form of that action until the start of your next turn.
Before the reflection fades, you can use it once to repeat the same type of action without using its normal action cost.
The repeated action must be one you could currently perform and must obey all of its normal requirements.

entries.name: Shared Expenditure
entries: Repeating an action this way doesn't duplicate resources.
If the repeated action would expend a spell slot, class resource, item charge, limited-use feature, ammunition, Hit Die, or another expendable resource, you must expend that resource again normally.

entries.name: Mirrored Execution
entries: The repeated action doesn't need to target the same creature, point, or object.
If it includes an attack, spell, movement, Grapple, Shove, item interaction, or another effect, you can choose new legal targets and resolve it normally.

entries.name: Perfect Echo
entries: Starting at 11th level, you can maintain two different recorded actions at once.

Starting at 17th level, once on each of your turns, the first reflected action you repeat doesn't expend a limited-use class or subclass resource, though it still requires spell slots, item charges, ammunition, or other external resources normally.

monster.name: Crown-Bound Object

ac.special: 15 or the object's original AC, whichever is higher or more appropriate

hp.special: 5 + three times your level, or the object's original Hit Points if higher or more appropriate

languages: understands your commands but can't speak unless its physical form permits it

trait.name: Animated Object
entries: {@b Original Object.} Animation doesn't reshape the object. It retains its original physical form, material, Armor Class, Hit Points, ability scores, saving throws, skills, movement speeds, resistances, immunities, vulnerabilities, senses, weapon properties, magical properties, traits, attacks, damage dice, special actions, and other existing abilities. If the original object has an Armor Class higher than 15, use the original Armor Class. Use the original Hit Points or other statistics when higher or more appropriate; this stat block supplies missing statistics without weakening superior native statistics.

{@b Object Nature.} The object doesn't need to breathe, eat, drink, or sleep. While animated, it counts as a Construct for effects that require a creature type, and it also remains an object for effects specifically concerning objects, structures, materials, weapons, armor, or similar things.

{@b Native Attacks.} The object can use a native attack instead of Crown Strike, retaining its normal damage dice, modifiers, range, reach, additional damage, magical properties, riders, and special effects. Use the Strength or Dexterity Crown Strike appropriate to its actual form; these are alternative rolls for the same attack. Retained superior ability scores still apply.

trait.name: Crowned Servant
entries: {@b Bound to the Crown.} The object obeys your commands absolutely, understands their meaning and intent despite lacking ordinary intelligence, and continues following them without further actions from you. It gains neither sapience nor an independent personality.

{@b Initiative.} The object takes its turn immediately after yours. If multiple Crown-Bound Objects act at the same time, you determine their order. The object doesn't require your Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction to take its turn or continue following an existing command.
{@b Floating Servant.} The object has a flying speed of 40 feet and can hover, regardless of its original shape. It can retain a faster appropriate original speed.

trait.name: Object Forms
entries: Forms reflect the object's existing shape and don't transform it. It can use multiple Forms if its construction supports them.

{@b Edged Form.} Crown Strike deals slashing damage when this Form is used. Once per turn when the object hits with an attack, it deals an extra {@damage PB} Slashing damage. When it scores a Critical Hit, roll one additional normal damage die of the attack.

{@b Piercing Form.} Crown Strike deals piercing damage when this Form is used. The object's melee reach increases by 5 feet while using a piercing portion of its form. Once per turn when it hits a creature no more than one size larger than itself, that creature can't willingly move farther away from the object until the start of the object's next turn.

{@b Crushing Form.} Crown Strike deals bludgeoning damage when this Form is used. Once per turn when the object hits a creature no more than one size larger than itself, choose one: push the creature 5 feet, knock it prone, or move it up to 5 feet to an unoccupied space within the object's reach.
{@b Guardian Form.} Crown Strike normally deals bludgeoning damage when this Form is used unless the object's actual form suggests otherwise.

{@b Grasping Form.} When the object hits a creature no more than one size larger than itself, it can immediately attempt to grapple the target as part of the same attack. The escape DC is {@dc 7 + PB} when using Strength or {@dc 12 + PB} when Dexterity better represents how the object binds the target. These use the object's listed ability scores; retained superior scores still apply. The object can continue attacking while maintaining the grapple if its physical form permits it.

{@b Projectile Form.} The object retains its actual range, ammunition requirements, weapon properties, damage, and magical properties. When making a native ranged attack, the object can use {@hit 4 + PB} as the attack bonus (use retained superior Dexterity if applicable) instead of its normal attack bonus. Being within 5 feet of a hostile creature doesn't impose disadvantage on its ranged attacks.

action.name: Crown Strike
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit -1 + PB} to hit, reach determined by the object's actual form, one target. {@h}{@damage 1d4 + -1 + PB} Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, as appropriate to the object's actual physical form. If another damage type is more appropriate because of its original magical or physical properties, use that type instead.

action.name: Crown Strike (Dexterity)
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 4 + PB} to hit, reach determined by the object's actual form, one target. {@h}{@damage 1d4 + 4 + PB} Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, as appropriate to the object's actual physical form. If another damage type is more appropriate because of its original magical or physical properties, use that type instead.

reaction.name: Interpose (Guardian Form Only)
entries: When another creature within the object's reach is hit by an attack, the object can move up to half its flying speed toward that creature without provoking opportunity attacks from the attacker and interpose itself. trait.name: Object Forms
entries: Forms reflect the object's existing shape and don't transform it. It can use multiple Forms if its construction supports them.

{@b Guardian Form.} Crown Strike normally deals bludgeoning damage when this Form is used unless the object's actual form suggests otherwise.

monster.name: Crownforged Titan

trait.name: Crown Authority
entries: {@b Absolute Servitor.} The Titan obeys your commands absolutely. It acts immediately after your turn and requires no Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction from you to continue carrying out an existing command. It understands the meaning and intent of your commands and can independently determine how to fulfill them. It doesn't become Sapient or develop an independent will.
{@b Titan Save DC.} Whenever a Crownforged Titan ability requires a Saving Throw, the save DC is {@dc 20 + PB} (20 + your Proficiency Bonus) unless that ability explicitly states otherwise.

{@b Titan Attack Formula.} This formula applies only to Crownforged Titans. Whenever the Titan makes an attack, its Attack Bonus equals the Titan's relevant Ability modifier + its Proficiency Bonus (+6) + your Proficiency Bonus. Its attack damage equals the attack's damage dice + the Titan's relevant Ability modifier + its Proficiency Bonus + your Proficiency Bonus. Use the ability relevant to the incorporated component's attack. The Titan Strike entries are alternative rolls for the same attack, not additional attacks. In War Titan Configuration, the Titan can replace one attack of its Multiattack with a Titan Strike.

This can include Magic Item properties, magical weapons, built-in spells, command-word abilities, siege weapons, firearms, launchers, engines, machinery, vehicles, armor, shields, chains, restraints, magical devices, technological systems, special materials, traps, and other functional components. The Titan can operate these components itself. Charges, ammunition, fuel, consumable components, and similar resources are still consumed normally.

trait.name: Sovereign Defenses
entries: {@b Sovereign Magic Immunity.} The Titan is immune to spells and magical effects unless you choose for that specific effect to affect it. This immunity doesn't interfere with your Crown features, the Titan's own abilities, magic belonging to incorporated components, or effects you voluntarily permit. If an effect would normally have a reduced effect on a successful Saving Throw, it instead has no effect on the Titan unless you allow it.

{@b Sovereign Adamantine Body.} The Titan is immune to all damage caused by nonmagical attacks, regardless of the damage type dealt by that attack. An attack must be magical or otherwise supernatural to bypass this immunity. After bypassing it, the Titan's other Damage Resistances and Damage Immunities still apply.

{@b Immutable Sovereign Form.} Unless you allow it, the Titan can't be transformed, polymorphed, petrified, forcibly changed in Size, merged into another creature or object, magically disassembled, forced to rearrange its components, partially teleported apart, or reshaped by another effect. Only your Crown authority can voluntarily reconfigure or separate it.

{@b Absolute Mass.} Unless you allow it, the Titan can't be Grappled, knocked Prone, Shoved, forcibly moved, forcibly teleported, carried, dragged, lifted, or physically Restrained. An effect that moves the entire surrounding region, plane, or structure can still move the Titan as part of that larger movement.

trait.name: Reconstruction
entries: {@b Indestructible Convergence.} At the start of each of the Titan's turns, it regains 120 Hit Points. This regeneration functions even while the Titan has 0 Hit Points. If it starts its turn at 0 Hit Points and eligible material remains available to constitute it, it regains Hit Points and reforms. Reducing the Titan to 0 Hit Points doesn't automatically destroy it.

{@b Matter Feeds the Titan.} Whenever the Titan regenerates, it can draw eligible unattended nonliving matter within 120 feet into itself. Eligible matter includes earth, soil, stone, sand, clay, rubble, minerals, raw metal, crystal, ice, snow, bone, dead wood, destroyed objects, damaged machinery, broken weapons, and other suitable nonliving matter. The material moves toward the Titan and becomes part of its body. The Titan doesn't require its original components in order to continue rebuilding itself.

{@b Reconstruction at 0 Hit Points.} Reaching 0 Hit Points doesn't automatically end Titan Convergence. Because of Indestructible Convergence, the Titan can reconstruct itself at the start of its next turn if sufficient eligible material remains. If Titan Convergence ends or the Titan can no longer reconstruct itself, its remaining components collapse into the spaces it occupied.

{@b Break Apart.} You can command the Titan to separate. Its surviving components detach and return to their original objects or materials. Any component maintained by another Crown effect can immediately resume functioning under that effect.

trait.name: Colossal Body
entries: {@b Crownforged Weapons.} All of the Titan's attacks count as magical. Whenever the Titan deals damage, it ignores Resistance to that damage. Immunity to that damage is treated as Resistance, and the Titan ignores that Resistance as well.
{@b Siege Incarnate.} The Titan deals four times normal damage to objects and structures.

{@b Unstoppable Advance.} The Titan can move through walls, fortifications, buildings, barricades, ordinary structures, unattended objects, and other noncreature physical barriers without spending additional movement. It can smash the material apart, push it aside, incorporate it into itself, or leave a passage behind.
{@b Colossal Reach.} The Titan has a base melee Reach of 15 feet unless an incorporated component reasonably grants greater Reach.

{@b Living Mass.} The Titan can carry creatures, vehicles, structures, and objects on or inside its body when its shape permits. Creatures can use sufficiently large portions of it as terrain, platforms, climbing surfaces, Half Cover, or Three-Quarters Cover.

trait.name: Titan Configuration
entries: The Titan can change Configuration as a Bonus Action; it lasts until changed or the Titan ends. When the Titan forms, choose one Configuration: War Titan, Fortress Titan, Siege Titan, Grasping Titan, or Devouring Titan. Changing Configuration rearranges the positions of existing components without changing their substance.

{@b War Titan.} Multiattack: the Titan makes 3 Titan Strikes. Once per turn when Titan Strike hits, the target must succeed on a {@dc 20 + PB} Strength saving throw or you choose one of the following: push it 30 feet, knock it Prone, throw it to an unoccupied space within 30 feet, or force it to drop all objects it is holding.

action.name: World-Crushing Trample
entries: The Titan can use this as part of its movement. Limit: Once per turn per creature. The Titan can move through the spaces of creatures smaller than itself.

On a successful save, the creature takes half damage and is moved to the nearest available space outside the Titan's path.

action.name: Sovereign Breach
entries: The Titan can replace one attack of its Multiattack with this action. The Titan can directly attack a magical barrier, ward, boundary, or supernatural obstruction within its Reach, including magical walls, walls of force, magical cages, magical domes, sealed magical doors, supernatural shields, wards preventing passage, barriers preventing teleportation, dimensional boundaries, magical prison walls, and similar effects.

entries: {@actSave str} {@dc 20 + PB}, any number of creatures within the Titan's Reach up to its remaining Grapple capacity. entries: Each creature currently Grappled by the Titan takes {@damage 3d12 + 15 + PB} Bludgeoning damage.

entries: This configuration lasts until it is changed again or the Titan ends. Choose War Titan, Fortress Titan, Siege Titan, Grasping Titan, or Devouring Titan. The Titan rearranges its components accordingly and retains its current Hit Points.

entries: When a creature within 30 feet takes damage, the Titan can move up to half its Speed toward that creature and interpose itself. Reduce the damage by {@dice 3d12 + 14 + PB}. The Titan takes damage equal to the amount prevented.

Changing Configuration rearranges the positions of existing components without changing their substance.

{@b War Titan.} Multiattack: the Titan makes 4 Titan Strikes. Once per turn when Titan Strike hits, the target must succeed on a {@dc 20 + PB} Strength saving throw or you choose one of the following: push it 30 feet, knock it Prone, throw it to an unoccupied space within 30 feet, or force it to drop all objects it is holding.

{@b Fortress Titan.} The Titan gains +3 AC while in this Configuration. Allies positioned on, within, or behind suitable portions of the Titan can gain Three-Quarters Cover. Hostile creatures treat the area within the Titan's Reach as Difficult Terrain.
{@b Siege Titan.} The Titan can independently operate all incorporated siege weapons, firearms, launchers, magical ranged weapons, and similar ranged mechanisms that remain functional.
{@b Grasping Titan.} The Titan can simultaneously Grapple a number of creatures equal to your Proficiency Bonus + the Titan's Proficiency Bonus. The escape DC for these Grapples is {@dc 20 + PB}.

{@b Devouring Titan.} Consume Matter can be used as a Bonus Action. The Titan can draw eligible unattended matter within 20 feet into itself. It regains Hit Points equal to 5 × your level × the Size value of the absorbed material (Tiny 1, Small 2, Medium 3, Large 4, Huge 5, Gargantuan 6), up to its Hit Point maximum. Endless Reconstruction — At the start of the Titan's turn, if eligible matter exists within 30 feet, it can absorb some of it and regain 70 Hit Points. This healing is in addition to Indestructible Convergence.

action.name: Multiattack (War Titan Only)
entries: While in War Titan Configuration, the Titan makes 4 Titan Strikes. Use the appropriate ability version for each attack. Existing options to replace an attack still apply.

action.name: Titan Strike
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 17 + PB} to hit, reach 20 ft. (or greater if granted by an incorporated component), one target. {@h}{@damage 6d12 + 17 + PB} Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage according to the incorporated component, or another justified damage type supplied by an incorporated magical component.

entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 8 + PB} to hit, reach 20 ft. (or greater if granted by an incorporated component), one target. {@h}{@damage 6d12 + 8 + PB} Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage according to the incorporated component, or another justified damage type supplied by an incorporated magical component.

entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 3 + PB} to hit, reach 20 ft. (or greater if granted by an incorporated component), one target. {@h}{@damage 6d12 + 3 + PB} Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage according to the incorporated component, or another justified damage type supplied by an incorporated magical component.

entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 11 + PB} to hit, reach 20 ft. action.name: World-Crushing Trample
entries: The Titan can use this as part of its movement. Limit: Once per turn per creature. The Titan can move through the spaces of creatures smaller than itself.

The first time it enters a creature's space on a turn, that creature must succeed on a {@dc 20 + PB} Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 12d12 + 17 + PB} Bludgeoning damage, be knocked Prone, and either be pushed to an unoccupied space adjacent to the Titan's path or carried beneath or within the Titan's moving mass until the movement ends.
On a successful save, the creature takes half damage and is moved to the nearest available space outside the Titan's path.

action.name: Sovereign Breach
entries: The Titan can replace one attack of its Multiattack with this action. The Titan can directly attack a magical barrier, ward, boundary, or supernatural obstruction within its Reach, including magical walls, walls of force, magical cages, magical domes, sealed magical doors, supernatural shields, wards preventing passage, barriers preventing teleportation, dimensional boundaries, magical prison walls, and similar effects.

For Sovereign Breach, such a barrier counts as something the Titan can physically attack even if its rules state that it can't be damaged, has no Hit Points, is immune to damage, can't be physically interacted with, can only be removed by a particular spell, or normally can't be destroyed by attacks. Make an attack using the Titan Attack Formula. Choose the relevant ability: {@hit 17 + PB|Strength}, {@hit 8 + PB|Dexterity}, {@hit 17 + PB|Constitution}, {@hit 3 + PB|Intelligence}, {@hit 11 + PB|Wisdom}, {@hit 7 + PB|Charisma}. If the effect has an AC, use it. Otherwise its AC is 10 + the spell or effect's level, or 20 if it has no meaningful level. On a hit, the magical barrier is shattered.

If it is a single continuous barrier, the entire barrier ends. If it is an exceptionally large magical structure, the Titan destroys a section up to a 30-foot Cube with each successful Breach Attack. Sovereign Breach ignores Damage Resistance, Damage Immunity, damage reduction, immunity to physical interaction, and requirements that only a particular spell can remove the barrier. The attack counts as both magical and physical for this purpose.

If a boundary prevents entering, leaving, teleporting, crossing dimensions, or passing through a region without physically manifesting, the Titan can attack the boundary itself. A successful Sovereign Breach destroys the restriction in the breached area.

action.name: Siege Barrage (Siege Titan Only)
entries: Choose a point within 300 feet. Each creature in a 30-foot-radius Sphere centered there must make a {@dc 20 + PB} Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 12d12 + 17 + PB} damage. Choose a damage type appropriate to the incorporated components, such as Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing, Fire, or another justified damage type. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage.

action.name: Seize (Grasping Titan Only)
entries: {@actSave str} {@dc 20 + PB}, any number of creatures within the Titan's Reach up to its remaining Grapple capacity. Each target chooses Strength or Dexterity and makes only that saving throw; use the corresponding Seize roll. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} and {@condition Restrained|XPHB} conditions until the Grapple ends.

action.name: Seize (Dexterity; Grasping Titan Only)
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 20 + PB}, any number of creatures within the Titan's Reach up to its remaining Grapple capacity. Each target chooses Strength or Dexterity and makes only that saving throw; use the corresponding Seize roll. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} and {@condition Restrained|XPHB} conditions until the Grapple ends.

bonus.name: Crush the Captive (Grasping Titan Only)
entries: Each creature currently Grappled by the Titan takes {@damage 4d12 + 17 + PB} Bludgeoning damage.

bonus.name: Reconfigure
entries: This configuration lasts until it is changed again or the Titan ends. Choose War Titan, Fortress Titan, Siege Titan, Grasping Titan, or Devouring Titan. The Titan rearranges its components accordingly and retains its current Hit Points.

reaction.name: Interpose the Fortress (Fortress Titan Only)
entries: When a creature within 30 feet takes damage, the Titan can move up to half its Speed toward that creature and interpose itself. Reduce the damage by {@dice 3d12 + 17 + PB}. The Titan takes damage equal to the amount prevented.

trait.name: Draconic Nature
entries: {@b Young Mind, Ancient Blood.} The wyrmling is fully sapient but is still a child. It can speak, reason, learn, negotiate, deceive, understand consequences, and make deliberate plans, but it normally lacks the experience, restraint, knowledge, and long-term judgment of older dragons. A wyrmling isn't automatically a scholar, mastermind, or expert spellcaster.

{@b Draconic Magical Instinct.} The dragon is proficient in Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}). It can make Arcana checks concerning spells, magical effects, Magic Items, curses, wards, and supernatural creatures. This instinct doesn't automatically reveal complete information.
{@b Keen Senses.} The dragon has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight or smell.
{@b No Change Shape.} The wyrmling doesn't possess Change Shape. True dragons of this variant first gain Change Shape at the Young age category.

trait.name: Draconic Magic
entries: {@b Fire Affinity.} When the dragon casts a spell that deals Fire damage, it ignores Resistance to Fire damage. A creature with Immunity to Fire damage remains immune.
{@b Innate Elemental Casting.} When the dragon casts a spell whose primary damage type is Fire, it can cast that spell without Verbal, Somatic, or non-costly Material components.

{@b Arcane Reclamation.} At the end of a Short Rest, the dragon can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed its Proficiency Bonus. It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

{@b Draconic Spell List.} Draconic magic grows from instinct and experience. The dragon knows every spell in the Red Dragon Spell List of a level no higher than 1. Those spells are presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait.

{@b Draconic At-Will Magic.} The dragon can cast each spell listed under At Will in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait without expending a spell slot and with no usage limit. A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The dragon can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable. An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the dragon's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack, if that dragon has Multiattack. Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell detect magic|XPHB}, {@spell burning hands|XPHB}.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: Each spell listed as Draconic High Magic can be cast once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot. Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the dragon from casting the same spell again using a spell slot. When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed. Draconic High Magic: {@spell burning hands|XPHB}.

trait.name: Sovereignty of the Burning Hoard
entries: To a red dragon, possession is not a legal concept but a fact of nature. What it claims becomes part of its identity, and resistance to its authority is treated as a personal insult. With age, the distinction between its treasure, its territory, and the world it believes it deserves begins to disappear.

entries.name: Claimed Treasure
entries: The dragon must touch the object for 1 minute to use this feature. The claim lasts until the dragon willingly releases it. The dragon can mystically mark up to PB × 10 objects as Claimed Treasure. While a Claimed object is on the same plane and within 1 mile, the dragon knows its direction, approximate distance, and whether it is moving. This doesn't reveal who carries the object or grant supernatural vision through it.

It doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.

entries: Black dragons don't merely destroy; they prefer to watch things decay. Civilizations, fortifications, bodies, and promises are simply structures waiting to fail. The older the dragon becomes, the more destruction itself seems to nourish it.

entries: Blue dragons regard the sky as a throne and the horizon as the boundary of their court. Mirage, thunder, sand, and lightning blur together around their territories. Eventually the weather ceases to be something surrounding the dragon and becomes something obeying it.

entries: White dragons may be less scholarly than their kin, but the hunt is a language they understand with terrifying clarity. trait.name: Sovereignty of the Burning Hoard

It can make Arcana checks concerning spells, magical effects, Magic Items, curses, wards, magical creatures, and supernatural phenomena. Its greater experience allows it to recognize and analyze magic much more reliably than a wyrmling, but this feature doesn't grant automatic knowledge.
{@b Keen Senses.} The dragon has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight or smell.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: The dragon can use this feature as an Action. The transformation lasts until the dragon ends it, uses this feature again, or dies. The dragon magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is equal to or lower than the dragon's own Challenge Rating, or returns to its true form. The assumed form can be any Size the chosen creature normally possesses.

While transformed, the dragon retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; personality and memories; alignment; Saving Throw proficiencies; Skill proficiencies; languages; Innate Draconic Spellcasting; Draconic Magical Instinct; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body.

It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics, including Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Armor Class, movement modes, natural weapons, physical senses, and other body-dependent traits and actions. It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features. The dragon can continue using its own draconic spellcasting while transformed.
Equipment it is wearing or carrying can merge into the new form or remain usable, as the dragon chooses when it transforms.

trait.name: Draconic Magic
entries: {@b Cold Affinity.} When the dragon casts a spell that deals Cold damage, it ignores Resistance to Cold damage. A creature with Immunity to Cold damage remains immune.
{@b Innate Elemental Casting.} When the dragon casts a spell whose primary damage type is Cold, it can cast that spell without Verbal, Somatic, or non-costly Material components.

{@b Arcane Reclamation.} At the end of a Short Rest, the dragon can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed its Proficiency Bonus. It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

{@b Draconic Spell List.} Draconic magic grows from instinct and experience. The dragon knows every spell in the White Dragon Spell List of a level no higher than 4. Those spells are presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait.

{@b Draconic At-Will Magic.} The dragon can cast each spell listed under At Will in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait without expending a spell slot and with no usage limit. A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The dragon can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable. An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the dragon's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack, if that dragon has Multiattack. Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell fog cloud|XPHB}, {@spell longstrider|XPHB}, {@spell Rime's binding ice|FTD}, {@spell pass without trace|XPHB}.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: Each spell listed as Draconic High Magic can be cast once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot. Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the dragon from casting the same spell again using a spell slot. When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed. trait.name: Memory of the Endless Hunt
entries: White dragons may be less scholarly than their kin, but the hunt is a language they understand with terrifying clarity. While within 1 mile, if there is a physical trail or scent the dragon could reasonably detect, it knows the trail's general direction.

entries: The dragon can use this feature as a Bonus Action. The dragon moves up to half its Speed toward its Chosen Prey. This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks from the Chosen Prey, and snow and ice don't cost the dragon extra movement during it.

trait.name: Web of the Verdant Lie
entries: Green dragons understand that controlling what someone believes is often more useful than controlling their body. They collect promises, weaknesses, fears, alliances, and secrets with the same appetite other dragons reserve for gold. entries.name: Borrowed Voice

After hearing a voice or sound for at least 1 minute, the dragon can reproduce it. entries.name: Venomous Bargain

entries.name: Web of Influence

On a success, the dragon learns one broad current reasonably exposed by the creature's behavior: a fear, desire, important loyalty, or immediate goal. This doesn't reveal memories or perfectly hidden truths.

trait.name: Frightful Presence

entries.name: Frozen Quarry

When the dragon deals Lightning damage to a creature with Lightning Immunity, that Immunity is treated as Lightning Resistance, and the dragon then ignores that Resistance. As a result, the dragon's Lightning damage affects creatures with Lightning Resistance or Lightning Immunity without reducing the damage.
{@b Arcane Reclamation.} At the end of a Short Rest, the dragon can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 14. It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

{@b Draconic Spell List.} Draconic magic grows from instinct and experience. The dragon knows every spell in the Blue Dragon Spell List of a level no higher than 9. Those spells are presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait.

{@b Draconic At-Will Magic.} The dragon can cast each spell listed under At Will in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait without expending a spell slot and with no usage limit. A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The dragon can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable. An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the dragon's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack, if that dragon has Multiattack. Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell detect magic|XPHB}, {@spell thunderwave|XPHB}, {@spell shatter|XPHB}, {@spell misty step|XPHB}, {@spell lightning bolt|XPHB}, {@spell dispel magic|XPHB}, {@spell storm sphere|XGE}, {@spell control winds|XGE}.

trait.name: Throne of the Storm
entries: Blue dragons regard the sky as a throne and the horizon as the boundary of their court. Mirage, thunder, sand, and lightning blur together around their territories. Eventually the weather ceases to be something surrounding the dragon and becomes something obeying it.

entries.name: Mirage of the Wastes
entries: The dragon can use this feature as an Action. This effect lasts for up to 1 hour. The dragon creates a harmless visual or auditory mirage within 60 feet occupying no more than a 10-foot Cube. Physical interaction reveals that it isn't real. The dragon also ignores natural penalties caused by extreme heat and blowing sand.

entries.name: Static Step
entries: The dragon can use this feature as a Reaction. When the dragon is targeted by an attack, it can move up to 20 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. If this movement changes whether the attack can legally reach it, the attack is resolved using the dragon's new position. The dragon can use this Reaction a number of times equal to its PB per Long Rest.

entries.name: Storm Dominion
entries: The dragon emits a 60-foot aura. Hostile creatures treat flying movement in the aura as Difficult Terrain. Hostile creatures also have Disadvantage on ranged weapon attacks made through more than 20 feet of the aura. The dragon chooses whether the effect visibly manifests as wind, sand, static, or clear storm pressure.

entries.name: Thunder Answers Defiance
entries: The dragon can use this feature as a Reaction. When a creature within 120 feet casts a spell or takes a Reaction, the dragon can strike it with lightning. The creature makes a Dexterity Saving Throw against the dragon's Spell Save DC, taking {@damage 6d10} Lightning damage on a failure or half as much damage on a success.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the dragon more than size. Its voice, gaze, posture, and supernatural presence carry the instinctive certainty of an apex creature that has survived centuries. Those who stand before it can feel that history pressing against their courage. At the start of its turn, the dragon can activate this feature. This effect lasts for up to 1 minute. Each creature of the dragon's choice within 180 feet that can see or hear it must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Spell Save DC.

On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the dragon for 1 minute. The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that dragon's Frightful Presence for 24 hours. This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition.

headerEntries: The dragon's spellcasting ability is Charisma. Its spell save DC is 23, and it has +15 to hit with spell attacks. It requires no Spellcasting Focus. action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dragon makes four attacks using any combination of its Bite, Claw, and Tail. A spell cast through Draconic High Magic can also replace that one attack.

entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 16} to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 6d10 + 9} Piercing damage plus {@damage 6d8} Lightning damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 16} to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 6d6 + 9} Slashing damage.

action.name: Tail
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 16} to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 6d8 + 9} Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Wing
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 16} to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 6d6 + 9} Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Lightning Breath {@recharge 5}
entries: The dragon exhales its breath weapon in a 180-foot-long, 15-foot-wide Line. Each creature in that area must make a {@dc 24} Dexterity Saving Throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 24d10} Lightning damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage. Ancient Lightning Supremacy applies to this Lightning damage.

action.name: Heaven-Splitting Lance
entries: {@atk rs} {@hit 15} to hit, range 360 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 12d12} Lightning damage. The target can't take Reactions until the end of its next turn. The target's Speed is halved until the end of its next turn. This attack is magical and counts as a spell attack, but isn't itself a spell.

action.name: Frightful Presence
entries: The dragon can replace one attack of its Multiattack with this action. This effect lasts for up to 1 minute. Each creature of the dragon's choice within 240 feet that is aware of it must make a {@dc 23} Wisdom Saving Throw. On a failed save, a creature is Frightened for 1 minute. The creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: The wyrm can use this feature as an Action. The transformation lasts until the wyrm ends it, uses this feature again, or dies. The wyrm magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 25 or lower, or returns to its true form.

While transformed, it retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; Saving Throw and Skill proficiencies; languages; personality and memories; Innate Draconic Spellcasting; Legendary Resistance; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body. It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics.

entries: When the wyrm would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, it doesn't die or fall Unconscious. Instead, it regains Hit Points equal to half its Hit Point maximum; ends any conditions or ongoing effects on itself that it chooses; recharges its Breath Weapon; regains 3 expended uses of Legendary Resistance; regains one expended use of Draconic High Magic, including a 9th-level spell; and immediately regains its full allotment of Legendary Actions.

trait.name: Memory of the Endless Hunt
entries: White dragons may be less scholarly than their kin, but the hunt is a language they understand with terrifying clarity. Tracks, scents, wounds, habits, and escape routes become parts of a living map in the dragon's mind. Once an elder white dragon decides something is prey, distance becomes a temporary inconvenience.

entries.name: Chosen Prey
entries: The wyrm must spend 1 minute observing a creature, its scent, or its tracks to use this feature. The effect lasts until replaced. The dragon marks one creature as its Chosen Prey. It has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) and Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) checks made to locate or track that creature. While within 1 mile, if there is a physical trail or scent the dragon could reasonably detect, it knows the trail's general direction.

entries.name: Relentless Pursuit
entries: The wyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action. The dragon moves up to half its Speed toward its Chosen Prey. This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks from the Chosen Prey, and snow and ice don't cost the dragon extra movement during it.

entries.name: Learn the Prey's Pattern

entries.name: Frozen Quarry

Whenever the dragon deals Cold damage to that creature, its Speed becomes 0 until the start of the dragon's next turn.

If the prey remains on the same plane, the wyrm can immediately move up to its Fly Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

trait.name: Dominion of Ruin
entries: Black dragons don't merely destroy; they prefer to watch things decay. Civilizations, fortifications, bodies, and promises are simply structures waiting to fail. The older the dragon becomes, the more destruction itself seems to nourish it.

entries.name: Mireborn Predator
entries: The dragon ignores Difficult Terrain created by mud, shallow water, swamp, or rotting vegetation. It can Hide while only Lightly Obscured by swamp vegetation, murky water, fog, or ruins.

entries.name: Cruel Ambush
entries: The healing prevention lasts until the start of the dragon's next turn. The dragon can take the Hide action as a Bonus Action while it has suitable concealment. trait.name: Change Shape
entries: The wyrm can use this feature as an Action. The transformation lasts until the wyrm ends it, uses this feature again, or dies. The wyrm magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 27 or lower, or returns to its true form.

It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics.

It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features. The wyrm can continue using its own draconic spellcasting while transformed.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The wyrm can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell modify memory|XPHB}, {@spell mass suggestion|XPHB}, {@spell dominate monster|XPHB}, {@spell feeblemind|XPHB}, {@spell psychic scream|XGE}, {@spell shapechange|XPHB}, and {@spell wish|XPHB}. trait.name: World-Heart Reignition (1/Long Rest)
