When the dragon deals Radiant damage to a creature with Radiant Immunity, that Immunity is treated as Radiant Resistance, and the dragon then ignores that Resistance. As a result, the dragon's Radiant damage affects creatures with Radiant Resistance or Radiant Immunity without reducing the damage.
{@b Arcane Reclamation.} At the end of a Short Rest, the dragon can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 14. It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

{@b Draconic Spell List.} Draconic magic grows from instinct and experience. The dragon knows the listed Crystal Dragon spells through 9th-level magic, as presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics) trait.

{@b Draconic At-Will Magic.} The dragon can cast each spell listed under At Will in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics) trait without expending a spell slot and with no usage limit. A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The dragon can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable. An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the dragon's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack. Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell detect magic|XPHB}, {@spell sanctuary|XPHB}, {@spell guiding bolt|XPHB}, {@spell lesser restoration|XPHB}, {@spell revivify|XPHB}, {@spell death ward|XPHB}, {@spell greater restoration|XPHB}, {@spell heal|XPHB}.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The dragon can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell greater restoration|XPHB}, {@spell heal|XPHB}, {@spell resurrection|XPHB}, {@spell mass heal|XPHB}, {@spell wish|XPHB}. Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the dragon from casting the same spell again using a spell slot. When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.

trait.name: Light That Wants to Live
entries: Crystal dragon magic doesn't merely illuminate—it reinforces life and possibility. Radiance passing through their crystalline bodies seems reluctant to disappear without leaving something useful behind. Even a wyrmling instinctively turns excess magical light into protection for itself or another.

entries.name: Reflected Vitality
entries: The Temporary Hit Points persist until depleted or replaced. Once per turn when the dragon deals Radiant damage to at least one creature or restores Hit Points to another creature, it chooses itself or one creature within 30 feet. That creature gains Temporary Hit Points equal to the dragon's PB + Intelligence modifier + Charisma modifier (18 Temporary Hit Points for this ancient dragon).

entries.name: Shared Brilliance
entries: The dragon can use this feature as a Reaction. The Temporary Hit Points persist until depleted or replaced. When a creature the dragon can see within 60 feet takes damage or fails a Saving Throw, the dragon releases a radiant pulse and chooses Shielding Light or Guiding Light.

entries.name: Shielding Light
entries: Reduce the triggering damage by {@damage 3d8} + the dragon's Charisma modifier.

entries.name: Guiding Light
entries: The target rerolls the failed Saving Throw and must use the new result. If Shielding Light reduces the triggering damage to 0, or if the reroll from Guiding Light succeeds, the target gains 12 Temporary Hit Points. The dragon can use Shared Brilliance a number of times equal to its PB per Long Rest.

entries.name: Beacon of Renewal
entries: The dragon can use this feature as an Action. This effect lasts for 1 minute. The dragon creates a 60-foot aura. A chosen creature that starts its turn in the aura while it has at least 1 Hit Point regains Hit Points equal to the dragon's PB + Charisma modifier. Whenever a chosen creature in the aura regains Hit Points from another source, the amount restored increases by the dragon's PB.

The first time on each of its turns that a chosen creature gains Temporary Hit Points, it can end Charmed, Frightened, or Poisoned on itself. If a chosen creature is at its Hit Point maximum when it would regain Hit Points from Beacon of Renewal, it gains that amount as Temporary Hit Points instead.

entries.name: Overflowing Life
entries: When a chosen creature in Beacon of Renewal regains Hit Points and that healing would raise it above its Hit Point maximum, the excess healing becomes Temporary Hit Points instead, to a maximum of 5 × the dragon's PB (35 for this ancient dragon). once per turn when a creature in the aura regains Hit Points from any source, the dragon can choose a second creature in the aura. The second creature regains Hit Points equal to half the healing the first creature actually received. Healing created by Overflowing Life can't trigger Overflowing Life again.

entries.name: Prismatic Purification
entries: When the dragon causes a creature to regain Hit Points with one of its spells or features, it can end Blinded, Charmed, Frightened, or Poisoned on that creature. A creature can benefit from Prismatic Purification only once per turn.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the dragon more than size. Its voice, gaze, posture, and supernatural presence carry the instinctive certainty of an apex creature that has survived centuries. Those who stand before it can feel that history pressing against their courage. At the start of its turn, the dragon can activate this feature. This effect lasts for up to 1 minute. Each creature of the dragon's choice within 180 feet that can see or hear it must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.

On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the dragon for 1 minute. The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that dragon's Frightful Presence for 24 hours. This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition.

spellcasting.name: Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics)
headerEntries: The dragon's spellcasting ability is Intelligence. Its spell save DC is 22, and it has +14 to hit with spell attacks. The dragon casts these spells psionically. It requires no Verbal or Somatic components and no Material components that have no listed cost and aren't consumed. Material components that have a listed cost or are consumed are still required normally.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dragon makes four attacks using any combination of its Bite, Claw, and Tail. The dragon can replace only one of these attacks with the casting of a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 Action. The spell is resolved normally and expends a spell slot or use as normal. A spell cast through Draconic High Magic can also replace that one attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 15} to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 6d10 + 8} Piercing damage plus {@damage 6d8} Radiant damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 15} to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 6d6 + 8} Slashing damage.

action.name: Tail
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 15} to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 6d8 + 8} Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Wing
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 15} to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 6d6 + 8} Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Scintillating Breath {@recharge 5}
entries: The Temporary Hit Points persist until depleted or replaced. The dragon exhales scintillating radiance in a 120-foot Cone. Each creature in that area must make a {@dc 23} Constitution Saving Throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 24d8} Radiant damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage. After resolving the Breath, the dragon chooses up to PB creatures within 120 feet. Each chosen creature gains 25 Temporary Hit Points.

legendaryHeader: The dragon can take 5 Legendary Actions, choosing from the options below. Only one Legendary Action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The dragon regains spent Legendary Actions at the start of its turn.

legendary.name: Detect
entries: The dragon makes a Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check.

legendary.name: Tail Attack
entries: The dragon makes one Tail attack.

legendary.name: Cast Cantrip
entries: The dragon casts one cantrip.

legendary.name: Psychic Step
entries: The dragon uses Psychic Step, but teleports no more than 60 feet and can't bring another creature with it.

legendary.name: Wing Attack (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: Each creature within 20 feet of the dragon must make a {@dc 23} Dexterity Saving Throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 6d6 + 8} Bludgeoning damage and falls Prone. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and doesn't fall Prone. The dragon can then fly up to half its Fly Speed.

legendary.name: Psionic Displacement (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The dragon chooses one creature it can see within 60 feet. The target must make a Strength Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC. On a failed save, the dragon moves the target up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. This movement isn't teleportation.

legendary.name: Breath Surge (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The dragon rolls one additional d6 to recharge its Breath Weapon. If the Breath Weapon is already available, the dragon can instead immediately use it.

legendary.name: Cast Psionic Spell (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The dragon casts one psionic spell of 5th level or lower that normally has a casting time of 1 Action, expending a spell slot or use as normal.

legendary.name: High Magic (Costs 5 Actions)
entries: The dragon casts one spell from Draconic High Magic whose use is still available.

monster.name: Ancient Topaz Dragon

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (5/Day)
entries: If the dragon fails a Saving Throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Draconic Nature
entries: {@b Draconic Magical Instinct.} The dragon is proficient in Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}). It can make Arcana checks concerning spells, magical effects, Magic Items, curses, wards, magical creatures, and supernatural phenomena. This trait doesn't grant automatic or complete knowledge.
{@b Keen Senses.} The dragon has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight or smell.

{@b Psionic Mind.} Thought flows as naturally as breath. The dragon can communicate telepathically with a creature it can see within 120 feet. A contacted creature can understand the dragon if it knows at least one language, and it can reply telepathically while it remains within 120 feet of the dragon.
{@b Amphibious.} The dragon can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Psychic Step
entries: Distance has become increasingly optional to an elder gem dragon. Its body follows thought with almost no delay, slipping between positions before ordinary movement can properly begin. Those it chooses to carry can briefly become part of that same act of will. The dragon can use this feature as a Bonus Action. The dragon teleports up to 120 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. When it teleports, the dragon can choose up to two willing creatures within 10 feet of it.

Each chosen creature teleports with the dragon and appears in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of it. This isn't a spell and requires no components. The dragon can use Psychic Step without a usage limit. Objects worn or carried by the dragon teleport with it normally.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: An ancient gem dragon can impose a different physical pattern upon its body without surrendering the psionic identity beneath. Its transformed body is a chosen vessel rather than a replacement for the mind, memories, or magic that define the dragon. Even while wearing another shape, its thought remains unmistakably draconic. The dragon can use this feature as an Action. The transformation lasts until the dragon ends it, uses this feature again, or dies.

The dragon magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 21 or lower, or returns to its true form. The assumed form can be any Size the chosen creature normally possesses.

While transformed, the dragon retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; personality and memories; alignment; Saving Throw proficiencies; Skill proficiencies; languages; Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics); Psionic Mind; Psychic Step; Draconic Magical Instinct; Legendary Resistance; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body.

It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics, including Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Armor Class, movement modes, natural weapons, physical senses, and other body-dependent traits and actions. It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features. The dragon can continue using its own psionic spellcasting while transformed.
Equipment it is wearing or carrying can merge into the new form or remain usable, as the dragon chooses when it transforms.

trait.name: Draconic Magic
entries: {@b Ancient Necrotic Supremacy.} The dragon's Necrotic damage ignores Necrotic Resistance. When the dragon deals Necrotic damage to a creature with Necrotic Immunity, that Immunity is treated as Necrotic Resistance, and the dragon then ignores that Resistance. As a result, the dragon's Necrotic damage affects creatures with Necrotic Resistance or Necrotic Immunity without reducing the damage.
{@b Arcane Reclamation.} At the end of a Short Rest, the dragon can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 14. It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the dragon's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack. Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell create or destroy water|XPHB}, {@spell detect magic|XPHB}, {@spell ray of enfeeblement|XPHB}, {@spell wither and bloom|SCC}, {@spell bestow curse|XPHB}, {@spell blight|XPHB}, {@spell enervation|XGE}, {@spell harm|XPHB}.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The dragon can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell harm|XPHB}, {@spell finger of death|XPHB}, {@spell Abi-Dalzim's horrid wilting|XGE}, {@spell power word kill|XPHB}, {@spell wish|XPHB}. Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the dragon from casting the same spell again using a spell slot. When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.

trait.name: Law of Ending
entries: Topaz dragons perceive decay less as tragedy and more as a universal rule. Water evaporates, flesh weakens, stone erodes, and every living thing eventually reaches its conclusion. Even a wyrmling can accelerate tiny fragments of that process through instinctive psionic entropy.

entries.name: Drying Touch
entries: Using Drying Touch on an environmental liquid requires an Action. The environmental change is permanent, and the healing prevention lasts until the start of the dragon's next turn. The dragon can touch nonmagical water or another ordinary liquid and instantly destroy up to 1 cubic foot of it through supernatural desiccation. This can't directly desiccate liquid inside a living creature. once per turn when the dragon deals Necrotic damage to a creature, that creature can't regain Hit Points until the start of the dragon's next turn.

entries.name: Entropic Field
entries: The dragon can use this feature as a Bonus Action. This effect lasts for 1 minute. The dragon creates a 30-foot aura. A chosen hostile creature that starts its turn in the aura must make a Constitution Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC. On a failed save, until the start of its next turn the creature can't regain Hit Points, can't gain Temporary Hit Points, and its Speed is reduced by 10 feet. The dragon can also cause nonmagical unattended plants, food, wood, cloth, and other ordinary organic matter in the aura to dry, wilt, or become brittle at an accelerated rate. Entropic Field doesn't automatically deal damage to creatures.

entries.name: Accelerated Ending
entries: The Maximum Hit Point reduction lasts 1 hour. Once per turn when the dragon deals Necrotic damage to a creature in its Entropic Field, the target must make a Constitution Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC. On a failed save, the target's Hit Point maximum is reduced by half the Necrotic damage it took from the triggering damage, to a maximum reduction of 5 × the dragon's PB (25 for this adult dragon). Multiple reductions from Accelerated Ending don't stack; only the highest reduction applies.
This isn't a disease or curse. {@spell Greater Restoration|XPHB} or other magic that removes reductions to a creature's Hit Point maximum can end the reduction normally.

entries.name: Entropy Becomes Law
entries: The radius of Entropic Field increases from 30 feet to 60 feet. A chosen hostile creature that starts its turn in the aura and fails the Constitution Saving Throw can't regain Hit Points, can't gain Temporary Hit Points, has its Speed reduced by 20 feet, and can't benefit from regeneration until the start of its next turn. Healing that would restore Hit Points to that creature before the start of its next turn restores 0 Hit Points instead. The first time on each of its turns that such a creature takes Necrotic damage from the dragon, it loses all Temporary Hit Points before that damage is applied.

entries.name: Collapse Toward the End
entries: The dragon can use this feature as a Reaction. When a creature the dragon can see within Entropic Field uses healing, regains Hit Points, or attempts to remove a reduction to its Hit Point maximum, the dragon can force it to make a Constitution Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC. On a failed save, the triggering effect is still expended or used normally but has no effect on that creature. The dragon can use Collapse Toward the End a number of times equal to its PB per Long Rest.

Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the dragon from casting the same spell again using a spell slot. When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.

trait.name: The Hidden Thought
entries: Emerald dragons prefer to know more than they reveal. Illusion is not merely concealment to them; it is a way to control which version of reality another mind receives. Their earliest psionic instincts are already devoted to watching without being watched in return.

entries.name: Observer Behind the Image
entries: The dragon can Hide as a Bonus Action while Lightly Obscured, behind an illusion, within Dim Light, or possessing Half Cover or better. when it communicates telepathically, the recipient can't determine the direction or physical location from which the telepathic voice originates unless the dragon allows it.

entries.name: False Presence
entries: The dragon can use this feature as a Bonus Action. This effect lasts for 1 minute. The dragon creates an illusory duplicate of itself in an unoccupied space it can see within 60 feet. The duplicate has no Hit Points, can't pass through objects, and looks, sounds, and smells like the dragon. When the dragon uses a Bonus Action, it can move the duplicate up to 40 feet.

The dragon can use the duplicate as the apparent origin point of its telepathy, its Illusion spells, and spells that target a mind or perception but don't create a physical projectile. The first time on each turn that a creature attacks the duplicate, the attack automatically misses and the attacker must make an Intelligence Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC. On a failed save, that creature can't see the real dragon until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Distributed Presence
entries: The dragon can use this feature as a Bonus Action. This effect lasts for 1 minute. When the dragon uses False Presence, it can maintain a number of duplicates at once equal to its PB (6 for this adult dragon). Each duplicate occupies its own position and can serve as an origin for the dragon's telepathy, Illusion spells, and mind- or perception-targeting spells as described by False Presence. When the dragon uses a Bonus Action to move its duplicates, each duplicate can move up to 40 feet.

entries.name: Swap the Thought
entries: The dragon can use this feature as a Reaction. When the dragon is targeted by an attack or fails a Saving Throw, it can swap positions with one of its duplicates within 120 feet. The chosen duplicate then disappears. For an attack, resolve the attack using the dragon's new position. For an Area of Effect, use the new position to determine whether the dragon remains in the area. This is psionic displacement, not the casting of a teleportation spell.

entries.name: No Single True Position
entries: The dragon can maintain a number of False Presence duplicates at once equal to PB + 3 (10 for this ancient dragon). While at least one duplicate exists, when a spell or magical effect that isn't an Area of Effect attempts to choose the dragon as a target, the creature creating the effect must make an Intelligence Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC. On a failed save, the dragon chooses one of its duplicates to become the target instead. The duplicate disappears after the effect is resolved.
If the effect can't legally target the chosen duplicate, the effect fails against the dragon, but any Action, spell slot, charge, or other limited use spent on that effect is still expended.

entries.name: Thought Without Origin
entries: A creature can't determine the dragon's precise location solely through telepathy, divination that detects thoughts, or magical detection of consciousness unless the dragon allows it. Such effects can reveal that a mind or consciousness is present in the relevant area but don't reveal the dragon's exact location by themselves.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the dragon more than size. Its voice, gaze, posture, and supernatural presence carry the instinctive certainty of an apex creature that has survived centuries. Those who stand before it can feel that history pressing against their courage. At the start of its turn, the dragon can activate this feature. This effect lasts for up to 1 minute. Each creature of the dragon's choice within 180 feet that can see or hear it must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.

On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the dragon for 1 minute. The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that dragon's Frightful Presence for 24 hours. This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition.

headerEntries: The dragon's spellcasting ability is Intelligence. Its spell save DC is 23, and it has +15 to hit with spell attacks. The dragon casts these spells psionically. It requires no Verbal or Somatic components and no Material components that have no listed cost and aren't consumed. Material components that have a listed cost or are consumed are still required normally.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dragon makes four attacks using any combination of its Bite, Claw, and Tail. The dragon can replace only one of these attacks with the casting of a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 Action. The spell is resolved normally and expends a spell slot or use as normal. A spell cast through Draconic High Magic can also replace that one attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 15} to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 6d10 + 8} Piercing damage plus {@damage 6d8} Psychic damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 15} to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 6d6 + 8} Slashing damage.

action.name: Tail
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 15} to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 6d8 + 8} Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Wing
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 15} to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 6d6 + 8} Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Disorienting Breath {@recharge 5}
entries: This effect lasts until the end of the target's next turn. The dragon exhales disorienting psychic force in a 120-foot Cone. Each creature in that area must make a {@dc 24} Intelligence Saving Throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 24d8} Psychic damage, can't take Reactions or Bonus Actions, and whenever it makes an Attack Roll, Ability Check, or Saving Throw before the end of its next turn, it rolls ({@dice 1d10}) and subtracts the result. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and suffers no additional effect.

legendaryHeader: The dragon can take 5 Legendary Actions, choosing from the options below. Only one Legendary Action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The dragon regains spent Legendary Actions at the start of its turn.

entries: The dragon makes one Tail attack.

legendary.name: Cast Cantrip

legendary.name: Psychic Step
entries: The dragon uses Psychic Step, but teleports no more than 60 feet and can't bring another creature with it.

legendary.name: Wing Attack (Costs 2 Actions)

monster.name: Ancient Sapphire Dragon

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (5/Day)
entries: If the dragon fails a Saving Throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Draconic Nature
entries: {@b Draconic Magical Instinct.} The dragon is proficient in Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}). It can make Arcana checks concerning spells, magical effects, Magic Items, curses, wards, magical creatures, and supernatural phenomena. This trait doesn't grant automatic or complete knowledge.
{@b Keen Senses.} The dragon has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight or smell.

{@b Psionic Mind.} Thought flows as naturally as breath. The dragon can communicate telepathically with a creature it can see within 120 feet. trait.name: Psychic Step
entries: Distance has become increasingly optional to an elder gem dragon. Its body follows thought with almost no delay, slipping between positions before ordinary movement can properly begin. Those it chooses to carry can briefly become part of that same act of will. The dragon can use this feature as a Bonus Action. The dragon teleports up to 120 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. When it teleports, the dragon can choose up to two willing creatures within 10 feet of it.

Each chosen creature teleports with the dragon and appears in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of it. This isn't a spell and requires no components. The dragon can use Psychic Step without a usage limit. Objects worn or carried by the dragon teleport with it normally.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: An ancient gem dragon can impose a different physical pattern upon its body without surrendering the psionic identity beneath. Its transformed body is a chosen vessel rather than a replacement for the mind, memories, or magic that define the dragon. Even while wearing another shape, its thought remains unmistakably draconic. It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics, including Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Armor Class, movement modes, natural weapons, physical senses, and other body-dependent traits and actions. It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features. The dragon can continue using its own psionic spellcasting while transformed.
Equipment it is wearing or carrying can merge into the new form or remain usable, as the dragon chooses when it transforms.

entries: {@b Ancient Thunder Supremacy.} The dragon's Thunder damage ignores Thunder Resistance. entries.name: Echo Map

entries.name: Expanded Echo Map
entries: The Tremorsense granted by Echo Map increases from 30 feet to 60 feet.

entries: The radius of Tactical Resonance increases from 90 feet to 150 feet.

entries.name: Local Gravity
entries: The dragon can use this feature as a Bonus Action. This effect lasts for 1 minute. The dragon chooses one creature or unattended object within 60 feet. entries.name: Crushing Gravity
entries: The area is Difficult Terrain for hostile creatures, their jump distance is quartered, and a hostile flying creature that starts its turn in the Domain must make a Strength Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC. On a failed save, it descends up to 30 feet.

entries.name: Liberating Gravity
entries: Chosen creatures in the Domain gain 10 feet of Speed, have their jump distance tripled, take no falling damage, and have Advantage on Saving Throws against being Grappled or Restrained by effects caused by physical force. As a Bonus Action, the dragon can move the center of the Domain up to 30 feet. The dragon can have only one Gravitational Domain at a time.

entries: The dragon can use this feature as a Reaction. Choose one: Redirect the movement by up to 90 degrees; Magnify the movement by up to 30 feet; or Suppress the movement by up to 30 feet, to a minimum of 0 feet. An unwilling creature can make a Strength Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC. On a success, its movement is unchanged. Absolute Vector doesn't teleport a creature and can't force a creature or object through a solid object.

If it is flying, its Fly Speed becomes 0 until the start of its next turn.

A creature that attempts to teleport into, out of, or through Event Horizon must make a Strength Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC. On a failed save, the teleportation fails, but the resource used to attempt it isn't expended.

The dragon is unaffected by the negative effects of Event Horizon, can use Psychic Step into or out of it freely, and treats every point inside the sphere as visible for purposes of Psychic Step unless solid Total Cover blocks that point.

entries.name: Gravitational Collapse
entries: While Event Horizon is active, the dragon can use this feature as a Bonus Action. Once per round, the dragon compresses Event Horizon. Creatures of its choice in the sphere make a Strength Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC. legendary.name: Breath Surge (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The dragon rolls one additional d6 to recharge its Breath Weapon. If the Breath Weapon is already available, the dragon can instead immediately use it.

legendary.name: Cast Psionic Spell (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The dragon casts one psionic spell of 5th level or lower that normally has a casting time of 1 Action, expending a spell slot or use as normal.

legendary.name: High Magic (Costs 5 Actions)
entries: The dragon casts one spell from Draconic High Magic whose use is still available.

monster.name: Crystal Wyrm

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (7/Day)
entries: If the wyrm fails a Saving Throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Draconic Magic
entries: {@b Wyrm Magic Resistance.} The wyrm has Advantage on Saving Throws against spells and other magical effects.
{@b Perfect Concentration.} The wyrm automatically succeeds on Constitution Saving Throws made to maintain Concentration as a result of taking damage.

{@b Wyrm Radiant Supremacy.} The wyrm's mastery of radiant power has exceeded the ordinary defensive categories used by lesser creatures. Resistance no longer represents meaningful protection, and even immunity can be forced into a state the dragon can overcome. Its signature energy behaves as an extension of psionic authority rather than an ordinary source of damage. The wyrm's Radiant damage ignores Radiant Resistance. When the wyrm deals Radiant damage to a creature with Radiant Immunity, that Immunity is treated as Radiant Resistance, and the wyrm then ignores that Resistance. As a result, the wyrm's Radiant damage affects creatures with Radiant Resistance or Radiant Immunity without reducing the damage.
{@b Arcane Reclamation.} At the end of a Short Rest, the wyrm can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 24. It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

{@b Draconic Spell List.} Draconic magic grows from instinct and experience. The wyrm knows the listed Crystal Dragon spells through 9th-level magic, as presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics) trait.

{@b Draconic At-Will Magic.} The wyrm can cast each spell listed under At Will in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics) trait without expending a spell slot and with no usage limit. A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The wyrm can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable. An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the wyrm's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack. Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell detect magic|XPHB}, {@spell sanctuary|XPHB}, {@spell guiding bolt|XPHB}, {@spell lesser restoration|XPHB}, {@spell revivify|XPHB}, {@spell death ward|XPHB}, {@spell greater restoration|XPHB}, {@spell heal|XPHB}, {@spell mass cure wounds|XPHB}, {@spell holy aura|XPHB}.

trait.name: Draconic Nature
entries: {@b Draconic Magical Instinct.} The dragon is proficient in Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}). It can make Arcana checks concerning spells, magical effects, Magic Items, curses, wards, magical creatures, and supernatural phenomena. This trait doesn't grant automatic or complete knowledge.
{@b Keen Senses.} The dragon has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight or smell.

{@b Psionic Mind.} Thought flows as naturally as breath. The dragon can communicate telepathically with a creature it can see within 120 feet. A contacted creature can understand the dragon if it knows at least one language, and it can reply telepathically while it remains within 120 feet of the dragon.

trait.name: Psychic Step
entries: Distance is no longer a route to a gem wyrm. Position is simply another state its mind can choose. Those close enough to enter that thought can cross space with it. The wyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action. The wyrm teleports up to 180 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. When it teleports, it can choose up to four willing creatures within 20 feet. Each chosen creature teleports with it and appears in an unoccupied space within 20 feet of the wyrm. This isn't a spell and requires no components. The wyrm can use Psychic Step without a usage limit, including while Grappled or Restrained. Objects worn or carried by the wyrm teleport with it normally.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: A gem wyrm can impose an entirely different physical pattern upon its body without diminishing the mind beneath. Its chosen shape is merely another arrangement of matter directed by the same ancient consciousness. No borrowed body can replace the psionic identity that defines the wyrm. The wyrm can use this feature as an Action. The transformation lasts until the wyrm ends it, uses this feature again, or dies.
The wyrm magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 26 or lower, or returns to its true form. The assumed form can be any Size the chosen creature normally possesses.

While transformed, the wyrm retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; personality and memories; alignment; Saving Throw proficiencies; Skill proficiencies; languages; Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics); Psionic Mind; Psychic Step; Draconic Magical Instinct; Legendary Resistance; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body.

It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics, including Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Armor Class, movement modes, natural weapons, physical senses, and other body-dependent traits and actions. It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features. The wyrm can continue using its own psionic spellcasting while transformed.
Equipment it is wearing or carrying can merge into the new form or remain usable, as the wyrm chooses when it transforms.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The wyrm can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell greater restoration|XPHB}, {@spell heal|XPHB}, {@spell resurrection|XPHB}, {@spell mass heal|XPHB}, {@spell true resurrection|XPHB}, {@spell holy aura|XPHB}, {@spell wish|XPHB}. Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the wyrm from casting the same spell again using a spell slot. When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.

trait.name: World-Heart Reignition (1/Long Rest)
entries: The death of a wyrm is not always a single event. Its ancient body and psionic identity can violently reassert themselves when destruction should have become final. For a brief second phase of existence, the creature returns with its greatest powers burning again. When the wyrm would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, it doesn't die or fall Unconscious.

Instead, it regains Hit Points equal to half its Hit Point maximum; ends any conditions or ongoing effects on itself that it chooses; recharges its Breath Weapon; regains 3 expended uses of Legendary Resistance; regains one expended use of Draconic High Magic, including a 9th-level spell; and immediately regains its full allotment of Legendary Actions.

trait.name: Light That Wants to Live
entries: Crystal dragon magic doesn't merely illuminate—it reinforces life and possibility. Radiance passing through their crystalline bodies seems reluctant to disappear without leaving something useful behind. Even a wyrmling instinctively turns excess magical light into protection for itself or another.

entries.name: Reflected Vitality
entries: The Temporary Hit Points persist until depleted or replaced. Once per turn when the dragon deals Radiant damage to at least one creature or restores Hit Points to another creature, it chooses itself or one creature within 30 feet. That creature gains Temporary Hit Points equal to the dragon's PB + Intelligence modifier + Charisma modifier (18 Temporary Hit Points for this ancient dragon).

entries.name: Shared Brilliance
entries: The wyrm can use this feature as a Reaction. The Temporary Hit Points persist until depleted or replaced. When a creature the dragon can see within 60 feet takes damage or fails a Saving Throw, the dragon releases a radiant pulse and chooses Shielding Light or Guiding Light.

entries.name: Shielding Light
entries: Reduce the triggering damage by {@damage 3d8} + the dragon's Charisma modifier.

entries.name: Guiding Light
entries: The target rerolls the failed Saving Throw and must use the new result. If Shielding Light reduces the triggering damage to 0, or if the reroll from Guiding Light succeeds, the target gains 12 Temporary Hit Points. The dragon can use Shared Brilliance a number of times equal to its PB per Long Rest.

entries.name: Beacon of Renewal
entries: The wyrm can use this feature as an Action. This effect lasts for 1 minute. The dragon creates a 60-foot aura. A chosen creature that starts its turn in the aura while it has at least 1 Hit Point regains Hit Points equal to the dragon's PB + Charisma modifier. Whenever a chosen creature in the aura regains Hit Points from another source, the amount restored increases by the dragon's PB.

The first time on each of its turns that a chosen creature gains Temporary Hit Points, it can end Charmed, Frightened, or Poisoned on itself. If a chosen creature is at its Hit Point maximum when it would regain Hit Points from Beacon of Renewal, it gains that amount as Temporary Hit Points instead.

entries.name: Overflowing Life
entries: When a chosen creature in Beacon of Renewal regains Hit Points and that healing would raise it above its Hit Point maximum, the excess healing becomes Temporary Hit Points instead, to a maximum of 5 × the dragon's PB (35 for this ancient dragon). once per turn when a creature in the aura regains Hit Points from any source, the dragon can choose a second creature in the aura. The second creature regains Hit Points equal to half the healing the first creature actually received. Healing created by Overflowing Life can't trigger Overflowing Life again.

entries.name: Prismatic Purification
entries: When the dragon causes a creature to regain Hit Points with one of its spells or features, it can end Blinded, Charmed, Frightened, or Poisoned on that creature. A creature can benefit from Prismatic Purification only once per turn.

entries.name: Life Beyond the Limit
entries: The wyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action. This effect lasts for 1 minute. The wyrm creates a 300-foot Life Nexus. Chosen creatures in the Nexus regain 20 Hit Points at the start of each of their turns, increase all healing they receive by the wyrm's PB, can't have their Hit Point maximum reduced, can't be prevented from regaining Hit Points, and can't have their regeneration suppressed.

entries.name: Overflowing Vitality
entries: When a chosen creature at its Hit Point maximum would regain Hit Points, all of that healing becomes Temporary Hit Points instead. Temporary Hit Points granted by Life Beyond the Limit can stack with themselves, to a maximum of 5 × the wyrm's CR (130 for this Crystal Wyrm).

entries.name: Life Echo
entries: Once per turn when a chosen creature receives healing, the wyrm can choose up to PB other chosen creatures in the Nexus. Each selected creature regains Hit Points equal to half the amount of healing the first creature actually received. Healing from Life Echo can't trigger Life Echo again.

entries.name: Refuse Deterioration
entries: Chosen creatures in the Nexus are immune to reductions to their Hit Point maximum, magical aging, magical decay of the body, and effects that prevent them from regaining Hit Points.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the dragon more than size. Its voice, gaze, posture, and supernatural presence carry the instinctive certainty of an apex creature that has survived centuries. Those who stand before it can feel that history pressing against their courage. At the start of its turn, the dragon can activate this feature. This effect lasts for up to 1 minute. Each creature of the dragon's choice within 300 feet that can see or hear it must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.

On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the dragon for 1 minute. The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that dragon's Frightful Presence for 24 hours. This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition. a creature that fails its initial Saving Throw can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
This additional effect occurs only on the initial failed save.

spellcasting.name: Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics)
headerEntries: The wyrm's spellcasting ability is Intelligence. Its spell save DC is 24, and it has +16 to hit with spell attacks. The wyrm casts these spells psionically. It requires no Verbal or Somatic components and no Material components that have no listed cost and aren't consumed. Material components that have a listed cost or are consumed are still required normally.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The wyrm makes five attacks using any combination of its Bite, Claw, and Tail. The wyrm can replace only one of these attacks with the casting of a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 Action. The spell is resolved normally and expends a spell slot or use as normal. A spell cast through Draconic High Magic can also replace that one attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 18} to hit, reach 25 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 8d10 + 10} Piercing damage plus {@damage 8d8} Radiant damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 18} to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 8d6 + 10} Slashing damage.

action.name: Tail
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 18} to hit, reach 35 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 8d8 + 10} Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Wing
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 18} to hit, reach 25 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 8d6 + 10} Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Scintillating Breath {@recharge 4}
entries: The Temporary Hit Points persist until depleted or replaced. The wyrm exhales scintillating radiance in a 180-foot Cone. Each creature in that area must make a {@dc 26} Constitution Saving Throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 32d8} Radiant damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage. After resolving the Breath, the wyrm chooses up to PB creatures within 180 feet. Each chosen creature gains 40 Temporary Hit Points.

legendaryHeader: The wyrm can take 7 Legendary Actions, choosing from the options below. Only one Legendary Action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The wyrm regains spent Legendary Actions at the start of its turn.

entries: The wyrm makes a Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check.

legendary.name: Tail Attack
entries: The wyrm makes one Tail attack.

legendary.name: Cast Cantrip

legendary.name: Psychic Step
entries: The wyrm uses Psychic Step, but teleports no more than 90 feet and can't bring another creature with it.

legendary.name: Wing Attack (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: Each creature within 25 feet of the wyrm must make a {@dc 26} Dexterity Saving Throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 8d6 + 10} Bludgeoning damage and falls Prone. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and doesn't fall Prone. The wyrm can then fly up to half its Fly Speed.

entries: The wyrm chooses one creature it can see within 120 feet. The target must make a Strength Saving Throw against the wyrm's Psionic Save DC. On a failed save, the wyrm moves the target up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. This movement isn't teleportation.

legendary.name: Thought Before Motion (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The wyrm moves up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks, or it uses a special 60-foot version of Psychic Step that can't bring another creature with it.

legendary.name: Cast Psionic Spell (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The wyrm casts one psionic spell of 7th level or lower that normally has a casting time of 1 Action, expending a spell slot or use as normal.

legendary.name: High Magic (Costs 5 Actions)
entries: The wyrm casts one spell from Draconic High Magic whose use is still available.

trait.name: Law of Ending
entries: Topaz dragons perceive decay less as tragedy and more as a universal rule. Water evaporates, flesh weakens, stone erodes, and every living thing eventually reaches its conclusion. Even a wyrmling can accelerate tiny fragments of that process through instinctive psionic entropy.

entries.name: Drying Touch
entries: Using Drying Touch on an environmental liquid requires an Action. The environmental change is permanent, and the healing prevention lasts until the start of the dragon's next turn. The dragon can touch nonmagical water or another ordinary liquid and instantly destroy up to 1 cubic foot of it through supernatural desiccation. This can't directly desiccate liquid inside a living creature. once per turn when the dragon deals Necrotic damage to a creature, that creature can't regain Hit Points until the start of the dragon's next turn.

entries.name: Entropic Field
entries: The wyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action. This effect lasts for 1 minute. The dragon creates a 30-foot aura. A chosen hostile creature that starts its turn in the aura must make a Constitution Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC. On a failed save, until the start of its next turn the creature can't regain Hit Points, can't gain Temporary Hit Points, and its Speed is reduced by 10 feet. The dragon can also cause nonmagical unattended plants, food, wood, cloth, and other ordinary organic matter in the aura to dry, wilt, or become brittle at an accelerated rate. Entropic Field doesn't automatically deal damage to creatures.

entries.name: Accelerated Ending
entries: The Maximum Hit Point reduction lasts 1 hour. Once per turn when the dragon deals Necrotic damage to a creature in its Entropic Field, the target must make a Constitution Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC. On a failed save, the target's Hit Point maximum is reduced by half the Necrotic damage it took from the triggering damage, to a maximum reduction of 5 × the dragon's PB (25 for this adult dragon). Multiple reductions from Accelerated Ending don't stack; only the highest reduction applies.
This isn't a disease or curse. {@spell Greater Restoration|XPHB} or other magic that removes reductions to a creature's Hit Point maximum can end the reduction normally.

entries.name: Entropy Becomes Law
entries: The radius of Entropic Field increases from 30 feet to 60 feet. A chosen hostile creature that starts its turn in the aura and fails the Constitution Saving Throw can't regain Hit Points, can't gain Temporary Hit Points, has its Speed reduced by 20 feet, and can't benefit from regeneration until the start of its next turn. Healing that would restore Hit Points to that creature before the start of its next turn restores 0 Hit Points instead. The first time on each of its turns that such a creature takes Necrotic damage from the dragon, it loses all Temporary Hit Points before that damage is applied.

entries.name: Collapse Toward the End
entries: The wyrm can use this feature as a Reaction. When a creature the dragon can see within Entropic Field uses healing, regains Hit Points, or attempts to remove a reduction to its Hit Point maximum, the dragon can force it to make a Constitution Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC. On a failed save, the triggering effect is still expended or used normally but has no effect on that creature. The dragon can use Collapse Toward the End a number of times equal to its PB per Long Rest.

entries: The wyrm can use this feature as an Action. This effect lasts for 1 minute. The wyrm creates a 300-foot Entropic Dominion. Hostile creatures in the Dominion can't regain Hit Points, can't gain Temporary Hit Points, and can't benefit from regeneration. Healing effects that target them still expend their resources but restore 0 Hit Points.

The first time on each turn that a creature in the Dominion takes Necrotic damage from the wyrm, its Hit Point maximum is reduced by half the Necrotic damage it took, to a maximum reduction of 10 × the wyrm's PB on that turn (80 for this Topaz Wyrm). This Hit Point maximum reduction lasts until the creature finishes a Long Rest or it is removed by appropriate magic.

entries.name: Nothing Returns Unchanged
entries: If a creature in the Dominion is returned from the dead by a spell or effect, it returns normally, but for 1 hour its Hit Point maximum is halved, its Speed is halved, and it has Disadvantage on all Saving Throws.

entries.name: Final Collapse
entries: The wyrm can use this feature as a Reaction. When a creature in the Dominion with fewer than 25 percent of its Hit Point maximum would regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points, the wyrm can cause that effect to fail against the creature. The triggering resource is still expended. The wyrm can use Final Collapse a number of times equal to its PB per Long Rest.

legendary.name: Wing Attack (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: Each creature within 25 feet of the wyrm must make a {@dc 26} Dexterity Saving Throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 8d6 + 10} Bludgeoning damage and falls Prone. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and doesn't fall Prone. The wyrm can then fly up to half its Fly Speed.

legendary.name: Psionic Displacement (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The wyrm chooses one creature it can see within 120 feet. The target must make a Strength Saving Throw against the wyrm's Psionic Save DC. On a failed save, the wyrm moves the target up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. This movement isn't teleportation.

legendary.name: Thought Before Motion (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The wyrm moves up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks, or it uses a special 60-foot version of Psychic Step that can't bring another creature with it.

legendary.name: Breath Surge (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The wyrm rolls one additional d6 to recharge its Breath Weapon. If the Breath Weapon is already available, the wyrm can instead immediately use it.

legendary.name: Cast Psionic Spell (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The wyrm casts one psionic spell of 7th level or lower that normally has a casting time of 1 Action, expending a spell slot or use as normal.

legendary.name: High Magic (Costs 5 Actions)
entries: The wyrm casts one spell from Draconic High Magic whose use is still available.

monster.name: Emerald Wyrm

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (7/Day)
entries: If the wyrm fails a Saving Throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Draconic Magic
entries: {@b Wyrm Magic Resistance.} The wyrm has Advantage on Saving Throws against spells and other magical effects.
{@b Perfect Concentration.} The wyrm automatically succeeds on Constitution Saving Throws made to maintain Concentration as a result of taking damage.

{@b Wyrm Psychic Supremacy.} The wyrm's mastery of psychic power has exceeded the ordinary defensive categories used by lesser creatures. Resistance no longer represents meaningful protection, and even immunity can be forced into a state the dragon can overcome. Its signature energy behaves as an extension of psionic authority rather than an ordinary source of damage. The wyrm's Psychic damage ignores Psychic Resistance. When the wyrm deals Psychic damage to a creature with Psychic Immunity, that Immunity is treated as Psychic Resistance, and the wyrm then ignores that Resistance. As a result, the wyrm's Psychic damage affects creatures with Psychic Resistance or Psychic Immunity without reducing the damage.
{@b Arcane Reclamation.} At the end of a Short Rest, the wyrm can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 24. It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

{@b Draconic Spell List.} Draconic magic grows from instinct and experience. The wyrm knows the listed Emerald Dragon spells through 9th-level magic, as presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics) trait.

{@b Draconic At-Will Magic.} The wyrm can cast each spell listed under At Will in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics) trait without expending a spell slot and with no usage limit. A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The wyrm can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable. An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the wyrm's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack. Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell disguise self|XPHB}, {@spell silent image|XPHB}, {@spell detect thoughts|XPHB}, {@spell phantasmal force|XPHB}, {@spell major image|XPHB}, {@spell greater invisibility|XPHB}, {@spell mislead|XPHB}, {@spell mass suggestion|XPHB}, {@spell project image|XPHB}, {@spell dominate monster|XPHB}.

trait.name: Draconic Nature
entries: {@b Draconic Magical Instinct.} The dragon is proficient in Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}). It can make Arcana checks concerning spells, magical effects, Magic Items, curses, wards, magical creatures, and supernatural phenomena. This trait doesn't grant automatic or complete knowledge.
{@b Keen Senses.} The dragon has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight or smell.

{@b Psionic Mind.} Thought flows as naturally as breath. The dragon can communicate telepathically with a creature it can see within 120 feet. A contacted creature can understand the dragon if it knows at least one language, and it can reply telepathically while it remains within 120 feet of the dragon.
{@b Tunneler.} The dragon can burrow through solid rock at half its Burrow Speed and leaves a 5-foot-wide tunnel in its wake.

trait.name: Psychic Step
entries: Distance is no longer a route to a gem wyrm. Position is simply another state its mind can choose. Those close enough to enter that thought can cross space with it. The wyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action. The wyrm teleports up to 180 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. When it teleports, it can choose up to four willing creatures within 20 feet. Each chosen creature teleports with it and appears in an unoccupied space within 20 feet of the wyrm. This isn't a spell and requires no components. The wyrm can use Psychic Step without a usage limit, including while Grappled or Restrained. Objects worn or carried by the wyrm teleport with it normally.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: A gem wyrm can impose an entirely different physical pattern upon its body without diminishing the mind beneath. Its chosen shape is merely another arrangement of matter directed by the same ancient consciousness. No borrowed body can replace the psionic identity that defines the wyrm. The wyrm can use this feature as an Action. The transformation lasts until the wyrm ends it, uses this feature again, or dies.
The wyrm magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 27 or lower, or returns to its true form. The assumed form can be any Size the chosen creature normally possesses.

While transformed, the wyrm retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; personality and memories; alignment; Saving Throw proficiencies; Skill proficiencies; languages; Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics); Psionic Mind; Psychic Step; Draconic Magical Instinct; Legendary Resistance; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body.

It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics, including Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Armor Class, movement modes, natural weapons, physical senses, and other body-dependent traits and actions. It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features. The wyrm can continue using its own psionic spellcasting while transformed.
Equipment it is wearing or carrying can merge into the new form or remain usable, as the wyrm chooses when it transforms.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The wyrm can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell mislead|XPHB}, {@spell mass suggestion|XPHB}, {@spell project image|XPHB}, {@spell dominate monster|XPHB}, {@spell psychic scream|XGE}, {@spell time stop|XPHB}, {@spell wish|XPHB}. Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the wyrm from casting the same spell again using a spell slot. When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.

trait.name: World-Heart Reignition (1/Long Rest)
entries: The death of a wyrm is not always a single event. Its ancient body and psionic identity can violently reassert themselves when destruction should have become final. For a brief second phase of existence, the creature returns with its greatest powers burning again. When the wyrm would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, it doesn't die or fall Unconscious.

Instead, it regains Hit Points equal to half its Hit Point maximum; ends any conditions or ongoing effects on itself that it chooses; recharges its Breath Weapon; regains 3 expended uses of Legendary Resistance; regains one expended use of Draconic High Magic, including a 9th-level spell; and immediately regains its full allotment of Legendary Actions.

trait.name: The Hidden Thought
entries: Emerald dragons prefer to know more than they reveal. Illusion is not merely concealment to them; it is a way to control which version of reality another mind receives. Their earliest psionic instincts are already devoted to watching without being watched in return.

entries.name: Observer Behind the Image
entries: The dragon can Hide as a Bonus Action while Lightly Obscured, behind an illusion, within Dim Light, or possessing Half Cover or better. when it communicates telepathically, the recipient can't determine the direction or physical location from which the telepathic voice originates unless the dragon allows it.

entries.name: False Presence
entries: The wyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action. This effect lasts for 1 minute. The dragon creates an illusory duplicate of itself in an unoccupied space it can see within 60 feet. The duplicate has no Hit Points, can't pass through objects, and looks, sounds, and smells like the dragon. When the dragon uses a Bonus Action, it can move the duplicate up to 40 feet.

The dragon can use the duplicate as the apparent origin point of its telepathy, its Illusion spells, and spells that target a mind or perception but don't create a physical projectile. The first time on each turn that a creature attacks the duplicate, the attack automatically misses and the attacker must make an Intelligence Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC. On a failed save, that creature can't see the real dragon until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Distributed Presence
entries: The wyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action. This effect lasts for 1 minute. When the dragon uses False Presence, it can maintain a number of duplicates at once equal to its PB (6 for this adult dragon). Each duplicate occupies its own position and can serve as an origin for the dragon's telepathy, Illusion spells, and mind- or perception-targeting spells as described by False Presence. When the dragon uses a Bonus Action to move its duplicates, each duplicate can move up to 40 feet.

entries.name: Swap the Thought
entries: The wyrm can use this feature as a Reaction. When the dragon is targeted by an attack or fails a Saving Throw, it can swap positions with one of its duplicates within 120 feet. The chosen duplicate then disappears. For an attack, resolve the attack using the dragon's new position. For an Area of Effect, use the new position to determine whether the dragon remains in the area. This is psionic displacement, not the casting of a teleportation spell.

entries.name: No Single True Position
entries: The dragon can maintain a number of False Presence duplicates at once equal to PB + 3 (10 for this ancient dragon). While at least one duplicate exists, when a spell or magical effect that isn't an Area of Effect attempts to choose the dragon as a target, the creature creating the effect must make an Intelligence Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC. On a failed save, the dragon chooses one of its duplicates to become the target instead. The duplicate disappears after the effect is resolved.
If the effect can't legally target the chosen duplicate, the effect fails against the dragon, but any Action, spell slot, charge, or other limited use spent on that effect is still expended.

entries.name: Thought Without Origin
entries: A creature can't determine the dragon's precise location solely through telepathy, divination that detects thoughts, or magical detection of consciousness unless the dragon allows it. Such effects can reveal that a mind or consciousness is present in the relevant area but don't reveal the dragon's exact location by themselves.

entries.name: Consensus Is Optional
entries: The wyrm can maintain up to 20 False Presence duplicates at once. Each duplicate can speak, carry the wyrm's telepathy, serve as a spell origin as allowed by the previous stages of this feature, and move independently when the wyrm directs its duplicates.

entries.name: Distributed Self
entries: Once per turn, the wyrm can use Distributed Self. The wyrm swaps positions with one duplicate within 300 feet. The duplicate isn't destroyed by this swap.

entries.name: You Chose the Wrong Dragon
entries: When a single-target attack, spell, or effect targets the wyrm while at least one duplicate exists, the user of that effect must make a {@dc 25} Intelligence Saving Throw. On a failed save, the wyrm chooses a duplicate to receive the effect instead. If the effect can't legally affect the duplicate, the effect fails and its resource is still expended.

entries.name: Thought Everywhere
entries: The wyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action. This effect lasts for 1 minute. The wyrm creates a 300-foot psychic field. Hostile creatures in the field can't determine the wyrm's precise location through telepathy or divination alone and have Disadvantage on checks made to distinguish its illusions. The wyrm can communicate telepathically with every creature in the field simultaneously and can cast an Enchantment spell, Illusion spell, or spell that deals Psychic damage from the position of any duplicate in the field.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the dragon more than size. Its voice, gaze, posture, and supernatural presence carry the instinctive certainty of an apex creature that has survived centuries. Those who stand before it can feel that history pressing against their courage. At the start of its turn, the dragon can activate this feature. This effect lasts for up to 1 minute. Each creature of the dragon's choice within 300 feet that can see or hear it must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.

On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the dragon for 1 minute. The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that dragon's Frightful Presence for 24 hours. This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition. a creature that fails its initial Saving Throw can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
This additional effect occurs only on the initial failed save.

spellcasting.name: Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics)
headerEntries: The wyrm's spellcasting ability is Intelligence. Its spell save DC is 25, and it has +17 to hit with spell attacks. The wyrm casts these spells psionically. It requires no Verbal or Somatic components and no Material components that have no listed cost and aren't consumed. Material components that have a listed cost or are consumed are still required normally.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The wyrm makes five attacks using any combination of its Bite, Claw, and Tail. The wyrm can replace only one of these attacks with the casting of a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 Action. The spell is resolved normally and expends a spell slot or use as normal. A spell cast through Draconic High Magic can also replace that one attack.

entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 18} to hit, reach 25 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 8d10 + 10} Piercing damage plus {@damage 8d8} Psychic damage.

entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 18} to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 8d6 + 10} Slashing damage.

action.name: Tail
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 18} to hit, reach 35 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 8d8 + 10} Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Wing
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 18} to hit, reach 25 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 8d6 + 10} Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Disorienting Breath {@recharge 4}
entries: This effect lasts until the end of the target's next turn. The wyrm exhales disorienting psychic force in a 180-foot Cone. Each creature in that area must make a {@dc 27} Intelligence Saving Throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 32d8} Psychic damage, can't take Reactions or Bonus Actions, can't distinguish the wyrm from its duplicates, and whenever it makes an Attack Roll, Ability Check, or Saving Throw before the end of its next turn, it rolls ({@dice 1d12}) and subtracts the result. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and suffers no additional effect.

trait.name: Resonance of Strategy
entries: Sapphire dragons hear a battlefield differently from other creatures. Every footstep, impact, vibration, and hollow space adds another piece to an invisible tactical map. Before they understand formal warfare, they already understand where things are moving and where stone is empty.

entries.name: Echo Map
entries: While touching stone, earth, metal, or another continuous solid surface, the dragon gains Tremorsense 30 feet. It can determine the approximate Size, direction, movement, and number of creatures moving on the same connected surface. It can detect movement through up to 10 feet of nonmagical stone but doesn't gain sight through that stone.

entries.name: Expanded Echo Map
entries: The Tremorsense granted by Echo Map increases from 30 feet to 60 feet.

entries.name: Tactical Resonance
entries: The wyrm can activate this feature as a Bonus Action; the protective movement uses a Reaction. This effect lasts for 1 minute. The dragon creates a 60-foot aura. It knows the location of every creature in the aura that touches a connected floor, wall, or ceiling, or that creates sound or vibration, provided the creature isn't completely isolated from vibration. Chosen allies in the aura can't be Surprised, gain a bonus to Initiative equal to the dragon's PB, and Opportunity Attacks against them have Disadvantage.

When an ally in the aura is targeted by an attack, the dragon can use its Reaction to move that ally up to 10 feet by psionic vibration before the attack is resolved. If the movement carries the ally beyond the attack's legal reach or range, the attack misses. The Tremorsense granted by Echo Map increases to 90 feet.

entries.name: Battlefield Harmonics
entries: The radius of Tactical Resonance increases from 60 feet to 90 feet. A chosen ally that starts its turn in the aura can move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks, has Advantage on Saving Throws against being pushed, pulled, or knocked Prone, and can receive telepathic tactical instructions from the dragon without an Action.

The first time in each round that a hostile creature in the aura moves at least 10 feet, the dragon can use its Reaction to force that creature to make a Constitution Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC. On a failed save, the creature's movement immediately ends and its Speed becomes 0 until the end of the current turn. The Tremorsense granted by Echo Map increases to 150 feet.

entries.name: Command the Initiative
entries: This effect lasts until combat ends. After Initiative is rolled but before the first turn begins, the dragon chooses up to PB willing creatures within Tactical Resonance. The dragon can freely reassign the rolled Initiative results among those chosen creatures. This doesn't change the numerical Initiative results; it changes which chosen creature uses each result.

entries.name: Resonant Command
entries: The wyrm can use this feature as a Reaction. When a chosen ally in Tactical Resonance ends its turn, the dragon can choose a different chosen ally in the aura. That creature can immediately move up to half its Speed, make one weapon attack, or take the Dodge action. The dragon can use Resonant Command a number of times equal to its PB per Long Rest.

entries.name: Ancient Battlefield Harmonics
entries: The radius of Tactical Resonance increases from 90 feet to 150 feet.

entries.name: Battle Is Already Solved
entries: This effect lasts until combat ends. After Initiative is rolled but before the first turn begins, the wyrm can freely reassign the rolled Initiative results among all chosen allies within Tactical Resonance. There is no PB limit on the number of chosen allies for this feature.

entries.name: Perfect Command Network
entries: This effect lasts while Tactical Resonance is active. The radius of Tactical Resonance increases to 300 feet. Chosen allies in the aura can't be Surprised, gain a bonus to Initiative equal to the wyrm's PB, impose Disadvantage on Opportunity Attacks made against them, have Advantage on Saving Throws against forced movement, and can communicate telepathically with the wyrm and with one another.

entries.name: Command Chain
entries: The wyrm can use this feature as a Reaction. When a chosen ally ends its turn, the wyrm chooses another chosen ally. That creature can immediately move up to half its Speed, make one weapon attack, cast one cantrip, take the Dodge action, or take the Disengage action. Command Chain has no usage limit, but each creature can benefit from it only once per round.

entries.name: Predictive Countermeasure
entries: The wyrm can use this feature as a Reaction. When a hostile creature in Tactical Resonance moves, casts a spell, makes an attack, or teleports, the wyrm chooses one chosen ally. That ally can immediately move up to 20 feet before the triggering action is resolved. If this movement leaves the triggering action without a legal target or places the ally outside its legal reach or range, that action can't continue against that ally.

entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 18} to hit, reach 25 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 8d6 + 10} Bludgeoning damage.

entries: This effect lasts until the end of the target's next turn. The wyrm exhales high-frequency resonant force in a 180-foot Cone. Each creature in that area must make a {@dc 27} Constitution Saving Throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 32d10} Thunder damage, is Incapacitated until the end of its next turn, has Speed 0, can't take Reactions or Bonus Actions, immediately loses Concentration, and can't teleport until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and suffers no additional effect.

legendary.name: Psionic Displacement (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The wyrm chooses one creature it can see within 120 feet. The target must make a Strength Saving Throw against the wyrm's Psionic Save DC. On a failed save, the wyrm moves the target up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. This movement isn't teleportation.
